EDCS-02900135.inscription_type: inscriptiones christianae, tituli operum, tituli sepulcrales
EDCS-02900135.translation: Victoria, who lived about 63 years, rested in the peace of Christ. Felix made this for his deserving and noble wife, deposited on the day before the Ides of May, in the consulship of Flavius Constantius, vir clarissimus. Here lies in holy remembrance, Fantinus, priest and abbot of the monastery, who lived 40 years, 10 months, and 5 days, and died on the 5th day before the Ides of June, in the 8th indiction, in the year 32 after the consulship of Basilius, and in the 7th year of Justin, in the same indiction.
EDCS-02900135.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Victoria and Fantinus, dating to the consulship of Flavius Constantius and a later period related to Basilius and Justin.

EDCS-03000135.translation: Valeria Sabina, daughter of Caius, stepdaughter of Caius Flaccus, mother of Flaccus.
EDCS-03000135.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription for Valeria Sabina, daughter of Caius, and related to Caius Flaccus.

EDCS-03000137.text_edition: \n Caio Flaccinio Cai filio Cai nepoti Flacco tribuno militum IIviro quinquennali patrono municipi\n
EDCS-03000137.translation: To Caius Flaccinius Flaccus, son of Caius, grandson of Caius, tribune of soldiers, quinquennial duumvir, patron of the municipality.
EDCS-03000137.summary: This is an honorary inscription for Caius Flaccinius Flaccus, who held several significant civic and military offices.

EDCS-03300084.translation: To the departed gods. Caius Canius Fortunatus lived 30 years. Placed [this?].
EDCS-03300084.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Caius Canius Fortunatus, who lived 30 years.

EDCS-03300085.translation: Publius Canuleius Bassus, son of Publius.
EDCS-03300085.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription for Publius Canuleius Bassus.

EDCS-03300086.translation: To the departed gods. Marcus Cocceius Restitutus, freedman of Augustus, is buried here. He lived 65 years. Flavius Speratus and Cocceius Restitutus placed this for their deserving father, and Cocceia Primigenia for her deserving tent-mate.
EDCS-03300086.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Marcus Cocceius Restitutus, placed by his sons Flavius Speratus and Cocceius Restitutus, and his tent-mate Cocceia Primigenia.

EDCS-03300087.translation: To the departed gods. Seia Pistica lived 70 years. Campuleia Caesania placed this for her mother.
EDCS-03300087.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Seia Pistica, placed by her daughter Campuleia Caesania.

EDCS-03300088.translation: To the departed gods. For Prisca, for her dearest son Magnesius, who deserved well. Placed [this].
EDCS-03300088.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Magnesius, placed by his mother Prisca.

EDCS-03300089.translation: For Lucifer(?), for his deserving daughter Calliste, who lived 4 years.
EDCS-03300089.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription for Calliste, who died at the age of 4.

EDCS-03300090.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription for Lucius Dasimius.

EDCS-03300092.summary: Fragment of an inscription providing a woman's name and filiation, possibly funerary.

EDCS-03300094.translation: To Triarius Pacatianus, his son, Sabbatius and Statia, parents, made this for him well-deserving, who lived 2 years and 5 months.
EDCS-03300094.summary: Funerary epitaph for a young boy named Triarius Pacatianus, set up by his parents. Dated by the length of his life to early childhood, likely 2nd-3rd century CE.

EDCS-03300095.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Pontilius Urbanus and Fortunata and [---] set this up for their son Pontilius Marcus.
EDCS-03300095.summary: Funerary epitaph for Pontilius Marcus, set up by his parents Pontilius Urbanus and Fortunata.

EDCS-03300096.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. For Antonia Ianuaria, his dearest wife, with whom he lived [3] years, Quintus Vinius Redemptus [set this up].
EDCS-03300096.summary: Funerary epitaph for Antonia Ianuaria, dedicated by her husband Quintus Vinius Redemptus, mentioning their years of marriage.

EDCS-03700104.translation: Pomptina Rufus, aged 53, made this while alive. Rufulus died aged 8 years, [his] brother [---]. To surpass [me?] is better if you can. With the greatest effort I sought and [---] this place and monument [---].
EDCS-03700104.summary: A funerary epitaph with a personal message, possibly from a father to his sons, recording ages of death and the cost of the monument, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-03700105.translation: To the Greek grammaticus. Julia, his wife.
EDCS-03700105.summary: A funerary or honorific inscription dedicated to a Greek teacher by his wife, Julia.

EDCS-04900049.translation: For Aurelia Saephara, the most distinguished lady.
EDCS-04900049.summary: An honorific dedication to Aurelia Saephara, a woman of high status, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05200089.text_edition: \n Vulcaci<o=Q> Rufino et Flavio Eusebio conssulibus Kalendis Augustis cum cibes sic frequentes coloniae Paestanorum in uno adfuissent consilioque habito berba sic fecerunt cum tot tantaque beneficia sblendentia sic de domo Aquilini Nestori probi adulescentis descendant quibus colonia nostra exornata unicuique nobis cibibus sic in oculis adque sic animis sint praecipuae cum unusquisque civium se conberterit sic opera ab his extructa oculis eorum occurrant sic faciem cibitatis sic honestam reddant utinam qui tantus populus esset status ut tantis muneribus domus eorum aliis quoque gloriosis muneribus remunerandus esset fateri beneficia eius munera populi intebimque sic contentos esse hoc munere flaminis gratulit quod publica voce et offerendum etiam cibes sic cupiverant cum Aquilius Nestorius contemplatione mutui honoris nos municipes sua dignatione unice diligat sitque similem nobis adfectionem etiam Aquilius Aper filius efus sic praebiturus placere cibibus sic patronatus cibitatis sic eidem offerri ut fulti patrocinio eorum populus noster plus honoris consecutus quam optulisset sic videatur quod fieri placere de ea re ita censuerunt feliciter \n
EDCS-05200089.translation: In the consulship of Vulcatius Rufus and Flavius Eusebius, on the Kalends of August, when the citizens of the Paestani colony had gathered in such numbers and with such unanimity, and after deliberation, spoke as follows: 'Just as the shining benefits from the house of Aquilius Nestor, a worthy young man, descend upon us, adorning our colony, so that they are especially prominent before the eyes and in the minds of each one of us, and as each citizen turns his attention to the buildings constructed by them, which render the appearance of the city honorable, may there be such a great populace as to reward their house with other glorious gifts in return. We must acknowledge his gifts and the people's contentment with this gift from the flamen, which they had eagerly wished to offer through public acclamation. Since Aquilius Nestor, in consideration of mutual honor, uniquely loves us, the townspeople, with his favor, and since his son, Aquilius Aper, is also prepared to show similar affection towards us, it is resolved that the patronage of the city be offered to him, so that our people, supported by their patronage, may appear to have obtained more honor than they have offered. It is therefore decreed as follows: May it be fortunate!'
EDCS-05200089.summary: A decree by the citizens of Paestum thanking and honoring Aquilius Nestor and his son for their benefactions to the colony, likely from the late Roman Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-05200090.text_edition: \n Caius Sextilius Luci filius Publius Claudius Cai filius IIviri\n
EDCS-05200090.translation: Gaius Sextilius son of Lucius and Publius Claudius son of Gaius, duo-viri.
EDCS-05200090.summary: An inscription recording the names and offices of two duoviri (chief magistrates) of a Roman colony, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05200094.text_edition: \n ------ ho]c pretium vitae Restuto potu praesidium GEN\n
EDCS-05200094.translation: Here the price of life, Restutus, having drunk, protection, divine.
EDCS-05200094.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription, possibly indicating a payment related to life and protection.

EDCS-06600001.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Castricio Marciano nutritori bene merenti Spedius Atimetus fecit\n
EDCS-06600001.translation: To the departed spirits, for Castricius Marcianus, a well-deserving foster father, Spedius Atimetus made this.
EDCS-06600001.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Spedius Atimetus to his foster father, Castricius Marcianus.

EDCS-06600003.translation: To Cinnamus, my most excellent husband.
EDCS-06600003.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary epitaph for a husband named Cinnamus.

EDCS-06600005.translation: Into this sarcophagus I have placed it, into which, when my body shall have been received, it shall be permitted to no one ever to approach, nor to disturb my bones, not a son, nor grandsons, nor any of the relations by marriage. But if anyone dares to break or to open it, he shall then incur a penalty to the public treasury, one thousand folles. Truly Nevia Prisca, if she shall have remained until the day of her death, she shall be received there next to her husband.
EDCS-06600005.summary: This is a funerary inscription from Nevia Prisca, establishing strict rules for her sarcophagus and promising her burial next to her husband.

EDCS-06600007.text_edition: \n Genio Fulloniani Quintianus actor ex voto posuit dedicatum Impperatoribus duobus Auggustis Severo III et Antonino III consulibus Idibus Martiis\n
EDCS-06600007.translation: Quintianus, the manager, placed this dedicated offering by vow to the Genius of the Fulloniani, during the consulship of the two emperors Augustus Severus III and Antoninus III, on the Ides of March.
EDCS-06600007.summary: This is a dedication by Quintianus to the Genius of the Fulloniani, dated to the consulship of Severus and Antoninus.

EDCS-06600008.translation: To the departed spirits, for Numonia, daughter of Quintus, Marciana, his most beloved wife, Quintus Manilius, son of Marcus, Iustus made this.
EDCS-06600008.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Numonia Marciana, dedicated by her husband Iustus.

EDCS-06600009.translation: Otacilius [---] to his husband [---], well-deserving, made this.
EDCS-06600009.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary epitaph for a husband, possibly made by Otacilius.

EDCS-06600010.translation: Quintus Poppaedius Dorotheus, freedman of Quintus. Poppaedia Dionysia, freedwoman of Quintus.
EDCS-06600010.summary: This inscription lists two freedpersons, Quintus Poppaedius Dorotheus and Poppaedia Dionysia, both freed by a Quintus.

EDCS-06600012.translation: To [---]nio, son of Lucius, Rufus, an official of the second rank and quinquennial censor. Lucius Haedinius [made this].
EDCS-06600012.summary: This is a fragmentary dedication to a man named Rufus, who held municipal offices.

EDCS-06600013.translation: Firmus and [---]a made this for their most beloved son, Bruttio Firmanus.
EDCS-06600013.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by parents, Firmus and [---]a, for their beloved son, Bruttio Firmanus.

EDCS-06600014.translation: To Allidius, son of Gaius, of the Aemilia tribe.
EDCS-06600014.summary: This inscription appears to be the beginning of a funerary dedication for Allidius, son of Gaius, belonging to the Aemilia tribe.

EDCS-06600015.translation: To Callippus, the actor, his fellow members of the association made this, a well-deserving man.
EDCS-06600015.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by fellow association members for Callippus, an actor, who is described as deserving.

EDCS-06600017.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Baia Thallusa had this made for her husband, Numerius Aeserius Rufus, who was well-deserving.
EDCS-06600017.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by a wife, Baia Thallusa, for her husband, Numerius Aeserius Rufus.

EDCS-06600019.text_edition: \n Insteio Celerino sodales Minervenses aere collato fecerunt\n
EDCS-06600019.translation: The fellow members of Minerva's association made this, collected from contributions.
EDCS-06600019.summary: This inscription records a funerary monument erected by the members of a Minerva association through collective contributions.

EDCS-06600020.translation: To Marcus Insteius Felicissimus. Tullia Septima, his wife, had this made for her well-deserving husband, with whom she lived for 30 years.
EDCS-06600020.summary: This is a funerary dedication by a wife, Tullia Septima, for her deceased husband, Marcus Insteius Felicissimus, noting their 30 years of marriage.

EDCS-06600021.translation: Marcus Insteius Callitychus and Praepusa made this for their dearest son, Marcus Insteius Pulcher, who lived for 3 years, 3 months, and 5 days.
EDCS-06600021.summary: This is a funerary dedication by parents for their young son, Marcus Insteius Pulcher, specifying his short lifespan.

EDCS-06600022.translation: To Otacilia Arbuscula, freedwoman of Lucius, the nurse.
EDCS-06600022.summary: This inscription is a dedication, likely funerary, to Otacilia Arbuscula, a freedwoman and nurse.

EDCS-06600024.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Verus, his father, for his dearest son Calitanus, who lived for 16 years.
EDCS-06600024.summary: This is a funerary dedication by a father, Verus, for his son Calitanus, who died at the age of 16.

EDCS-06600026.text_edition: \n Marcus Alutius filius Pomptina us annorum XIX mater infelix fecit filium \n
EDCS-06600026.translation: Marcus Alutius, aged 19, his unhappy mother made this for her son.
EDCS-06600026.summary: This funerary inscription records a monument made by an unhappy mother for her son, Marcus Alutius, who died at 19.

EDCS-06600028.translation: To Faunus. Marcus Iulius Staphylus and Lucius Rufius Mysticus gave this offering.
EDCS-06600028.summary: This inscription records a dedication to the god Faunus by two individuals, Marcus Iulius Staphylus and Lucius Rufius Mysticus.

EDCS-06600029.text_edition: \n Caio Utiano Cai filio Pomptina Rufo Latiniano IIIIviro iure dicundo iterum Insteia Marci filia Polla sacerdos Iuliae Augustae Volceis et Atinae optimo et indulgentissimo viro qui eam pupillam annorum VII in domum receptam per annos LV cum summo honore uxorem habuit hunc decuriones Volceiani inpensa publica funerandum et statua equestri STRI honorandum censuerunt Latiniae Marci filiae Posillae sorori Latiniani\n
EDCS-06600029.translation: To Gaius Utianus Rufus Latinianus, son of Caius, twice appointed a magistrate with judicial authority, Insteia Polla, daughter of Marcus, priestess of Julia Augusta, offered this to her husband, Latinianus, for being the best and most indulgent man, who received her as an orphaned girl of seven years into his household and had her as his wife with the highest honor for fifty-five years. The decurions of Volceii decreed that he should be buried at public expense and honored with an equestrian statue; [this was done] for Latinia Posilla, daughter of Marcus, sister of Latinianus.
EDCS-06600029.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Gaius Utianus Rufus Latinianus, honoring his public service and his marriage, with a decree for his burial and statue, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-06600031.translation: To the departed spirits. Albius Antonius made this for Allidius Valerius Acentus, who served him well, who lived for about 55 years.
EDCS-06600031.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Albius Antonius for Allidius Valerius Acentus, who lived approximately 55 years and had served his benefactor well.

EDCS-06600032.translation: For Publius Apronius, freedman of a woman. [---] lives for Apronia Iconia, freedwoman of Lucius, from the will of Publius Valerius Lepidus, freedman of Publius, and [---] for seven thousand sesterces.
EDCS-06600032.summary: This inscription is a bequest from the will of Publius Valerius Lepidus, establishing funds for the deceased Apronia Iconia and possibly another individual.

EDCS-06600034.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Marco Insteio Silvano fecit Marcus Insteius Silvester fratri pientissimo vixsit! menses XV\n
EDCS-06600034.translation: To the departed spirits. Marcus Insteius Silvester made this for his most devoted brother, Marcus Insteius Silvanus, who lived 15 months.
EDCS-06600034.summary: This is a tombstone erected by Marcus Insteius Silvester for his infant brother, Marcus Insteius Silvanus, who died at 15 months old.

EDCS-06600037.text_edition: \n Imperatori Caesari Marco Aurelio Severo Alexandro Pio Felici Augusto divi Severi Pii nepoti divi Antonini Magni Pii filio pontifici maximo decreto decurionum\n
EDCS-06600037.translation: To Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Severus Alexander Pius Felix Augustus, grandson of the deified Severus Antoninus Pius, son of the deified Antoninus Magnus Pius, by decree of the decurions, Pontifex Maximus.
EDCS-06600037.summary: This inscription is an honorific dedication to Emperor Marcus Aurelius Severus Alexander, likely erected by the local council (decurions).

EDCS-06600038.text_edition: \n Iuli Amatoris militis cohortis tertiae praetoriae Iunius Felix miles cohortis decimae urbanae optimo commilitoni\n
EDCS-06600038.translation: To Julius Amator, a soldier of the third praetorian cohort. Iunius Felix, a soldier of the tenth urban cohort, [dedicated this] to his excellent fellow soldier.
EDCS-06600038.summary: This is an epitaph honoring Julius Amator, a soldier in the praetorian guard, dedicated by his colleague Iunius Felix from the urban cohort.

EDCS-06600040.translation: To the departed spirits. To Teltonus, his freedman, for his well-deserving patron, Teltonus.
EDCS-06600040.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the deceased patron Teltonus by his freedman, also named Teltonus.

EDCS-06600042.translation: To Marcus Tihonius Helios, his most devoted son. Marcus Tihonius Helius, his father, made this for him, his well-deserving son.
EDCS-06600042.summary: This is a funerary dedication by a father, Marcus Tihonius Helius, for his devoted son, Marcus Tihonius Helios.

EDCS-06600043.translation: To the departed spirits. For Titus Helvius Helvianus, his dearest son. Titus Helvius Tertullus [---]
EDCS-06600043.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Titus Helvius Tertullus for his beloved son, Titus Helvius Helvianus.

EDCS-06600044.translation: To the spirits of the departed. To Numerius Pontilius Campanus, his most excellent father. Numerius Pontilius [dedicated this].
EDCS-06600044.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Numerius Pontilius for his father, Numerius Pontilius Campanus.

EDCS-06600047.translation: To the spirits of the departed. To Staia Grumentina. Gaius Apidius Faustus, her husband, made this for her, deserving well.
EDCS-06600047.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Gaius Apidius Faustus for his wife, Staia Grumentina.

EDCS-06600048.translation: To Marcus Vibius, son of Marcus. Marcus Vibius, [his] father, and [---].
EDCS-06600048.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary epitaph, likely set up by a father for his son, Marcus Vibius.

EDCS-06600049.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Latania Germanilla, daughter of Publius, who lived 40 years. The Latiinii Lucanus and Lucanianus, their most loving and most dutiful sisters, made this for her.
EDCS-06600049.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Latania Germanilla, who died at 40, dedicated by her sisters.

EDCS-06600050.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Antonia Onesima. Spurius Baebius Fortunatus, her husband, deserving well, made this for her, with whom he lived 27 years.
EDCS-06600050.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Antonia Onesima, dedicated by her husband Spurius Baebius Fortunatus, with whom she lived 27 years.

EDCS-06600051.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Allidius Sopo, Allidius Epulianus, Allidia Calibe, his children. To their sweet father. Farewell. Allidia Cladisce [dedicated this] to her husband Soponianus, deserving well, with whom she lived 13 years, 6 months, and 5 days.
EDCS-06600051.summary: This funerary epitaph, likely dedicated to Soponianus by his wife Allidia Cladisce, is unusual in that it also names his children and mentions the children of the dedicant separately.

EDCS-06600052.translation: To the spirits of the departed. To [---]clia Prima, his wife. Amandus, with his children, made this for her, deserving well.
EDCS-06600052.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for A[---]clia Prima, dedicated by her husband Amandus and their children.

EDCS-06600056.summary: This is a name inscription, possibly a tombstone or property marker, identifying Gnaeus Balbius, son of Marcus.

EDCS-06600057.translation: Manius Scuracius Marsus, freedman of a woman. May you rest well.
EDCS-06600057.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Manius Scuracius Marsus, a freedman, with a wish for his repose.

EDCS-06600058.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Sura, his comrade in arms, deserving well. Fusca made this for her, with whom she lived 62 years.
EDCS-06600058.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Fusca for her comrade in arms, Sura, with whom she lived for 62 years.

EDCS-06600063.text_edition: \n Grati pater et filius balineum sua pecunia fecerunt decreto decurionum pater epulo dato dedicavit\n
EDCS-06600063.translation: The father and son Gratus built the bathhouse with their own money and dedicated it after the council decreed a banquet to be held.
EDCS-06600063.summary: This inscription records the private construction of a bathhouse by a father and son, approved by the local council.

EDCS-06600064.text_edition: \n Marcus Vehilius Luci filius curator rei publicae Cosilinatium porticum et murum a solo inpensa et constantia sua restituit\n
EDCS-06600064.translation: Marcus Vehilius, son of Lucius, the public official of Cosilinum, restored the portico and wall from the ground up through his own expense and perseverance.
EDCS-06600064.summary: This inscription records the restoration of public works by an official named Marcus Vehilius.

EDCS-06600065.translation: Maria, daughter of Caius, of the Annia tribe.
EDCS-06600065.summary: This is a simple funerary or dedicatory inscription identifying a woman named Maria and her tribal affiliation.

EDCS-06600068.translation: A monument erected for Valeria, deserving.
EDCS-06600068.summary: This inscription records the erection of a monument for a woman named Valeria.

EDCS-06600072.translation: To the Emperor Caesar, son of the deified Magnus, grandson of the deified Severus, Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus, by decree of the council.
EDCS-06600072.summary: This is a formal dedication to Emperor Marcus Aurelius Antoninus, likely on a public building, authorized by the local council.

EDCS-06600073.translation: Antesphorus, alive, made [this] for himself and for Pomponius Pedon, son of [---], lived 17 years, and for [---]ula, daughter of [---]ule, lived 20 years, and for their mother [---].
EDCS-06600073.summary: This funerary inscription records a man named Antesphorus dedicating a tomb for himself and his family members, including his deceased wife and daughter.

EDCS-06600075.text_edition: \n Tito Helvio Quarto filio Tito Helvio Hespero privigno Helviae Secundae coniugi Secundio Helviae Proculae vilicus sibi et suis fecit quod facere filius patri debuit idcirco filio fecit pater\n
EDCS-06600075.translation: For Titus Helvius Quartus, son; for Titus Helvius Hespero, stepson; for Helvia Secunda, wife; the vilicus [manager] Secundio made [this] for himself and his family, because the son ought to have done it for the father, therefore the father made it for the son.
EDCS-06600075.summary: This inscription is a funerary monument set up by a manager for his wife, her son by a previous marriage, and his own son, explaining the circumstances of its erection.

EDCS-06600076.translation: To the spirits of the departed; for Marcellinus, son; the parents made [this].
EDCS-06600076.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by parents for their deceased son, Marcellinus.

EDCS-06600077.summary: This is a dedication to a nurse named Cerialis.

EDCS-06600078.translation: To mother Secundila, most dutiful, well-deserving, [---]s and Secundus and [---]essa made [this].
EDCS-06600078.summary: This funerary inscription records a monument erected by Secundus and others for their mother Secundila.

EDCS-06600085.translation: Gaius, son of Gaius Samius, lived 11 years.
EDCS-06600085.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the age of a boy named Gaius Samius.

EDCS-06600088.translation: Tarsius the priest made this; whoever reads this, pray for him.
EDCS-06600088.summary: This inscription is a funerary request for prayers, likely from a priest named Tarsius.

EDCS-06600090.text_edition: \n Caius Luxsilius sic Cai filius Pomptina Macer arma haec quae cernis princeps ludendo fui id ita fuisse campus urbis testis est vixit annis XVIIII Herennia Luci filia Tertia talarum vitilem utut cordi forem vixit annis II\n
EDCS-06600090.translation: I, Gaius Luxsilius Macer, son of Gaius, of the Pomptina tribe, was the first to use these arms you see, and the Campus Martius of the city is witness that it was so. I lived 19 years. Herennia Tertia, daughter of Lucius, that I might be dear to you in my games, lived 2 years.
EDCS-06600090.summary: This is a tombstone for Gaius Luxsilius Macer and Herennia Tertia, detailing their names, tribal affiliations, ages at death, and the former's claim to fame in games.

EDCS-06600098.translation: To Oppius, aedile, twice as duovir, and to his father Volcius Tullius, aedile, and to his freedwoman mother Dionysia.
EDCS-06600098.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Oppius, who held the positions of aedile and duovir, and to his parents.

EDCS-06600099.translation: For the memory of Babbianus. Lucius Fulvius Pa[---]alus made this for himself and his family.
EDCS-06600099.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Babbianus, with Lucius Fulvius Pa[---]alus as the dedicator.

EDCS-06600100.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Felicissimus Bruttio Asiaticus placed this.
EDCS-06600100.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Bruttio Asiaticus by Felicissimus.

EDCS-06600101.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Felicio, his son, made this for his well-deserving mother Glaphyra.
EDCS-06600101.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Glaphyra by her son Felicio.

EDCS-06600102.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Gaius Oppius Romanus and Caesellia Luperca, most unhappy parents, for their son Ionio and for themselves.
EDCS-06600102.summary: This funerary inscription records the placement of a monument by parents, Gaius Oppius Romanus and Caesellia Luperca, for their son Ionio and for themselves.

EDCS-06600104.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Spurius Teius Ligdamus, a wretched father, made this for his son Spurius Teio Arelonius, who well deserved it and lived 24 years.
EDCS-06600104.summary: This funerary inscription records a monument dedicated by a father to his son, noting the son's age and the father's lament.

EDCS-06600105.summary: A fragment of an inscription, likely a funerary dedication to a wife, with an unknown name and date.

EDCS-07000341.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum Ledae Silvester coniugi bene merenti fecit cum qua vixit annos LXV\n
EDCS-07000341.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Silvester made this for his well-deserving wife Leda, with whom he lived for 65 years.
EDCS-07000341.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Silvester to his wife Leda, noting their years of marriage.

EDCS-07000342.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Quintianae filiae carissimae bene merenti quae vixit annos XXXVI fecit pia mater Quinta\n
EDCS-07000342.translation: To the divine shades. To Quintiana, dearest daughter, well-deserving. She lived 36 years. Her devoted mother Quinta made this.
EDCS-07000342.summary: A funerary epitaph dedicated by a mother to her deceased daughter, dated by its style to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-07000352.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Ulpiae Heraiidi coniugi carissimae Marcus Ma Das \n
EDCS-07000352.translation: To the divine shades. To Ulpia Heraclis, dearest wife. Marcus Ma[---] made this.
EDCS-07000352.summary: A funerary epitaph dedicated by a husband to his deceased wife, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-07400239.text_edition: \n Bonae memoriae sacrum Fidelix sic Criscentia sic quae bissit sic annis sic plus minus LXX mensis V dies VIII cui bene fecerunt fili recessit in pace\n
EDCS-07400239.translation: Sacred to good memory. Criscentia, faithful, who lived about 70 years, 5 months, and 8 days, for whom her sons did well, departed in peace.
EDCS-07400239.summary: A funerary epitaph to Criscentia, likely of Christian faith, recording her lifespan and burial by her sons.

EDCS-07400241.text_edition: \n Bonae memoriae s(acrum) Ianuarius fidelis in pace vixit annis plus minus L cui bene fecit uxsor sic sua recessit III Kalendas Septembres\n
EDCS-07400241.translation: Sacred to good memory. Ianuarius, faithful, who lived about 50 years, departed in peace. His wife did well for him, on the 3rd day before the Kalends of September.
EDCS-07400241.summary: A funerary epitaph to Ianuarius, likely of Christian faith, recording his lifespan and burial by his wife, with a date in late August.

EDCS-07400242.text_edition: \n Marcuana fidelix sic quae visit sic annis sic XXX mensis GIII dies cui maritus et parentes fecerunt bene\n
EDCS-07400242.translation: Marcuana, faithful, who lived 30 years, 3 months, and [---] days, for whom her husband and parents did well.
EDCS-07400242.summary: A funerary epitaph for Marcuana, recording her lifespan and erected by her husband and parents.

EDCS-07400243.text_edition: \n Bonae memoriae sacrum Marciana fidelis quae vixit nnos XLV menses VII dies GII quei sic bene fecerunt frater et fili praecessit in pace\n
EDCS-07400243.translation: Sacred to good memory. Marciana, faithful, who lived 45 years, 7 months, and 2 days, for whom her brother and son did well, preceded in peace.
EDCS-07400243.summary: A funerary epitaph for Marciana, likely of Christian faith, recording her lifespan and burial by her brother and son.

EDCS-07400245.text_edition: \n Bonae memoriae Prima fidelis quae vixit annis plus minus LXX mensibus VIIII diebus VII quei sic vene sic fecit Firmus praecessit in pace\n
EDCS-07400245.translation: Sacred to good memory. Prima, faithful, who lived about 70 years, 9 months, and 7 days, for whom Firmus did well, preceded in peace.
EDCS-07400245.summary: A funerary epitaph for Prima, likely of Christian faith, recording her lifespan and burial by Firmus.

EDCS-07400248.text_edition: \n Bonae memoriae nostri Primenius fidelis qui bisit sic annos plus menus sic LII defunctus est quartum Calendas sic Februarias qui sic bene fecet sic usor sic et fili eius\n
EDCS-07400248.translation: Here lies Primenius, our faithful, who lived about 52 years, departed on the 4th day before the Kalends of February, for whom his wife and his son did well.
EDCS-07400248.summary: A funerary epitaph for Primenius, likely of Christian faith, recording his lifespan and burial by his wife and son, with a date in late January.

EDCS-07400250.text_edition: \n Hic requiescet sic Gloriosa quae bixit sic Christo annos plus minus quinque\n
EDCS-07400250.translation: Here lies Gloriosa, who lived about five years in Christ.
EDCS-07400250.summary: A funerary epitaph for a young child named Gloriosa, likely of Christian faith, recording her age at death.

EDCS-07600165.text_edition: \n Octaviae Crotonidi Sexti Arelli Ursi coniugi merentissimae locus datus decreto decurionum\n
EDCS-07600165.translation: To Octavia Crotonis, most deserving wife of Sextus Arelis Ursus. A plot was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-07600165.summary: An epitaph recording the allocation of a burial plot by local officials to the wife of a prominent citizen.

EDCS-07600166.text_edition: \n Lucius Marius Luci filius Lucius Lurius Luci filius duumviri murum fornicem aream fecerunt\n
EDCS-07600166.translation: Lucius Marius, son of Lucius, and Lucius Lurius, son of Lucius, the duumvirs, built the wall, arch, and area.
EDCS-07600166.summary: This inscription records the construction of a wall, arch, and area by two duumvirs, likely in a public capacity.

EDCS-07600167.text_edition: \n Quinti filia Severinae ob merita patris ordo decurionum populusque aere conlato\n
EDCS-07600167.translation: The order of decurions and the people, with contributed money, [erected this] for Quintus' daughter Severina, because of her father's merits.
EDCS-07600167.summary: This inscription records a dedication made by the local council and populace for Severina due to her father's merits, funded by public subscription.

EDCS-08300231.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum Sextus Clodius Firmus vixit annos XVIIII patronus liberto bene merenti fecit\n
EDCS-08300231.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Sextus Clodius Firmus lived 19 years; his patron made [this] for a well-deserving freedman.
EDCS-08300231.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Sextus Clodius Firmus at 19 years old, dedicated by his patron.

EDCS-08300232.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum Iunia Caletyche vixit annos XX patronus libertae bene merenti fecit\n
EDCS-08300232.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Iunia Caletyche lived 20 years; her patron made [this] for a well-deserving freedwoman.
EDCS-08300232.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Iunia Caletyche at 20 years old, dedicated by her patron.

EDCS-08300233.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum Sextus Lucilius Felicianus verna Putiolanus sic vixit nnos LX coniux bene merenti fecit\n
EDCS-08300233.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Sextus Lucilius Felicianus, a slave born in the household at Puteoli, lived 60 years; his spouse made [this] for a well-deserving spouse.
EDCS-08300233.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Sextus Lucilius Felicianus at 60 years old, dedicated by his spouse.

EDCS-08300234.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Sileria Latice vixit annos XXXV menses V bene merenti fecit\n
EDCS-08300234.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the departed. Sileria Latice lived 35 years and 5 months; [she was dedicated] for a well-deserving person.
EDCS-08300234.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Sileria Latice at 35 years and 5 months, dedicated by a well-deserving person.

EDCS-08300235.summary: This is a brief funerary inscription recording the lifespan of Flavia Pherusa.

EDCS-08300236.text_edition: \n Have Cai Mari Ursule vixit nnos L\n
EDCS-08300236.translation: Hail Caius Marius Ursus, you lived 50 years.
EDCS-08300236.summary: This inscription is a greeting and record of the lifespan of Caius Marius Ursus.

EDCS-08300237.text_edition: \n Euctus publicus Petelinorum vilicus vixit annos XXIIII\n
EDCS-08300237.translation: Euctus, public official of the Petelini, lived 24 years.
EDCS-08300237.summary: This inscription records the death of Euctus, a public official of the Petelini, at the age of 24.

EDCS-08300238.text_edition: \n Have Megoni Natalis vixit annum I menses X sit tibi terra levis\n
EDCS-08300238.translation: Hail Megon Natalis, you lived 1 year and 10 months; may the earth lie lightly upon you.
EDCS-08300238.summary: This funerary inscription records the short life of Megon Natalis (1 year, 10 months) with a common wish for the deceased.

EDCS-08300239.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Helvi Lucani Helvius Priscus patri bene merenti fecit\n
EDCS-08300239.translation: To the Divine Manes. Helvius Priscus made this for his well-deserving father, Helvius Lucanus.
EDCS-08300239.summary: A funerary dedication made by a son for his father.

EDCS-08300240.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum Babulliae Marci filiae Villianae vixit annos XXII Marcus Vaonius Lucanus coniugi bene merenti et <sibi> fecit\n
EDCS-08300240.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Villiana, daughter of Marcus Babullius, lived 22 years. Marcus Vaonius Lucanus made this for his well-deserving wife and himself.
EDCS-08300240.summary: A funerary dedication by a husband for his deceased wife and himself, specifying her age at death.

EDCS-08300241.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Meneiae Cai filiae Marcellae Meneius Marcellus nepti et sibi\n
EDCS-08300241.translation: To the Divine Manes. Meneius Marcellus for his granddaughter Marcella, daughter of Caius, and for himself.
EDCS-08300241.summary: A funerary dedication by a grandfather for his granddaughter and himself.

EDCS-08300242.text_edition: \n Coelia Quinti filia Rufa hic est sita\n
EDCS-08300242.translation: Coelia Rufa, daughter of Quintus, is buried here.
EDCS-08300242.summary: A simple tombstone inscription identifying a woman buried at this location.

EDCS-08300243.text_edition: \n Firma Augantianae sic filiae titulum posuit quae vixit annis XXIIII diebus V Dis Manibus\n
EDCS-08300243.translation: Firma dedicated this monument to her daughter, who lived 22 years and 5 days. To the Divine Manes.
EDCS-08300243.summary: A funerary dedication by a mother for her daughter, specifying her age at death.

EDCS-08400178.text_edition: \n Ummidiae Flori Plaetorius Primus matri bene merenti\n
EDCS-08400178.translation: Plaetorius Primus for his well-deserving mother, Ummidia Flora.
EDCS-08400178.summary: A funerary dedication by a son for his mother.

EDCS-08400179.text_edition: \n Manius Megonius Eryx vixit nnos XIIX sit tibi terra levis\n
EDCS-08400179.translation: Manius Eryx, son of Megonius, lived 18 years. May the earth be light upon you.
EDCS-08400179.summary: A tombstone for a young man, Manius Eryx, who died at 18 years old, with a common epitaph.

EDCS-08400180.text_edition: \n Have Cai Aufidi Felix vixit nnos L\n
EDCS-08400180.translation: Greetings. Caius Aufidius Felix lived 50 years.
EDCS-08400180.summary: A tombstone inscription recording the name and age at death of Caius Aufidius Felix.

EDCS-08400181.text_edition: \n Have Cai Au<f=E>idi Successe vixit annos XXX sit tibi terra <l=E>(evis) \n
EDCS-08400181.translation: Greetings. Caius Aufidius Successus lived 30 years. May the earth be light upon you.
EDCS-08400181.summary: A tombstone inscription recording the name and age at death of Caius Aufidius Successus, with a common epitaph.

EDCS-08400182.text_edition: \n Have Philicia Luci filia Aphro vixit annos III menses XI dies X sit tibi terra levis\n
EDCS-08400182.translation: Greetings. Philicia, daughter of Lucius Aphro, lived 3 years, 11 months, and 10 days. May the earth be light upon you.
EDCS-08400182.summary: A tombstone inscription for a young child, Philicia, detailing her very short lifespan.

EDCS-08400183.text_edition: \n Have Silvia Sexti Arelli Ursi serva vixit nnos XXX fecit Dionysius conservae bene merenti\n
EDCS-08400183.translation: Have, slave of Sextus Arellius Ursius, lived 30 years. Dionysius made this for his well-deserving fellow slave.
EDCS-08400183.summary: This epitaph records the death of a slave named Have, dedicated by her fellow slave Dionysius, likely dating to the 1st-2nd century CE.

EDCS-08400184.text_edition: \n Diis Manibus Modiae Benedictae vixit annos XL\n
EDCS-08400184.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Modia Benedicta lived 40 years.
EDCS-08400184.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Modia Benedicta, who lived 40 years, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-08600134.text_edition: \n Publio Petronio Trophimo Petronia Chreste mater posuit Publius Petronius Tiasus posuit annorum XX hic iacet sepultus\n
EDCS-08600134.translation: Petronia Chreste, mother, set this up for Publius Petronius Trophimus. Publius Petronius Tiasus set this up. He lived 20 years and lies buried here.
EDCS-08600134.summary: This epitaph records the death of Publius Petronius Trophimus, set up by his mother and potentially another relative, indicating his burial place.

EDCS-09001262.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum Sexto Arellio Onesimo vixit annos LXV sit tibi terra levis\n
EDCS-09001262.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. For Sextus Arellius Onesimus, who lived 65 years. May the earth lie lightly upon you.
EDCS-09001262.summary: This funerary epitaph is dedicated to Sextus Arellius Onesimus, who lived 65 years, with a common wish for a light burial.

EDCS-09001263.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus have Caste mater filio pientissimo fecit qui vixit annos XVI menses VII dies XVIIII\n
EDCS-09001263.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. For Caste. A mother made this for her most dutiful son, who lived 16 years, 7 months, and 19 days.
EDCS-09001263.summary: This epitaph is a memorial from a mother to her son, Caste, who died at the age of 16 years, 7 months, and 19 days.

EDCS-09200228.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Nerviliae Narbuliae libertae bene merenti vixit annis IV et Caio Nervilio Iusto filio qui militavit in praetorio annis X vixit annis XXXII Caius Nervilius Iustus veteranus deductus Vellias militavit centurio in classe praetoria Misenense fecit sibi et suis bene merentibus\n
EDCS-09200228.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. For Nervilia Narbula, his freedwoman, who lived 4 years, and for Gaius Nervilius Justus, his son, who served in the Praetorian guard for 10 years and lived 32 years. Gaius Nervilius Justus, a veteran, discharged, served as centurion in the Praetorian fleet at Misenum. He made this for himself and his deserving relatives.
EDCS-09200228.summary: This complex funerary monument honors Nervilia Narbula and her son Gaius Nervilius Justus, a veteran of the Praetorian fleet at Misenum, who served for 10 years and lived 32 years.

EDCS-09200230.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Magnesiae vixit annos XVIII menses XI dies IIIX fecit Lucius Cominius Callistio bene merenti\n
EDCS-09200230.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. For Magnesia, who lived 18 years, 11 months, and 8 days. Lucius Cominius Callistio made this for his well-deserving [relative/friend].
EDCS-09200230.summary: This epitaph records the death of Magnesia, who lived 18 years, 11 months, and 8 days, and was memorialized by Lucius Cominius Callistio.

EDCS-09200231.text_edition: \n Iulia Lais sibi et Aulo Gabinio Auli filio Romilia Menandra suo aedili quaestori iterum et Gabinio Theophilo viro patri eius et suis\n
EDCS-09200231.translation: Iulia Lais for herself, and for Aulus Gabinius, son of Aulus, aedile, quaestor for the second time, and for Gabinius Theophilus, her father, and for her [other] relatives.
EDCS-09200231.summary: This funerary dedication by Iulia Lais is for herself, her father Gabinius Theophilus, and her husband Aulus Gabinius, who held the offices of aedile and quaestor.

EDCS-09200233.text_edition: \n Brittius Praesens vir clarissimus corrector curavit\n
EDCS-09200233.translation: Brittius Praesens, a man of consular rank, oversaw [this construction/dedication].
EDCS-09200233.summary: This inscription records that Brittius Praesens, a highly esteemed official (corrector), supervised the erection of a monument or dedication.

EDCS-09200237.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription that identifies an individual as the son of Cornelius.

EDCS-09200238.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus D Fortunato vixit annos VI Duc Chrysus filio pientissimo\n
EDCS-09200238.translation: To the departed spirits. Fortunatus lived 6 years. D[---] from Chrysus, his most dutiful son.
EDCS-09200238.summary: A funerary epitaph for a child named Fortunatus, dedicated by his son.

EDCS-09200239.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Chariteni filiae quae vixit annis VI mensibus X Margaris mater bene merenti fecit\n
EDCS-09200239.translation: To the departed spirits. Charitenis, his daughter, who lived 6 years and 10 months. Margaris, the mother, made this for her deserving daughter.
EDCS-09200239.summary: A funerary epitaph for a young girl named Charitenis, dedicated by her mother.

EDCS-09300190.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus nae Auli Quinti servae vixit annos XIX sine omine ullo florentes annos mors subita eripuit es contubernali optimae\n
EDCS-09300190.translation: To the departed spirits. To Nae, slave of Aulus Quintus, who lived 19 years without any ill omen; a sudden death snatched away her flourishing years. To her best companion.
EDCS-09300190.summary: A funerary epitaph for a slave woman named Nae, commemorating her youth and relationship.

EDCS-09300193.text_edition: \n Marco Arrio Marci filio Pomptina Clymeno IIviro quinquennali quaestori pecuniae publicae populus ex aere conlato ob munificentiam eius posuit quod eis annonam cratuitam sic de suo praebuerit ob cuius dedicationem epulum divisit decurionibus HS VIII nummum Augustalibus HS VI nummum populo viritim HS IIII nummum mulieribus HS II nummum loco dato decreto decurionum Curantes sic Publio Stlammio Simile et Tito Valerio Fabricio\n
EDCS-09300193.translation: The people, from bronze collected together, erected this to Marcus Arrius, son of Marcus, of the Pomptina tribe, quinquennial duovir, quaestor of public money, because of his generosity in providing the corn supply at a fixed price from his own means; on occasion of its dedication, he distributed a banquet: to the decurions 8 sesterces, to the Augustales 6 sesterces, to the people individually 4 sesterces, to the women 2 sesterces, on a site granted by decree of the decurions. Publius Stlammius Similis and Titus Valerius Fabricius oversaw it.
EDCS-09300193.summary: A public monument erected by the people to Marcus Arrius in recognition of his generosity in providing the grain supply and hosting a celebratory banquet, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-09400197.text_edition: \n Collegium dei invicti Aurio liberto pecunia sua fecit\n
EDCS-09400197.translation: The Collegium of the Invictus God erected this for Aurios, a freedman, with his own money.
EDCS-09400197.summary: A dedication made by a collegium (association) to their freedman.

EDCS-09400198.text_edition: \n Caius Iulius Cai libertus Phileros Marcus Avianius Marci libertus Philippus Menti Bonae sacraverunt\n
EDCS-09400198.translation: Gaius Julius Phileros, freedman of Gaius, and Marcus Avianius Philippus, freedman of Marcus, consecrated this to Menti Bonae.
EDCS-09400198.summary: A dedication to the deity Menti Bonae by two freedmen, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-09400199.text_edition: \n L(ucius) Fundanius Luci libertus Hermes magister Bonae Menti sacrum\n
EDCS-09400199.translation: Lucius Fundanius Hermes, freedman of Lucius, master, [made] this sacred offering to Bona Menti.
EDCS-09400199.summary: A dedication to the deity Bona Menti by a freedman serving as a magister (master or official).

EDCS-09400200.text_edition: \n Publius Tirienus Publi libertus Agatho magister Menti Bonae\n
EDCS-09400200.translation: Publius Tirienus Agatho, freedman of Publius, master, [made this offering] to Menti Bonae.
EDCS-09400200.summary: A dedication to the deity Menti Bonae by a freedman serving as a magister (master or official).

EDCS-09400201.text_edition: \n Publius Pomponius Lucanus Lucius Valerius Benignus magistri Menti Bonae Augustae sacraverunt\n
EDCS-09400201.translation: Publius Pomponius Lucanus and Lucius Valerius Benignus, masters, consecrated this to Menti Bonae Augustae.
EDCS-09400201.summary: A dedication to the imperial cult of Menti Bonae Augustae by two individuals serving as magistri (masters or officials).

EDCS-09400205.text_edition: \n Lucio Virusio Pollioni Daphno Augustali Sextiae Spuri filiae Cl Lucio Virusio Ianuario Augustali\n
EDCS-09400205.translation: To Lucius Virius Pollio Daphnus, Augustalis, and Sextia, daughter of Spurius, and Lucius Virius Ianuarius, Augustalis.
EDCS-09400205.summary: An inscription commemorating or dedicating to several individuals, at least two of whom held the rank of Augustalis, suggesting an imperial cult or public honors context.

EDCS-09400207.text_edition: \n Numerius Numestius Callistratus Marcus Suitius Andronicus\n
EDCS-09400207.translation: Numerius Numestius Callistratus, Marcus Suitius Andronicus.
EDCS-09400207.summary: This is a funerary inscription commemorating Numerius Numestius Callistratus and Marcus Suitius Andronicus.

EDCS-09400208.text_edition: \n Marco Mineio Marci filio Marci nepoti Flacco tribuno militum Mineia soror\n
EDCS-09400208.translation: Mineia, sister, [erected this] to Marcus Mineius Flaccus, son of Marcus, grandson of Marcus, tribune of the soldiers.
EDCS-09400208.summary: This is a funerary inscription honoring Marcus Mineius Flaccus, a military tribune, erected by his sister.

EDCS-09400209.text_edition: \n Lucio Mineio Marci filio Marci nepoti Mineia soror\n
EDCS-09400209.translation: Mineia, sister, [erected this] to Lucius Mineius, son of Marcus, grandson of Marcus.
EDCS-09400209.summary: This is a funerary inscription honoring Lucius Mineius, erected by his sister.

EDCS-09400212.text_edition: \n Gaio Pomponio Marci Pomponi Libonis trierarchi filio Maecia Diogeni duoviro quinquennali huic ordo decurionum ob munificentiam eius quot sic familiam gladiatoriam ex sua liberalitate ob honorem quinquennalitatis primus ediderit item acceptis sestertium XXV milibus nummum pecunia publica alium diem enixe curaverit statuam ponendam pecunia publica censuerunt loco dato decreto decurionum\n
EDCS-09400212.translation: The order of decurions decreed that a statue be erected at public expense to Gaius Pomponius Diogenes, son of Marcus, grandson of Marcus Pomponius Libo, trierarch, duovir quinquennalis, because he was the first to present a gladiatorial troupe at his own expense for his quinquennial term, and moreover, by diligently arranging another day with 25,000 sesterces of public money, he took care of it; the site was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-09400212.summary: This inscription records a decree by the decurions to erect a statue honoring Gaius Pomponius Diogenes for his munificence in sponsoring gladiatorial games and managing public funds during his quinquennial term, likely dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-09400213.text_edition: \n Marco Pomponio Marci Pomponi Libonis trierarchi filio Maecia Diogeni duoviro quinquennali coloni ex aere collato statuam quam honoris causa vivo ei summa effecta optulerunt sic Titus Flavius Marullus trierarchus Augustalis et Lucius Dicitius Artemidorus heredes ponendam curaverunt\n
EDCS-09400213.translation: The colonists, with funds collected, erected this statue in honor, while he was alive, to Marcus Pomponius Diogenes, son of Marcus, grandson of Marcus Pomponius Libo, trierarch, duovir quinquennalis, which they presented to him when his highest office was achieved; moreover, the heirs Titus Flavius Marullus, trierarch Augustalis, and Lucius Dicitius Artemidorus took care to have it erected.
EDCS-09400213.summary: This inscription records the erection of a statue by colonists to Marcus Pomponius Diogenes, a duovir quinquennalis, for his achievements, with the heirs of the statue's commissioner overseeing its construction, likely dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-09400214.text_edition: \n Caio Plaetorio Cai filio Crescenti IIviro ob munificentiam eius quod is populo in annonam HS XXV milia nummum ab herede suo dari iusserit statuamque sibi ab eodem remissa pecunia publica poni caverit ob cuius dedicationem decurionibus singulis HS XII nummos Vinicius Maecia Lucanus Laurens praetor heres ex testamento dedit loco dato decreto decurionum\n
EDCS-09400214.translation: The order of decurions granted the site for a statue to Gaius Plaetorius Crescent, son of Gaius, duovir, because he ordered that 25,000 sesterces be given to the people for the grain supply by his heir, and that a statue be erected for himself with money remitted by the same heir from public funds; for its dedication, Vinicius Maecia Lucanus Laurens, as praetor and heir by testament, gave 12 sesterces to each of the decurions.
EDCS-09400214.summary: This decree records the erection of a statue honoring Gaius Plaetorius Crescent, a duovir, for his munificence in providing funds for the grain supply and for remitting money for his statue, with his heir distributing funds to decurions on the dedication day, likely dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-09400215.text_edition: \n Marco Egnio Marci filio Maecia Fortunatiano IIviro iterum quinquennali huic splendidissimus ordo decurionum postulante populo ob praecipuam et insignem munificentiam erga patriam statuam ponendam decrevit quod cum XXV (milibus) HS acceptis at sic conparationem familiae gladiatoriae maiorem quantitatem auxerit at sic nobilium gladiatorum conductionem adiectis etiam ursis mirae magnitudinis set sic et noxeo sic omni quoque cultu atparatuque sic aucto diem sublimiter exornavit\n
EDCS-09400215.translation: The most distinguished order of decurions, at the request of the people, decreed that a statue be erected to Marcus Egnus Fortunatianus, son of Marcus, duovir for the second time, quinquennalis, because of his outstanding and remarkable munificence towards his fatherland; for, having received 25,000 sesterces, he increased the provision of a gladiatorial troupe and added the engagement of distinguished gladiators, as well as bears of amazing size, and moreover, he greatly adorned the day with every kind of service and preparation.
EDCS-09400215.summary: This inscription details the decree by the decurions to erect a statue honoring Marcus Egnus Fortunatianus, a duovir quinquennalis, for his exceptional generosity in funding gladiatorial games, including exotic animals and performers, likely dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-09400218.text_edition: \n Marco Tullio Ciceroni Venneiano patrono coloniae Paestanorum praetori Laurentium Lavinatium splendido equiti Romano s tabularius\n
EDCS-09400218.translation: To Marcus Tullius Cicero Venneianus, patron of the people of Paestum, praetor of the Laurentes Lavinates, distinguished Roman knight.
EDCS-09400218.summary: This is an honorary inscription for Marcus Tullius Cicero Venneianus, who held significant civic and military positions, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09400220.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Marcus Tullius Marci filius Maecia Cicero equiti Romano sibi fecit vivus\n
EDCS-09400220.translation: To the Divine Shades. Marcus Tullius Cicero, son of Marcus, distinguished Roman knight, made this for himself while alive.
EDCS-09400220.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Marcus Tullius Cicero, a distinguished Roman knight, made by himself during his lifetime, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-09400223.text_edition: \n Caius Camurtius Cai filius Caius Vibius Cai filius IIviri faciendum ex senatus consulto curaverunt\n
EDCS-09400223.translation: Gaius Camurtius, son of Gaius, and Gaius Vibius, son of Gaius, duovirs, carried out the construction by decree of the Senate.
EDCS-09400223.summary: This inscription records that two duovirs, Gaius Camurtius and Gaius Vibius, oversaw the construction of a public work as mandated by a senatorial decree, likely dating to the Roman Republican or early Imperial period.

EDCS-09400224.text_edition: \n Lucius Caesius Luci filius M Marcus Valerius Marci filius Rufus IIviri macerias circum virecta ex senatus consulto faciendas coeraverunt\n
EDCS-09400224.translation: Lucius Caesius, son of Lucius, and Marcus Valerius Rufus, son of Marcus, as IIviri, took care that the walls around the pleasure grounds were built in accordance with a decree of the Senate.
EDCS-09400224.summary: This inscription records the construction of walls around pleasure grounds, overseen by two magistrates (IIviri) by senatorial decree.

EDCS-09400225.text_edition: \n Caius Sextilius Luci filius Publius Claudius Cai filius IIviri de senatus sententia\n
EDCS-09400225.translation: Gaius Sextilius, son of Lucius, and Publius Claudius, son of Gaius, as IIviri, by decision of the Senate.
EDCS-09400225.summary: This inscription records the action of two magistrates (IIviri) taken by senatorial decision.

EDCS-09400226.text_edition: \n Lucius Galonius Luci libertus A de suo faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-09400226.translation: Lucius Galonius, freedman of Lucius A, took care to have it built at his own expense.
EDCS-09400226.summary: This inscription records a public work undertaken at personal expense by Lucius Galonius, a freedman.

EDCS-09400227.translation: To Quintus Lautinius, son of Publius, the architect.
EDCS-09400227.summary: This is a dedication to Quintus Lautinius, an architect.

EDCS-09400228.text_edition: \n Laureia Quinti filia Polla aedem Isidis cum porticus sic pecunia sua restituit decreto decurionum\n
EDCS-09400228.translation: Laureia Polla, daughter of Quintus, restored the temple of Isis with its porticoes at her own expense by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-09400228.summary: This inscription records the restoration of the temple of Isis and its porticoes, funded by Laureia Polla at her own expense by decree of local councillors.

EDCS-09400231.text_edition: \n L(ucio) Venedio Luci liberto o qui vixit annos LX v(ivo) Lucio Venedio Luci liberto Artemidoro vivae VenediaI sic Luci libertae Philumenae vivo Lucio Venedio Luci liberto Afro\n
EDCS-09400231.translation: Of Lucius Venedius, freedman of Lucius, who lived 60 years, [while] Lucius Venedius, freedman of Lucius, is alive, and Venedia, freedwoman of Lucius, and Philumena, freedwoman of Lucius, and Afro.
EDCS-09400231.summary: This inscription likely records a funerary monument or endowment involving Lucius Venedius and his freedmen and freedwomen, with a note about the age of one individual.

EDCS-09400232.text_edition: \n Cineribus Luci Vari Primi trierarchi de liburna Diana\n
EDCS-09400232.translation: For the ashes of Lucius Varius Primus, trierarch of the gunboat Diana.
EDCS-09400232.summary: This inscription is a dedication for the remains of Lucius Varius Primus, who served as a trierarch on a naval vessel named Diana.

EDCS-09400233.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Caio Valerio Nasoni militi ex classe praetoria Misenensi centuria Secundi vixit annis XXXX militavit annis XXIII Amatia Callytiche coniugi bene merenti fecit\n
EDCS-09400233.translation: To Gaius Valerius Nason, soldier of the praetorian fleet at Misenum, century of Secundus, who lived 40 years and served 23 years. Amatia Callytiche made [this] for her deserving husband.
EDCS-09400233.summary: This is a tombstone for Gaius Valerius Nason, a soldier in the praetorian fleet, erected by his wife.

EDCS-09400234.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Nonia Zoe hic quiescit Quintus Geminius Artemidorus uxori pientissimae\n
EDCS-09400234.translation: To the divine spirits. Nonia Zoe rests here. Quintus Geminius Artemidorus [made this] for his most dutiful wife.
EDCS-09400234.summary: This tombstone records the burial of Nonia Zoe, for whom her husband Quintus Geminius Artemidorus erected a memorial.

EDCS-09400235.translation: Lucius Lollius Diogenes made [this] for himself.
EDCS-09400235.summary: This inscription records a self-funded funerary monument or endowment made by Lucius Lollius Diogenes.

EDCS-09400236.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Quinto Veratio Volusiano vixiit sic annos LI menses X dies XXII\n
EDCS-09400236.translation: To the departed spirits. Quintus Veratius Volusianus lived for 51 years, 10 months, and 22 days.
EDCS-09400236.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Quintus Veratius Volusianus.

EDCS-09400237.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Numoniae Veneriae coniugi dulcissimae pientissimae quae vicxit sic mecum annis sic VIII menses VII dies XV nnm XXVII bene merenti Nannaeius sic Quetinus\n
EDCS-09400237.translation: To the departed spirits. For Numnonia Veneria, his most beloved and most dutiful wife, who lived with me for 8 years, 7 months, and 15 days. For her, who deserved well, Nannaeus Quetinus. (He lived 27 years).
EDCS-09400237.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated by Nannaeus Quetinus to his wife Numnonia Veneria, recording her lifespan and their years of marriage.

EDCS-09400238.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Valeriae Luci filiae Marianae vixit annos II dies XL\n
EDCS-09400238.translation: To the departed spirits. Valeria Mariana, daughter of Lucius, lived for 2 years and 40 days.
EDCS-09400238.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Valeria Mariana, daughter of Lucius.

EDCS-09400239.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Iucundo Sotera coniugi bene merenti fecit\n
EDCS-09400239.translation: To the departed spirits. For Iucundus, to his well-deserving wife Sotera, he made this.
EDCS-09400239.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Iucundus for his deserving wife Sotera.

EDCS-09401030.text_edition: \n Aulo Gabinio Crispino Quinto Caeio Secundo Gabiniae Crispinae ultimae gentis suae\n
EDCS-09401030.translation: For Aulus Gabinius Crispinus, for Quintus Caelius Secundus, for Gabinia”（Crispina） the last of their family.
EDCS-09401030.summary: This is a funerary inscription commemorating Aulus Gabinius Crispinus, Quintus Caelius Secundus, and Gabinia Crispina, possibly family members.

EDCS-09401032.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Iulius Callistus vixit annos XV menses VI quod facere debuerit ille patri suo fecit Iulius Acianus pater filio pientissimo\n
EDCS-09401032.translation: To the departed spirits. Iulius Callistus lived for 15 years and 6 months. What he ought to have done for his father, his father Iulius Acianus did for his most dutiful son.
EDCS-09401032.summary: This is a funerary epitaph where a father, Iulius Acianus, sets up a monument for his son Iulius Callistus, who died at 15.

EDCS-09401033.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Terentiae Compses fecerunt Terentius Scymnus et Philistia Iucundilla fecerunt matri bene merenti\n
EDCS-09401033.translation: To the departed spirits. Terentius Scymnus and Philistia Iucundilla made this for their deserving mother.
EDCS-09401033.summary: This funerary epitaph records that Terentius Scymnus and Philistia Iucundilla erected a monument for their deserving mother.

EDCS-09401034.text_edition: \n Valeria Publi filia Florilla fecit sibi et Publio Valerio Felicioni liberto et delicio suo qui vixit annos XV\n
EDCS-09401034.translation: Valeria Florilla, daughter of Publius, made this for herself, and for Publius Valerius Felicioni, her freedman and darling, who lived for 15 years.
EDCS-09401034.summary: This funerary epitaph records that Valeria Florilla dedicated the monument to herself and her freedman and darling, Publius Valerius Felicioni, who died at 15.

EDCS-09700119.text_edition: \n Caio Mulvio Cai filio Pomptina Ofillio Restituto aedili praetori IIviro quinquennali quaestori praefecto cohortis I Morinorum et Cersiacorum tribuno militum legionis II adiutricis piae fidelis praefecto alae I Vespasianae Dardanorum praefecto fabrum II Augustales Herculani patrono\n
EDCS-09700119.translation: For Gaius Mulvius, son of Caius, (who held the offices of) aedile, praetor, duovir for five years, quaestor, prefect of the I Morinorum cohort and the Cersiacorum, military tribune of the II Adjutrix legion, pious and faithful, prefect of the I Vespasiana Dardanorum ala, prefect of craftsmen, an Augustal, patron of Herculani.
EDCS-09700119.summary: This is a public inscription honoring Gaius Mulvius, son of Caius, listing his extensive career in various military and civic offices.

EDCS-09700946.text_edition: \n Spediae Cai filiae Gallae vixit annos II menses X Caio Spedio Cai filio Basso vixit annos VI menses X Caio Spedio Cai filio Basso ae Spedi \n
EDCS-09700946.translation: For Spedia Galla, daughter of Caius, lived for 2 years and 10 months. For Gaius Spedius Bassus, son of Caius, lived for 6 years and 10 months. For Gaius Spedius Bassus, son of Caius. (For) Ae Spedius.
EDCS-09700946.summary: This funerary inscription records the deaths of Spedia Galla and two individuals named Gaius Spedius Bassus, sons of Caius, and possibly another Spedius.

EDCS-09701429.text_edition: \n Titidia Cnaei liberta Sura Titidia |(mulieris) liberta Salvia fecit sibi et suis\n
EDCS-09701429.translation: Sura, freedwoman of Titidius (son of Cnaeus), made this for herself and her family, her freedwoman Salvia, wife of Titidius.
EDCS-09701429.summary: A funerary inscription by a freedwoman for herself and her family, likely dating to the early Imperial period.

EDCS-09800086.text_edition: \n Caio Caesari pontifici maximo imperatori consuli tertium ex senatus consulto populus patrono\n
EDCS-09800086.translation: To Gaius Caesar, pontifex maximus, imperator, consul for the third time, patron of the people, by decree of the Senate.
EDCS-09800086.summary: A dedication from the Roman Senate and people to Gaius Caesar, son of Augustus, likely dating to his consulship around 1 CE.

EDCS-10700899.summary: A personal name inscription, possibly a tombstone or dedication by Lucius Ansius Quintillianus.

EDCS-10700901.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum Aurelius Diogenes veteranus vixit annis I mensibus\n
EDCS-10700901.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Aurelius Diogenes, veteran, lived for one year and [? months].
EDCS-10700901.summary: A funerary inscription for Aurelius Diogenes, a veteran, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10700903.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Sepptimus vixit ann(os) XXXV colle<g=C>ius sic Geni municipii et coniuxs sic bene merenti fecerunt \n
EDCS-10700903.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Sepptimus lived 35 years. Colle(g)ius and his wife, in accordance with the spirit of the municipality, made this for him as a well-deserving person.
EDCS-10700903.summary: A funerary inscription for Sepptimus, erected by his wife and likely a municipal official, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10700904.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum vixit annis LX collegius sic Serapis et Iunonis fecerunt sic Tauriane sic\n
EDCS-10700904.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Lived 60 years. The college of Serapis and Juno made this for Tauriana.
EDCS-10700904.summary: A funerary inscription for Tauriana, dedicated by the college of Serapis and Juno, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-10700905.summary: A funerary inscription for Calliste, a freedwoman, indicating the beginning of a text that is now lost.

EDCS-10700906.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Cornelia Urbana vixit annis coniux bene merenti fecit\n
EDCS-10700906.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Cornelia Urbana lived for [? years]. Her wife made this for her as a deserving person.
EDCS-10700906.summary: A funerary inscription for Cornelia Urbana, erected by her wife, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10700907.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Duc Doryphoride sic alumnae vixit annis X patrona fecit\n
EDCS-10700907.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. Duc Doryphoride lived for 10 years. His patroness made this for him as a deserving foster child.
EDCS-10700907.summary: A funerary inscription for Duc Doryphoride, a foster child, erected by his patroness, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10700908.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum iae Eubiotae coniugi dulcissimae mulieri sanctissimae Pharus maritus bene merenti fecit\n
EDCS-10700908.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. To Iae Eubiota, his most sweet wife, a most holy woman. Pharus, her husband, made this for her as a deserving person.
EDCS-10700908.summary: A funerary inscription for Eubiota, erected by her husband Pharus, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10700909.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus es vixit annis XXIII mensibus Felicula mater filio karissimo et pientissimo\n
EDCS-10700909.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. [...] lived 23 years and [? months]. Felicula, his mother, for her dearest and most dutiful son.
EDCS-10700909.summary: A funerary inscription for a son, erected by his mother Felicula, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10700910.translation: His wife made this for him, a deserving man.
EDCS-10700910.summary: This is a funerary inscription from a husband to his well-deserving wife.

EDCS-10700911.translation: To the departed spirits. Vagellia Methe lived 39 years. Her husband [made this] for his most deserving wife.
EDCS-10700911.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Vagellia Methe, who died at the age of 39, set up by her husband.

EDCS-10700912.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Salvia Octavia vixit nnos VI menses II mater bene merenti\n
EDCS-10700912.translation: To the departed spirits. Salvia Octavia lived 6 years and 2 months. Her mother made this for her well-deserving daughter.
EDCS-10700912.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Salvia Octavia, who died at the age of 6 years and 2 months, set up by her mother.

EDCS-10700913.translation: Tullia, freedwoman of Cespius, Zosima, greetings.
EDCS-10700913.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Zosima, a freedwoman, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-10700914.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum Lucio Vagellio Baroni vixit annos III menses III parentes filio dulcissimo\n
EDCS-10700914.translation: To the departed spirits and sacred to Lucius Vagellius Baron, who lived 3 years and 3 months. His parents made this for their dearest son.
EDCS-10700914.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lucius Vagellius Baron, who died at the age of 3 years and 3 months, set up by his parents.

EDCS-10700915.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Vagellia Tyche vixit annis XXXXII filia matri pientissimae fecit\n
EDCS-10700915.translation: To the departed spirits. Vagellia Tyche lived 42 years. Her daughter made this for her most devoted mother.
EDCS-10700915.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Vagellia Tyche, who died at the age of 42, set up by her daughter.

EDCS-10700919.text_edition: \n Sanctum mundum Attinis pro reditu a fundamentis Helviae Abascante et Capitolina filia decreto decurionum pecunia sua fecerunt\n
EDCS-10700919.translation: Attinis made this sacred structure, sound and whole, from the foundations for Helvia Abascante and her daughter Capitolina, with their own money, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-10700919.summary: This inscription records the construction of a sacred building by Attinis for Helvia Abascante and her daughter, funded by them and approved by the town council.

EDCS-10700920.text_edition: \n Plotia Rutila spectacula ima maeniana et pulpitum scaenae decreto decurionum sua pecunia faciundum curavit eademque probavit\n
EDCS-10700920.translation: Plotia Rutila had the lower seating area and the stage floor constructed at her own expense and also approved them, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-10700920.summary: This inscription records Plotia Rutila's funding and approval of the construction of the lower seating area and stage floor of a theater or similar venue, by decree of the decurions.

EDCS-10700924.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Cai Brutti Praesentis servo conservo carissimo fecit cum quo vixit annos XX\n
EDCS-10700924.translation: To the departed spirits. [This was made by] Caius Bruttius Praesens for his dearest fellow slave and companion, with whom he lived for 20 years.
EDCS-10700924.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a slave, set up by a fellow slave with whom he shared 20 years of life.

EDCS-10700928.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Marco Teltonio Mercurio Acilia Iucunda marito optimo bene merenti fecit\n
EDCS-10700928.translation: To the departed spirits. Acilia Iucunda made this for her excellent husband, Marcus Teltonius Mercurius, a deserving man.
EDCS-10700928.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Marcus Teltonius Mercurius, set up by his wife Acilia Iucunda.

EDCS-10700929.text_edition: \n Herennia viro suo bene merenti posuit\n
EDCS-10700929.translation: Herennia dedicated [this] to her deserving husband.
EDCS-10700929.summary: A wife dedicates a monument to her deserving husband.

EDCS-10700934.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Luciis Vetinis Paulo et Severino filiis pientissimis et uxori matri filiorum et Aciliae bene merentibus fecit Vetina Severus aedilis IIvir suis Pontiae Esperidi et Aciliae Soteri et sibi vivos fecit\n
EDCS-10700934.translation: To the departed spirits. Vetina Severus, aedile and duovir, made [this] for his very dutiful sons Lucius Vetinius Paulus and Severinus, and for his wife, the mother of his sons, and for the deserving Acilia, and for himself while alive.
EDCS-10700934.summary: A man sets up a family tomb for himself, his wife, and his sons, and identifies himself by his magistracies, likely in the early imperial period.

EDCS-10700938.text_edition: \n Gresio Cai filio Horatia Liboni fratri\n
EDCS-10700938.translation: To Gresius, son of Caius, to Horatius Libo, his brother.
EDCS-10700938.summary: A tombstone for Gresius, son of Caius, dedicated by his brother.

EDCS-10700939.text_edition: \n Insteiae Quinti filiae Firmae Quinto Instio sic Quinti filio Pomptina Cimbro Aemiliae Cai filiae Bassae Quinto Insteio Quinti filio Gresia Cai filia Tertia sibi et suis fecit\n
EDCS-10700939.translation: Quinto Instio, son of Quintus, [and] Gresia, daughter of Caius, Tertia, [and] the wife of Quintus Instius, son of Quintus, Pomptina Cimbri, daughter of Aemilia, daughter of Caius Bassus, made [this] for themselves and their families.
EDCS-10700939.summary: A family tomb set up by Gresia, daughter of Caius, Tertia, for herself, her family, and others including a Quinto Instio.

EDCS-10700942.translation: [---]s, son of Caius, Po[---]alis and C[---] [---] Celadus(?).
EDCS-10700942.summary: A fragmented tombstone inscription mentioning individuals, possibly including Celadus.

EDCS-10700943.summary: A very brief funerary inscription indicating that Tertia erected the monument.

EDCS-10701369.text_edition: \n Imperatori Caesari divi Traiani Parthici filio divi Nervae nepoti Traiano Hadriano Augusto pontifici maximo tribunicia potestate IIII consuli III patri patriae decreto decurionum publice\n
EDCS-10701369.translation: By decree of the council, publicly [dedicated] to the Emperor, Caesar, son of the divine Trajan, the Parthian, nephew of the divine Nerva, Trajan Hadrian Augustus, chief priest, with tribunician power for the fourth time, consul for the third time, father of the country.
EDCS-10701369.summary: A public dedication of a monument to Emperor Hadrian, likely during his reign (c. 117-138 AD).

EDCS-10701370.text_edition: \n Domino nostro Flavio Valerio Constantio nobilissimo ordo splendidissimae civitatis Reginae devotus numini maiestatiqye sic aeius sic\n
EDCS-10701370.translation: To our lord Flavius Valerius Constantius, most noble. The council of the most splendid city of Regína, devoted to his divine majesty and power, [erected this].
EDCS-10701370.summary: The city council of Regina dedicates a monument to the emperor Constantius, likely Constantius Chlorus (late 3rd/early 4th century AD).

EDCS-10701374.text_edition: \n Tito Sextio Titi filio Veturia Laterano clarissimo puero patrono ob multa merita parentium eius Regienses Iulii dono dedit\n
EDCS-10701374.translation: The people of Regium, of the tribe Iulia, dedicated [this] to Titus Sextius Lateranus, son of Titus, a most distinguished boy, patron, because of the many merits of his parents.
EDCS-10701374.summary: The citizens of Regium dedicate a monument to Titus Sextius Lateranus, honoring his merits and his parents.

EDCS-10701375.text_edition: \n Quintus Sattius Flavius Vettius Gratus vir clarissimus augur publicus populi Romani Quiritium corrector sacrario a solo restituto\n
EDCS-10701375.translation: Quintus Sattius Flavius Vettius Gratus, most distinguished man, public augur of the Roman Quirites, corrector, after the sanctuary was restored from the ground up.
EDCS-10701375.summary: This inscription records the restoration of a sanctuary by Quintus Sattius Flavius Vettius Gratus, a prominent official.

EDCS-10701376.text_edition: \n Flavio Zenodoro viro clarissimo vita dum fretum Hesperios inter Siculosque relabans miscebit tortis aequora gurgitibus semper honos nomenque tuum laudesque manebunt Flavio Hadriano Hierio Zenodoro viro clarissimo correctori Lucaniae et Bryttiae sic ordo populusque Reginorum ad sempiternam memoriam eius posuerunt\n
EDCS-10701376.translation: Flavio Zenodoro, most distinguished man, when he shall mix with the western seas and Sicilian waters, ever shall honor, name, and praises remain. The order and people of Reginum erected this to his eternal memory for Flavio Hadrianus Hierius Zenodoro, most distinguished man, corrector of Lucania and Bryttia.
EDCS-10701376.summary: This inscription is a posthumous honorific dedication by the community of Reginum for Flavio Zenodoro, a distinguished corrector.

EDCS-10701378.text_edition: \n Caius Iulius Iuliae divi Augusti filiae libertus Celos sic sibi et Caio Iulio Iuliae divi Augusti filiae liberto Thiaso patri sexviro Augustali et Iuliae divai sic Augustae libertae matri ex testamento\n
EDCS-10701378.translation: Celos, freedman of Julia, daughter of the deified Augustus, to himself, and to his father Caius Iulius Thiasos, freedman of Julia, daughter of the deified Augustus, and freedman of the deified Augusta, a sexvir Augustalis, and to his mother Iulia, freedwoman of the deified Augusta, by his will.
EDCS-10701378.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by Celos for himself, his father, and his mother, who were freedmen and freedwomen associated with the imperial family.

EDCS-10701379.text_edition: \n Caio Iulio Neoptolemi filio Euandro trierarcho Caius Iulius Cai filius Niger trierarchus\n
EDCS-10701379.translation: To Caius Iulius Euander, son of Neoptolemus, trierarch. Caius Iulius Niger, son of Caius, trierarch.
EDCS-10701379.summary: This inscription records two trierarchs, Caius Iulius Euander and Caius Iulius Niger.

EDCS-10701380.text_edition: \n Marco Fabio Colendo librario notario vixit annis XIX Cinarus paedagogus sibi et suis\n
EDCS-10701380.translation: To Marcus Fabius Colendus, scribe and notary. Lived 19 years. Cinarus, the pedagogue, for himself and his family.
EDCS-10701380.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Marcus Fabius Colendus, a scribe and notary, set up by his pedagogue.

EDCS-10701382.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Cerinthus vixit nnos XXXVII\n
EDCS-10701382.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Cerinthus lived 37 years.
EDCS-10701382.summary: This is a simple funerary dedication to the Manes for Cerinthus.

EDCS-10701383.text_edition: \n vixit annos XL Paezusa mater eius vixit annos XXC Hecebolus cognatus de suo\n
EDCS-10701383.translation: Lived 40 years. Paezusa, his mother, lived 20 years. Hecebolus, a relative, from his own funds.
EDCS-10701383.summary: This tombstone records the ages of death for an individual and his mother, with a relative contributing to the monument.

EDCS-10701384.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Paulina vixit annos XXXVII menses V dies XXIII\n
EDCS-10701384.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Paulina lived 37 years, 5 months, and 23 days.
EDCS-10701384.summary: This is a funerary dedication to the Manes for Paulina, specifying her age in years, months, and days.

EDCS-10701385.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Marcus Petronius Dionysius vixit nnos LIII Crania Iulia fecit\n
EDCS-10701385.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Marcus Petronius Dionysius lived 53 years. Crania Iulia made this.
EDCS-10701385.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Marcus Petronius Dionysius and was erected by Crania Iulia.
