EDCS-10701386.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Quintius Ianuarius qui vixit annos XXV Quintia vixit annos V menses X dies Quintia Vagelliana coniugi et filiae bene merentibus\n
EDCS-10701386.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Quintus Ianuarius, who lived 25 years. Quintia lived 5 years, 10 months, and days. Quintia Vagelliana for her well-deserving husband and daughter.
EDCS-10701386.summary: This tombstone is dedicated by Quintia Vagelliana to her husband Quintus Ianuarius and daughter Quintia.

EDCS-10701387.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Balerio sic Boeotiano vixit annos VIII Staberia Aprilla vixit annos XL Valerius Boeotianus bene merentibus\n
EDCS-10701387.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Boeotianus Valerius lived for 8 years. Staberia Aprilla lived for 40 years. Valerius Boeotianus [erected this] for those who deserved well.
EDCS-10701387.summary: A funerary epitaph for a father and daughter, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period, with the father, Valerius Boeotianus, dedicating the monument.

EDCS-10701393.text_edition: \n Imperator Caesar Marcus Valerius Maxentius Pius Felix Invictus ac perpetuus semper Augustus milia passuum DDominis nnostris Invictissimis Imperatoribus Valentiniano et Valenti AAuggustis bono rei publicae natis ------] bono rei publicae natis \n
EDCS-10701393.translation: From Emperor Caesar Marcus Valerius Maxentius Pius Felix Invictus and perpetual Augustus, for a distance of miles, by order of our unconquered Lords Emperors Valentinianus and Valens, born for the good of the state, [erected] for the good of the state.
EDCS-10701393.summary: This inscription records a milestone or road construction, dedicated to the emperors Valentinianus and Valens, likely during the reign of Maxentius in the late 4th century CE.

EDCS-10701708.text_edition: \n Traiano Hadriano Augusto pontifici maximo tribunicia potestate II patri patriae consuli II decreto decurionum\n
EDCS-10701708.translation: To Trajan Hadrian Augustus, chief priest, holding tribunician power for the second time, father of the fatherland, consul for the second time, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-10701708.summary: A dedication on a monument or public building in honor of Emperor Hadrian, likely from the 2nd century CE, showing his various titles and honors granted by local authorities.

EDCS-10701709.text_edition: \n Valerio Cai filio Romilia Caepioni aedili IIIIviro D P HOLAR C vixit annos XLII Valeria Caepilia patri\n
EDCS-10701709.translation: To Valerius, son of Caius, of the Romilia tribe, aedile, duovir. [He] lived for 42 years. Valeria Caepilia [erected this] for her father.
EDCS-10701709.summary: A funerary epitaph for Valerius, son of Caius, who held local magistracies, erected by his daughter Valeria Caepilia, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10801419.translation: Here lies in peace Maria. She lived for 2 years. Completed on the 20th of July, in the consulship of Flavius Faustus (?).
EDCS-10801419.summary: A Greek epitaph for a child named Maria who died young, with her lifespan and burial date given, likely from the late Roman or Byzantine period.

EDCS-10801423.translation: In the consulship of Flavius Philippus and Sallius, on the Ides of January. [I, the] deacon, made [this] for my wife, who lived with me for 3 years, most sweet and most chaste. Placed in peace.
EDCS-10801423.summary: A Latin funerary inscription for a deacon's wife, who lived with him for three years, placed in peace, dating to the consulship of Philippus and Sallius (likely 5th century CE).

EDCS-10801424.text_edition: \n Leucosius episcopus Flavio Eventio filio centurioni qui vixit annis XXXV mensibus sex hic militavit annis XIII pater filio fecit in pace positus in PXChristo\n
EDCS-10801424.translation: Leucosius the bishop [erected this] for his son Flavius Eventius, a centurion who lived for 35 years and 6 months. He served here for 13 years. The father made [this] for his son, placed in Christ.
EDCS-10801424.summary: A funerary inscription by a bishop for his son, a centurion, who served in the army for 13 years and died at 35, likely from the late Roman or early Christian period.

EDCS-10801440.translation: Of good memory. Primenius the faithful lived for more or less 52 years. He died on the fourth day before the Kalends of February. His wife and sons who did well erected [this]. To the Spirits of the Underworld. To Claudius Helios, who lived for 64 years and 2 months. Aurelia Marta erected [this] for her deserving husband.
EDCS-10801440.summary: A bilingual or two-part funerary epitaph with one section for Primenius and another for Claudius Helios, with familial dedications, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11400093.translation: Tiberius Bervenus Sabinus, son of Tiberius, duovir with curule aedile power for the second time, bequeathed by his will to the citizens of Reginum Iulium, in the prytaneum, a bronze statue of Mercury, a silver basin, seven silver Lares, a Corinthian bronze basin; also in the temple of Apollo the Greater, writing tablets of parchment with ivory covers, an ivory box, and nineteen painted panels. His heirs took care of their placement.
EDCS-11400093.summary: A detailed will of Tiberius Bervenus Sabinus, a local magistrate, bequeathing various valuable items, including religious and artistic objects, to the municipality and a temple, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11400094.text_edition: \n V Idus Apriles Imperatore Vespasiano Caesare Augusto VIIII consule Tito Vespasiano Caesare Augusti filio VII consule ob munificentiam earum quae dendrophoros honoraverunt honos decretus est eis quae infra scriptae sunt Claudia Iusta IVA sacrata Sia Faustina sacrata S Eutychia Amullia Primigenia Satria Pietas Claudia Ptolemais Terentia Athenais\n
EDCS-11400094.translation: On the 3rd Ides of April, in the 9th consulship of Emperor Vespasian Caesar Augustus and the 7th consulship of Titus Vespasian Caesar Augustus, son of Augustus. For their generosity, honors were decreed to those who honored the dendrophoroi, namely: Claudia Iusta, votary; Sia Faustina, votary; Eutychia; Amullia Primigenia; Satria Pietas; Claudia Ptolemais; Terentia Athenais.
EDCS-11400094.summary: A public dedication honoring women who supported the dendrophoroi (tree-bearers), likely a religious or civic group, during the consulships of Vespasian and his son Titus, in 79 CE.

EDCS-11400098.translation: To the departed spirits. Fabia Sperata and Alexander, Rhodians, made this for themselves.
EDCS-11400098.summary: This funerary inscription honors Fabia Sperata and Alexander and includes a Greek phrase indicating they made it for themselves, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11400099.translation: To the departed spirits. Of Thesei Marcellinus, slave of Vipsanius, who lived 17 years.
EDCS-11400099.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Thesei Marcellinus, a slave who died at age 17, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11400100.translation: To the departed spirits. Vagellia Marcellina lived 47 years. Cornelius Firmus made this for his well-deserving mother.
EDCS-11400100.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Cornelius Firmus for his mother, Vagellia Marcellina, who died at age 47, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11400104.translation: To Emperor Caesar Lucius Aurelius Verus Augustus Armeniacus, son of the deified Antoninus Pius, grandson of the deified Hadrian, great-grandson of the deified Trajan Parthicus, great-great-grandson of the deified Nerva, pontifex maximus, with tribunician power for the 3rd time, imperator for the 2nd time, consul for the 2nd time, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-11400104.summary: This is a dedication to Emperor Lucius Aurelius Verus, listing his titles and honors, including his third tribunician power and second consulship, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11400105.translation: Aticius, son of Titus, of the Pollia tribe, from Mutina, centurion of the 30th Legion Classica.
EDCS-11400105.summary: This is an epitaph for Aticius, a centurion of the 30th Legion Classica, who was from Mutina and belonged to the Pollia tribe, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11400106.translation: To Quintus Calvius Invictus, holding aedile power, and to Numerius Calvius Rufus, holding aedile power. Acerronia Selenium provided this at her own expense.
EDCS-11400106.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Acerronia Selenium at her own expense to Quintus Calvius Invictus and Numerius Calvius Rufus, both holding aedile power, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11400107.translation: To the departed spirits. Gaius Cornelius Troilus, four times magistrate with aedile power, four times magistrate with the power to declare law, quaestor of public funds and alimentary matters, lived 30 years and 5 months. Sestia Pontice made this for her most beloved son.
EDCS-11400107.summary: This funerary inscription is for Gaius Cornelius Troilus, who held several civic offices and lived 30 years and 5 months; it was set up by his mother, Sestia Pontice, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11400108.translation: To the departed spirits. Gaius Octavius Crescens, patron of the municipality, who discharged all offices, lived 80 years. His most pious wife made this for her well-deserving husband.
EDCS-11400108.summary: This funerary inscription honors Gaius Octavius Crescens, a patron of the municipality who had held all offices and lived to 80, and was set up by his devoted wife, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11400109.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. For Publius Vagellius Pusillio, son of Publius, an illustrious Roman knight, patron of the municipality. The heirs [made this].
EDCS-11400109.summary: This funerary inscription is for Publius Vagellius Pusillio, a Roman knight and municipal patron, and was set up by his heirs, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11400110.translation: [...] Iulius [...] was a magistrate with the power to declare law, a priest [...] the people [...]
EDCS-11400110.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription mentioning a magistrate with judicial power and a priest, possibly erected by the people, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11400111.translation: To the departed spirits. Felix lived 10 years; the guild of the cushion-bearers set this up for her as one well-deserving.
EDCS-11400111.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a woman named Felix, set up by her guild, the 'cannofori', possibly relating to the wool or textile trade, dated to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11400112.translation: To Quintionius, the steward. Philematium made this for herself and a fellow slave from her own funds.
EDCS-11400112.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Philematium, who set up her own tombstone and one for a fellow slave, indicating her status as a slave or freedwoman and her relationship with the steward Quintionius.

EDCS-11400113.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Alimma, who in her life maintained the highest discipline, lived 21 years, 4 months. Her most loving father and most dutiful fellow slave, with the owner's permission, set this up for her as one well-deserving.
EDCS-11400113.summary: This funerary inscription records the life and death of Alimma, who lived 21 years and 4 months and was noted for her discipline; it was erected by her father and a fellow slave.

EDCS-11400115.translation: To the departed spirits. Cantinia Hymnis.
EDCS-11400115.summary: A very brief funerary inscription identifying the deceased as Cantinia Hymnis.

EDCS-11400116.translation: To the departed spirits. Claudia Pritiba lived 27 years. Iucundinus made this for his well-deserving wife.
EDCS-11400116.summary: This funerary inscription records that Claudia Pritiba died at the age of 27 and was memorialized by her husband Iucundinus.

EDCS-11400117.translation: To the departed spirits. Ediste, nurse of her masters, lived 35 years, 3 months. Caerellius Felicio, husband, [set this up] for his most dutiful and perfectly disciplined wife, whose labor and [---] and experience [---]
EDCS-11400117.summary: This funerary inscription honors Ediste, a nurse who lived 35 years and 3 months, and was memorialized by her husband Caerellius Felicio for her devotion and discipline.

EDCS-11400119.translation: To the departed spirits. Octavia Tyche lived 16 years. Her children paid [for this] from their own means for their well-deserving daughter.
EDCS-11400119.summary: A funerary inscription for Octavia Tyche, who died at 16 years old, paid for by her children.

EDCS-11400120.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Lucius Ovius Minicius Flavianus lived 4 years, 7 months, 6 days. Father made this for his son.
EDCS-11400120.summary: This funerary inscription records the short life of Lucius Ovius Minicius Flavianus, who died at the age of 4 years, 7 months, and 6 days, and was memorialized by his father.

EDCS-11400122.translation: To the departed spirits. Publius Vagellius Laco lived 57 years, 6 months, 4 days. His son made this for his well-deserving father.
EDCS-11400122.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Publius Vagellius Laco at the age of 57 years, 6 months, and 4 days, memorialized by his son.

EDCS-11400123.translation: [For one] who had discharged all his duties, Gaius Octavianus Crescens [---]
EDCS-11400123.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription likely honoring Gaius Octavianus Crescens, who had fulfilled all his duties, possibly a public official or military figure.

EDCS-11400126.translation: Quintus Vibullius, son of Lucius, grandson of Quintus, and Gaius Cincius Paulus, son of Gaius, as quinquennial censors, had the statue of Proserpina repaired and set up, and the altars repaired, by decree of the Senate; they were magistrates. Helvia, daughter of Quintus, and Orbia, daughter of Marcus, were wives. [---]
EDCS-11400126.summary: This inscription records the repair and erection of a statue and altars in honor of Proserpina, carried out by two magistrates (quattuorviri) by senatorial decree, with their wives identified, likely dating to the early Imperial period.

EDCS-11400132.translation: To Gaius Abutius Murra, son of Gaius, a magistrate with the power of jurisdiction.
EDCS-11400132.summary: This is a dedicatory inscription for Gaius Abutius Murra, a magistrate, likely erected by himself or on his behalf, dating to the Republican or early Imperial period.

EDCS-11400134.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Gnaeus Julius Maturus, son of Gnaeus, a magistrate with curule aedile powers, quaestor of alimentary funds, lived 47 years. Pontilius Caedimnus to his friend.
EDCS-11400134.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Gnaeus Julius Maturus, who held several municipal offices and lived to be 47, dedicated by his friend Pontilius Caedimnus, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-11400136.translation: Quintus Laronius, son of Quintus, [augur], and Lucius Libertius, son of Gaius, chief priest, quinquennial magistrates with censorial powers, by decree of the Senate, it is established [---] HS [---]
EDCS-11400136.summary: This inscription records two high-ranking officials, an augur and a chief priest, serving as quinquennial magistrates with censorial powers, who acted by senatorial decree, likely from the late Republican or early Imperial period.

EDCS-11400138.translation: To Latia Au/leia Aurina, daughter of Publius, priestess of Augustus, [---] SE [---] V [---] G [---] D [---] G [---] X [---]
EDCS-11400138.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Latia Au/leia Aurina, a priestess of Augustus, with significant portions missing, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-11400139.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. To [---] Marcianus, [in] the capacity of prefect, [---] with censorial ornaments, [---] of 60 years, [---] P. [He/She] made [it].
EDCS-11400139.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for an individual named Marcianus, who held the rank of prefect and possibly possessed censorial ornaments, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-11400140.translation: To Quintus Muticilius Sex(tus) Deccianus, son of Quintus, of the Aemilia tribe, quinquennial magistrate with censorial power, quaestor of public funds, honored with the public horse, appointed to the decurionate by the deified Emperor Hadrian, and appointed to the decurionate by Emperor Antoninus Augustus Pius, patron of the municipality, for his love of country and generosity and his many merits, by consent of the people, on whose behalf for the dedication he gave HS VIII sesterces to the Augustales and HS VI sesterces to the people individually, HS IV sesterces. The site was granted at public expense by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-11400140.summary: This inscription honors Quintus Muticilius Sex. Deccianus, a prominent local official and patron of the municipality, detailing his career and his generous donations to the community and religious collegia, likely dating to the reign of Antoninus Pius.

EDCS-11400142.translation: To the departed spirits. To Satrius Ingenuus, son of Lucius, magistrate with aedile powers, lived 24 years. His father made [this] for his well-deserving son.
EDCS-11400142.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Satrius Ingenuus, who held the office of aedile, erected by his father, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-11400146.translation: Of Publius Olius Felix, son of Gnaeus.
EDCS-11400146.summary: This is a simple ownership or funerary inscription for Publius Olius Felix, son of Gnaeus, dating to the Roman period.

EDCS-11400147.translation: To Lucius Laberius Optatus, freedman of Lucius, honored with censorial ornaments, lived 22 years. To Clutoria Quartae, daughter of Lucius, lived 24 years. The mother [made this] for her daughter and son-in-law.
EDCS-11400147.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a freedman, Lucius Laberius Optatus, who received censorial honors, and his wife Clutoria Quartae, erected by the mother of the wife, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-11400148.translation: To Publius Lucius Gallus, Augustalis. Paquia Repentina, Mettia Auge [erected this].
EDCS-11400148.summary: This inscription, likely from a tomb, records the dedication by Paquia Repentina and Mettia Auge to Publius Lucius Gallus, an Augustalis, probably a freedman.

EDCS-11400150.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Ampliatus lived 30 years. His wife made this for him, a well-deserving husband.
EDCS-11400150.summary: This is a tombstone for Ampliatus, who lived 30 years, erected by his wife, indicating a date within the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11400151.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. To Athenaïs, her mother made this for her most beloved daughter.
EDCS-11400151.summary: This is a tombstone where a mother dedicated a monument to her daughter, Athenaïs, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11400152.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Lucius Atilius Parthenius [erected this].
EDCS-11400152.summary: This is a tombstone fragment likely for Lucius Atilius Parthenius, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11400153.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Atilia Hygia lived 35 years. Atilius Euhodus [made this] for his well-deserving wife.
EDCS-11400153.summary: This tombstone records the death of Atilia Hygia at age 35 and was erected by her husband Atilius Euhodus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11400154.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Marcus Aurelius Maximus, son of Marcus, lived 25 years. Aurelius Africanus lived 63 years. [This was erected] for a brother and a father.
EDCS-11400154.summary: This tombstone records the deaths of Marcus Aurelius Maximus (age 25) and Aurelius Africanus (age 63), likely erected by the latter for his brother and father, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11400155.translation: Marcus Caerellius Heraclida, freedman of Marcus.
EDCS-11400155.summary: This inscription likely names Marcus Caerellius Heraclida, a freedman, possibly on a tombstone or property marker, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11400156.translation: Caesia Secunda, from her will, for herself and her family, for Caesia Cila, daughter of Prima, her sister. Marcus Mamercius, son of Marcus. Quintus Caesius Salvivus, freedman of Quintus. Quintus Caesius Communis, freedman of Quintus. Quintus Caesius Respectus, freedman of Quintus. Quintus Caesius Hymenaeus.
EDCS-11400156.summary: This complex inscription details arrangements made in the will of Caesia Secunda, naming family members and freedmen, likely related to funerary arrangements or property, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11400157.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Cottia Felicula lived 57 years. Her daughter made this for her well-deserving mother.
EDCS-11400157.summary: This tombstone records the death of Cottia Felicula at age 57, erected by her daughter, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11400158.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Crato lived 35 years. [Erected by his] parents.
EDCS-11400158.summary: This tombstone records the death of Crato at age 35 and was erected by his parents, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11400159.translation: He lived 14 years, he was pious towards his own. Farewell.
EDCS-11400159.summary: A funerary epitaph for a boy who lived 14 years and was known for his piety.

EDCS-11400160.translation: Aemilia Fortunatus ordered this to be made according to his will.
EDCS-11400160.summary: A funerary dedication commissioned by Fortunatus in accordance with a will, likely for a member of the Aemilia family.

EDCS-11400161.translation: To the divine spirits of Quintus Instius Florinus.
EDCS-11400161.summary: A dedication to the underworld spirits for Quintus Instius Florinus.

EDCS-11400162.translation: To the divine spirits, for Julia Myrinae, from Raia Charis, her most excellent mother.
EDCS-11400162.summary: A funerary dedication from a mother to her deceased daughter, Julia Myrinae.

EDCS-11400163.translation: To the divine spirits. Sextus Manlius Lupus, son of Sextus, lived 7 years, 8 months, 10 days.
EDCS-11400163.summary: A funerary epitaph for Sextus Manlius Lupus, recording his lifespan of 7 years, 8 months, and 10 days.

EDCS-11400164.translation: Sacred to the divine spirits. Minicia Eutychia, daughter of Lucius, lived 75 years.
EDCS-11400164.summary: A funerary epitaph for Minicia Eutychia, recording her lifespan of 75 years.

EDCS-11400165.translation: Sacred to the divine spirits. Munatia Limene lived 35 years. Her son made this for his most devoted mother.
EDCS-11400165.summary: A funerary monument made by a son for his devoted mother, Munatia Limene, who lived 35 years.

EDCS-11400166.translation: Sacred to the divine spirits. Marcus Numisius Commodus lived 55 years. His son [made this] for his father.
EDCS-11400166.summary: A funerary dedication for Marcus Numisius Commodus, who lived 55 years, likely made by his son.

EDCS-11400167.translation: Sacred to the divine spirits. Titus Scaefius Dionysius lived 17 years. Pullius Dionysius [made this] for his most excellent son and for himself.
EDCS-11400167.summary: A funerary dedication by Pullius Dionysius for his son Titus Scaefius Dionysius, who died at 17, and for himself.

EDCS-11400169.translation: Alexander, freedman (?), made this from his own property for Gaius Segulius Tiflanus, son of Gaius, of the Camilia tribe, who deserved well of him. Also for Gaius Segulius Alexander. Mallia Zotiniu. This is a monument or tomb, he shall not inherit (?).
EDCS-11400169.summary: A funerary monument erected by a freedman for his patron Gaius Segulius Tiflanus, and also for others named Gaius Segulius, with a note about inheritance.

EDCS-11400170.translation: Dedicated to the departed spirits. Titiria Antiochis lived for 14 years, 4 months, and 9 days. Her mother made this for her daughter.
EDCS-11400170.summary: A funerary epitaph for a young girl, Titiria Antiochis, set up by her mother, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11400171.translation: Dedicated to the departed spirits. Trygetus lived for 22 years. His brother, the heir, made this for him, a deserving person.
EDCS-11400171.summary: A funerary epitaph for Trygetus, erected by his brother who was also his heir, probably from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11400172.translation: Dedicated to the departed spirits. Turillius Amiantus lived for 58 years. His wife made this for her deserving husband.
EDCS-11400172.summary: A funerary epitaph for Turillius Amiantus, created by his wife, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11400173.translation: Dedicated to the departed spirits. Turillia Quinta lived for 15 years, 6 months, and 20 days. Her father and husband made this for her, a deserving person.
EDCS-11400173.summary: A funerary epitaph for Turillia Quinta, set up by her father and husband, probably from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11400174.translation: Dedicated to the departed spirits. Lucius Vagellius Felix lived for 39 years. His wife made this for him, a deserving person.
EDCS-11400174.summary: A funerary epitaph for Lucius Vagellius Felix, erected by his wife, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11400175.translation: Titus Varius Albarius, Suallia Quinta's daughter Bedesia, Pullia Primigenia, freedwoman of Lucius, Lucius Pullius Secundus, freedman of Lucius, Lucius Pullius Hippotyrus, freedman of Lucius, Publius Varius Pisciniensis, Quintus Suallius Urbanus, freedman of Quintus, Pullia Charis, freedwoman of Lucius, made this monument or tomb for themselves and their kin; it will not pass to an heir.
EDCS-11400175.summary: A funerary monument inscription listing multiple individuals and family members, establishing ownership and inheritance exclusion, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11400176.summary: A very fragmentary inscription mentioning a name, Zmyrna, possibly a funerary or dedicatory text, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11400190.text_edition: \n Imperator Caesar Titus Aelius Hadrianus Antoninus Augustus Pius pontifex maximus tribunicia potestate VI consul III pater patriae imperator II Coloniae Minerviae Nerviae Augustae Scolacio aquam dat\n
EDCS-11400190.translation: Emperor Caesar Titus Aelius Hadrianus Antoninus Augustus Pius, Pontifex Maximus, holding tribunician power for the 6th time, Consul for the 3rd time, Father of the Country, Imperator for the 2nd time, grants water to the colony of Colonia Minervia Nervia Augusta Scolacium.
EDCS-11400190.summary: An imperial rescript from Antoninus Pius granting water to the colony of Scolacium, dating to his reign (138-161 AD).

EDCS-11400192.translation: Sacred to Hera Lachnia, for the health of Marciana, sister of the Emperor. Oecius, freedman, procurator.
EDCS-11400192.summary: A dedicatory inscription to the goddess Hera Lachnia, set up by a freedman and procurator for the health of the Emperor's sister, Marciana, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11400193.translation: To Futia Lolliana, daughter of Gaius, my most dutiful daughter. Gaius Fudius Onirus, twice aedile, also gave 10,000 sesterces from the decurions, so that from its interest, every year on the 7th of the Ides of April, celebrating the birthday of my daughter, you may feast and gather, and 400 sesterces for distributions, and you must not convert them to other uses. The place was given by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-11400193.summary: A funerary endowment inscription from a father for his deceased daughter, Futia Lolliana, specifying funds for annual celebrations and distributions, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11400194.translation: To Futia Lolliana, daughter of Gaius, most dutiful daughter. Gaius Futi[u]s Onirus has granted this space by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-11400194.summary: This is a funerary monument (likely a tombstone or a dedication of land for a tomb) from the Roman period, dedicated to Futia Lolliana by Gaius Futi[u]s Onirus, with the land granted by a local decree.

EDCS-11400195.translation: Septimia Prepusa gave to her daughter Futia Prepida, daughter of Gaius, and to her grandson Gaius Iulius Glago, son of Gaius, and to her most dutiful daughter, for the dedication of this statue, to the decurions and their children for each HS VIII nummi, to the Augustales and their children for each HS VI nummi, to the people man by man HS IIII nummi, to women HS II nummi. Gaius Iulius Anthus [...] and his family [...] erected [...]. The space was granted by decree of the decurions. Gaius Iulius [...] oversaw it.
EDCS-11400195.summary: This inscription records the distribution of money and benefits upon the dedication of a statue, with varying amounts given to different social classes and their families, indicating a civic or religious event in a Roman town.

EDCS-11400196.translation: To Lucius Lollius Marcianus, son of Lucius, grandson of Lucius, great-grandson of Lucius, of the Cornelia tribe, honored with the public equestrian rank, patron of the colony, who held all offices. Futia Longina, daughter of Gaius, his mother, gave a distribution to the decurions, the Augustales while feasting, and to the people man by man, for the dedication of his statue. The space was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-11400196.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Lucius Lollius Marcianus, a prominent citizen, by his mother Futia Longina, commemorating the dedication of his statue and including a distribution of food and/or money to various civic bodies.

EDCS-11400197.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Underworld. To Iulia Gramma, his incomparable wife. Sextus Iulius Primus erected this.
EDCS-11400197.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Iulia Gramma by her husband Sextus Iulius Primus, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-11400199.translation: To Manius Megonius Leon, son of Manius, grandson of Manius, great-grandson of Manius, of the Cornelia tribe, former aedile, former duovir by the Cornelia law, former quaestor of public funds, patron of the municipium, former quinquennial duovir. The decurions and Augustales, and the people, from bronze collected by contribution, for his merits.
EDCS-11400199.summary: This is a dedication from the Roman period honoring Manius Megonius Leon for his civic service and merits to the municipality, erected by the local council, Augustales, and populace.

EDCS-11400200.translation: To Manius Meconius Leon, of the Cornelia tribe, former aedile, former duovir by the Cornelia law, former quaestor of public funds, patron of the municipium. The Augustales, as patron, for his merits. The space was granted by decree of the decurions. From the will, I wish that in addition to this, HS X thousand nummi be given to the public treasury of the Petelinum people, and likewise the Caedician vineyard with a part of the Pompeian estate, as they are in their best and largest state within their own boundaries which were mine, I wish them to be bought with the interest from the semisses, HS X thousand nummi, for the equipment of the triclinia of our Augustales, which I have handed over to them during my lifetime, candelabra and two-wicked lamps, according to the judgment of the Augustales, so that they may more easily perform their public duties of hospitality, which I have considered to pertain to the utility of our public treasury, [making it] easier for those who undertake the burden of Augustaleship while they have this benefit before their eyes. Furthermore, I wish the interest from the times, semisses, HS X thousand nummi, to be for the equipment of the Augustales, according to their judgment, so that they may more easily preserve my perpetual gift, and I do not wish the interest, which they have thus received from the public treasury, to be transferred to other uses, unless it is necessary for the preparation of the vineyard. I also wish the vineyard with a part of the Pompeian estate, as I have said above, to be given to the Augustales of our town, this vineyard which is called Aminea, so that if you agree with my intention, by which I believe I have foreseen your needs, you may have wine for your uses, only when you publicly hold feasts. And by this means, relieved of expenses, those who are compelled to the office of Augustales will more easily come forward, being able to cultivate the rented part of the Pompeian vineyard. I wish these things to be done and ensured as I have arranged. In addition to this, I wish my heirs to provide and the public treasury of Petelinum to provide for the body of the Augustales, from my other estates, a sufficient yearly stake for the planting of the vineyard which I have bequeathed to the Augustales. And to you, Augustales, I ask that you ratify this will of mine and entrust it to your care to be observed in perpetual form, so that this my will concerning you may be more easily known to your body, the entire part of the place which pertains to your honor.
EDCS-11400200.summary: This extensive inscription from the Roman period is a posthumous dedication and testament by an Augustalis (a member of a college of priests or officials) of Petelinum, detailing bequests of money, land, and specific items (lamps, candelabra, wine) to the Augustales and the public treasury, intended to support their civic duties and feasting. It also records the granting of the land by local decree and provides detailed instructions for the management of the bequests, aiming to perpetuate his generosity and honor the Augustales.

EDCS-11400207.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Underworld. To Lucius Aurelius Stephanus, procurator in charge of the imperial couriers.
EDCS-11400207.summary: This is a funerary dedication from the Roman imperial period to Lucius Aurelius Stephanus, who held a significant administrative position related to the emperor's communication network.

EDCS-11400211.translation: To Gaius Marius Rufus, son of Publius, of the Aemilia tribe, duovir for dispensing justice in Copia, aged 21. Publius Marius Rufus, son of Publius, erected this for his son and himself, and for Marcus Dossennius Olsian, son of Marcus, brother, duovir for dispensing justice in Blanda, and for Iulia and Cincia Rufa, mother of them both.
EDCS-11400211.summary: This is a tombstone from the Roman period, erected by Publius Marius Rufus for his son Gaius, himself, and other family members, including his brother and mother, indicating multiple burials in the same plot.

EDCS-11400212.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Underworld. Marcus Annius Hilarus erected this for his most dutiful son Marcus Annius, who lived 17 years and 7 months; had fate allowed, this tombstone would have been erected for his father, deserving of good treatment. He erected this.
EDCS-11400212.summary: This is a funerary inscription from the Roman period, lamenting the early death of Marcus Annius, and suggesting that his father, Marcus Annius Hilarus, had planned to erect a tomb for himself that would have been passed on to his son.

EDCS-11400213.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Underworld. To Gnaeus Pompeius Sabinus, who lived 16 years, 6 months, and 19 days. Gnaeus Pompeius Sabinus and Aemilia Primilla erected this for their most dutiful son.
EDCS-11400213.summary: This is a funerary dedication from the Roman period to Gnaeus Pompeius Sabinus, who died at a young age, by his parents Gnaeus Pompeius Sabinus and Aemilia Primilla.

EDCS-11400217.translation: Sacred to Mefitis Utiana. Marcus Helvius Clarus Verulanus Priscus, son of Marcus, of the Pomptina tribe, six-time aedile, quaestor, quinquennial magistrate, priest of Rome and the deified Augustus, curator of the public affairs of the people of Potentia, dedicated at his own expense.
EDCS-11400217.summary: This is a public dedication by Marcus Helvius Clarus Verulanus Priscus, a prominent local official, to the goddess Mefitis Utiana, funded by himself.

EDCS-11400220.translation: Sacred to Venus Erycina. Oppia Restituta, freedwoman of Numerius, gave this gift during the consulship of Faustinus and Rufinus.
EDCS-11400220.summary: This is a private dedication to Venus Erycina by a freedwoman, likely made during the consulship of Faustinus and Rufinus.

EDCS-11400221.translation: To Atrius, son of Quintus, of the Horatia tribe, Sep[---]to, quaestor for the roads, tribune of the soldiers of the Second Legion Adjutrix, Pious and Faithful, who received military decorations in the Suebic War, likewise in the Sarmatic War: a mural crown, a vallary crown, two pure spears, two silver vexilla, a deputy tribune of the legions, quaestor with proconsular power of the province of Crete and Cyrene, tribune of the plebs, praetor, patron of the municipality; [the place was] given by decree of the decurions, by his son in his will.
EDCS-11400221.summary: A complex funerary and honorary inscription for Atrius, detailing his extensive military and political career, and honoring him as patron of the municipality, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-11400233.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Marcus Allius Felix lived for 5 years and 10 months. Allius Optatus and Iulia Lucretia (dedicated this) to their son.
EDCS-11400233.summary: This is a tombstone for Marcus Allius Felix, erected by his parents Allius Optatus and Iulia Lucretia.

EDCS-11400257.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Vitalia lived for 16 years. Her most dutiful mother erected this for her daughter.
EDCS-11400257.summary: This is a tombstone for Vitalia, erected by her mother.

EDCS-11400269.summary: This is a funerary dedication to a son named Constantius.

EDCS-11400274.translation: Felicissima the mother made this for her well-deserving daughter Felicia, who lived 30 years.
EDCS-11400274.summary: This is a tombstone erected by Felicissima for her daughter Felicia.

EDCS-11400288.translation: Pietas, comrade-in-arms of Secundus, the leader, gives as a gift, at her own expense, an arch and a lamp to Juno.
EDCS-11400288.summary: This is a dedication of a public amenity (an arch and lamp) to Juno by Pietas, a female associate of a military leader.

EDCS-11400293.translation: To Tiberius Caesar Augustus, son of the deified Augustus, consul, pontifex maximus, with tribunician power for the 17th time. By decree of the decurions, publicly.
EDCS-11400293.summary: This public dedication honors Emperor Tiberius and records his titles and the 17th year of his tribunician power.

EDCS-11400294.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Trajan Hadrian Augustus, son of the deified Trajan Parthicus, grandson of the deified Nerva, pontifex maximus, with tribunician power for the 3rd time, consul for the 3rd time. Lucius Aquilius Mamius, aedile, praetor, quinquennial duumvir, gave this gift in honor of his augurship.
EDCS-11400294.summary: This is a dedication by Lucius Aquilius Mamius to Emperor Hadrian, honoring his augurship and recording the emperor's titles and consulships.

EDCS-11400295.translation: To Furía Sabiniliana Tranquillina Augusta, wife of our lord. Dedicated publicly.
EDCS-11400295.summary: This is a public dedication to Furía Sabiniliana Tranquillina Augusta, the empress.

EDCS-11400300.translation: To the departed spirits. For Aelius Dignus, aide to the most eminent prefects of the praetorium, who lived 3 years, served 3 years. Iulia Vera[3]ia, his wife, made this for her well-deserving husband, with whom she lived for [3] years.
EDCS-11400300.summary: This is a tombstone for Aelius Dignus, a soldier who served as an aide to praetorian prefects, set up by his wife.

EDCS-11400301.translation: To the departed spirits. For Aelius Marcianus, a soldier of the VI Praetorian Cohort, the Pious Vindex, Gordiana Maxima, with 12 years of service. Valerius Valerianus, a evocatus, took care of the making of this.
EDCS-11400301.summary: This is a tombstone for Aelius Marcianus, a soldier with 12 years of service in the VI Praetorian Cohort, arranged by Valerius Valerianus.

EDCS-11400312.translation: To the departed spirits. For Gaius Stremponius Bassus, son of Gaius, of the Pomptina tribe, aedile, praetor twice, quinquennial magistrate, augur, curator of the public affairs of Potentini, curator of the Aquillian fund, quaestor of public affairs three times. His wife Helvia Psychario and his sons Gaius Stremponius Bassianus and Faustina made this for him as a well-deserving person.
EDCS-11400312.summary: This is a tombstone for Gaius Stremponius Bassus, a prominent local official, erected by his wife and sons.

EDCS-11400317.translation: For Publius Titius Viator, a priest of Hercules. Crescens, his freedman, took care of the making of this for himself and his comrade Allia Casta, as a well-deserving person.
EDCS-11400317.summary: This inscription records the construction of a monument for Publius Titius Viator and his comrade Allia Casta, arranged by his freedman.

EDCS-11400370.translation: Sacred to Aesculapius. Herculanius, agent, in fulfillment of a vow.
EDCS-11400370.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Aesculapius by Herculanius, an agent.

EDCS-11400371.translation: In the consulship of Emperor Lucius Aurelius [Commodus] and Quintillus. For the safety of Bruttia Crisppina. Idaeus, her agent, willingly, gladly, deservedly fulfilled the vow.
EDCS-11400371.summary: This is a votive inscription for the safety of Bruttia Crisppina, dedicated by her agent Idaeus during the consulship of Commodus and Quintillus.

EDCS-11400372.translation: For Emperor Severus Augustus. By public decree of the decurions, at public expense.
EDCS-11400372.summary: This inscription indicates a public monument erected in honor of Emperor Severus by local town councilors.

EDCS-11400373.translation: To Emperor Caesar Valerius Flavius Constantinus Pius Felix Augustus, devoted to his divine power and majesty.
EDCS-11400373.summary: This is an inscription honoring Emperor Constantine, expressing devotion to his divine authority.

EDCS-11400374.translation: To Emperor Marcus Galerius Maximianus Augustus. [3] erected at his own expense.
EDCS-11400374.summary: This inscription honors Emperor Galerius Maximianus and states it was erected at his own expense.

EDCS-11400379.translation: Ansia Tarvi, daughter Rufa, by decree of the decurions, took care of the making of the sacred grove, its wall, its boundary wall, and its gate at her own expense.
EDCS-11400379.summary: This inscription records Ansia Rufa, by decree of the local council, funding the construction of a sacred grove, wall, and gate.

EDCS-11400380.translation: Gaius Luxsilius [restored text] also [restored text] at the pool also [restored text] weapons
EDCS-11400380.summary: This fragmented inscription seems to record the name of Gaius Luxsilius in relation to a pool and weapons, possibly related to a military or athletic context, with much of the text missing.

EDCS-11400381.translation: Ansia Egloge and Ansia Urbana for themselves and for their dearest daughter Cyparena, aged 18.
EDCS-11400381.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Ansia Egloge and Ansia Urbana for their beloved daughter Cyparena, who died at the age of 18.

EDCS-11400382.translation: [restored text] and Aurelia Saturnina made this monument for their well-deserving foster father.
EDCS-11400382.summary: This inscription records that Aurelia Saturnina and another person erected a monument for their deserving foster father.

EDCS-11400383.translation: To the departed spirits. Bruttia Victoria for her husband Lucius Bruttio Victorino.
EDCS-11400383.summary: This is a funerary dedication set up by Bruttia Victoria for her husband, Lucius Bruttio Victorino.

EDCS-11400384.translation: Lucius Cincius Cominus, son of Lucius, for his father Lucius Cincius Como and his mother Anicia Fausta.
EDCS-11400384.summary: This inscription records Lucius Cincius Cominus honoring his parents, Lucius Cincius Como and Anicia Fausta.

EDCS-11400385.translation: Cornelia made this for Publius Pomponius.
EDCS-11400385.summary: This is a simple dedication by Cornelia for Publius Pomponius.

EDCS-11400386.translation: Father Donatus for his sweetest son Donatus, who was well-deserving and lived for three years [restored text].
EDCS-11400386.summary: This funerary epitaph was erected by a father named Donatus for his son of the same name, who died after three years of life.

EDCS-11400387.translation: To the departed spirits. Vergilia for her incomparable husband Eutichianus, with whom she lived for 40 years, a well-deserving man.
EDCS-11400387.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Vergilia for her husband Eutichianus, commemorating their 40 years of marriage.

EDCS-11400388.translation: [restored text]io for his father Marcus [restored text] who was [restored text]. Iulianus, his son, made this.
EDCS-11400388.summary: This fragmented inscription records that Iulianus erected a monument for his father Marcus, with significant portions of the text missing.

EDCS-11400389.translation: Herennia Iunia, freedwoman of Gnaeus, set this up for her husband Gaius Laturnius Rufus, son of Marcus, a well-deserving man.
EDCS-11400389.summary: This funerary inscription records Herennia Iunia setting up a monument for her deserving husband, Gaius Laturnius Rufus.

EDCS-11400390.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Gaius Luxilius Rufus made this for his well-deserving wife, Luxilia Lupula, freedwoman of Gaius, with whom he lived for 42 years.
EDCS-11400390.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by a husband for his wife.

EDCS-11400393.translation: Marcus Ovilonius Lucanus, son of Lucius. He lives. And Baia Quinta, daughter of Titus.
EDCS-11400393.summary: A funerary epitaph possibly commemorating a living couple, with the inscription suggesting one or both are alive.

EDCS-11400394.summary: A funerary epitaph for a woman named Ovilonia Quinta.

EDCS-11400395.translation: Rufinus and Marcella, parents, and their associate Crescens, made this for their incomparable daughter Primilla, well-deserving, who lived 20 years.
EDCS-11400395.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by parents and an associate for their daughter.

EDCS-11400397.translation: For good memory. Urbicus made this for his brother Quintianus.
EDCS-11400397.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by a brother for his deceased brother.

EDCS-11400398.summary: A fragmented inscription, likely a tombstone, identifying a man by his name and filiation.

EDCS-11400399.translation: Staia Castae, daughter of Sextus, lived 22 years. Her father and mother made this, most unfortunate.
EDCS-11400399.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by grieving parents for their daughter who died at age 22.

EDCS-11400400.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Sextus Staius Modestus made this for his well-deserving Staia Castae, daughter, most dutiful, and for Antonia Apolloniae, wife, most holy.
EDCS-11400400.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by a husband for his deceased daughter and wife.

EDCS-11400401.translation: Gaius Tegianensis Syneros and Helena for themselves and their family.
EDCS-11400401.summary: An epitaph indicating a burial plot or tomb intended for a couple and their household.

EDCS-11400402.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Tegeanensi Prima, who lived 34 years, 7 months, and 12 days. Marcus Tegeanensis Crescens made this for his sweetest wife, with whom he lived 20 years and 9 months, well-deserving.
EDCS-11400402.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by a husband for his deceased wife, detailing her age at death and the duration of their marriage.

EDCS-11400403.translation: To Trecida, slave of Publius Nanonius Nepos, lived 16 years.
EDCS-11400403.summary: A tombstone recording the age of a deceased slave.

EDCS-11400404.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Felix, her grandfather, made this for Victor, most sweet grandson.
EDCS-11400404.summary: A tombstone erected by a grandfather for his beloved grandson.

EDCS-11400411.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Aurelius Fanodorus made this for his brother Aurelius Aemon.
EDCS-11400411.summary: A tombstone erected by a brother for his deceased sibling.

EDCS-11400414.translation: To Heilotus Felicissimus, for his most sweet daughter Epidia, daughter of Reburrus, who lived three years, ten months, and twenty-one days.
EDCS-11400414.summary: A tombstone recording the very young age at death of a daughter.

EDCS-11400415.translation: To Aesculapius, Publius Latinus Lucanus, quaestor, aedile, duovir with judicial power, willingly paid his vow.
EDCS-11400415.summary: A votive inscription to Aesculapius by a local magistrate.

EDCS-11400416.translation: To Jupiter and the household gods, Publius Nanonius Diophantus of Augusta Atinas.
EDCS-11400416.summary: An inscription dedicating offerings to Jupiter and the Penates by an individual.

EDCS-11400418.translation: Aulus Antonius Horus built the temple to the Great Mother, and the portico which is in front of the temple, and the priest's cell, from his own money, from the ground up; he gave it as a gift. On its dedication, he gave cakes and mulsum to the decurions, the Augustales, and the people.
EDCS-11400418.summary: A dedication of a temple, portico, and priest's cell to the Great Mother, including details of the dedication feast, by a local magistrate.

EDCS-11400419.text_edition: \n Divo Pio Severo Augusto publice decreto decurionum\n
EDCS-11400419.translation: To the deified Pius Severus Augustus, by public decree of the decurions.
EDCS-11400419.summary: A decree by the town council to honor the deified Emperor Antoninus Pius.

EDCS-11400420.translation: To Publius Licinius Valerianus, most noble Caesar, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-11400420.summary: A decree by the town council honoring the Caesar Publius Licinius Valerianus.

EDCS-11400422.translation: Quintus Statius Gallus, son of Quintus, of the Voltinia tribe, twice military tribune, three times duovir; Melencia, daughter of Sextus, his wife, Posilla; Quintus Statius Gallus, son of Quintus, of the Voltinia tribe, son, praefectus fabrum, duovir.
EDCS-11400422.summary: A funerary monument honoring a family, detailing the political and military careers of the father and son.

EDCS-11400423.translation: To Aulus Antonius Pelagianus, son of Aulus, of the Pomptina tribe, four-time quinquennial magistrate, a Roman knight, most rare and most blameless; the decurions, Augustales, and the common people of Petelia, given a site by decree of the decurions, have dedicated this as curator of public affairs and patron.
EDCS-11400423.summary: This is a dedication by the community of Petelia to Aulus Antonius Pelagianus, honoring him for his civic service as curator and patron.

EDCS-11400424.translation: To the gods of the underworld. To Aulus Antonius Pelagianus, an incomparable father. Antonius Pelagianus and Pelagiane made this.
EDCS-11400424.summary: This is a tomb inscription set up by sons named Antonius Pelagianus and Pelagiane for their father, Aulus Antonius Pelagianus.

EDCS-11400425.translation: To the gods of the underworld. For Marcus Antonius Rufus. The college of Mercuriales made this.
EDCS-11400425.summary: This is a tomb inscription set up by the college of Mercuriales for Marcus Antonius Rufus.

EDCS-11400426.translation: Titus Helvius Sabinianus, acting as a rope-maker (?) and curator, made this for himself.
EDCS-11400426.summary: This is a tomb inscription for Titus Helvius Sabinianus, who made it for himself, possibly indicating his profession as a rope-maker and curator.

EDCS-11400427.translation: To the gods of the underworld. To Titus Helvius Varro, son of Titus, of the Pomptina tribe, a Roman knight, an excellent father. Titus Helvius Tertullus made this for him as deserving.
EDCS-11400427.summary: This is a tomb inscription set up by Titus Helvius Tertullus for his father, Titus Helvius Varro, honoring his memory and civic status.

EDCS-11400428.translation: Lucia Suettia, freedwoman of Marcus, a priestess.
EDCS-11400428.summary: This is a dedication by Lucia Suettia, a freedwoman and priestess, possibly to a deity or in memoriam.

EDCS-11400429.translation: To Marcus Traesius Faustus, son of Marcus, of the Pomptina tribe, senior, four-time quinquennial magistrate of the Potentini, curator of public affairs of the Bantinor, curator of public affairs of the Atinati, for his merits. The decurions, Augustales, and common people have seen to this, with Lucius Porcius Rufus contributing the bronze.
EDCS-11400429.summary: This is a dedication by the community and officials to Marcus Traesius Faustus, honoring his extensive service as a magistrate and curator for multiple communities.

EDCS-11400430.translation: To the gods of the underworld. To Antonia Ianuaria, dearest daughter, who lived 15 years, 3 months, and 6 days. Atinas Ianuarius and Antonia Prima, most unhappy parents, [made this].
EDCS-11400430.summary: This is a tomb inscription set up by parents for their deceased daughter, Antonia Ianuaria, specifying her age at death.

EDCS-11400431.translation: Antonia Modesta made this for her deserving husband, Publius Otacilius Campanus.
EDCS-11400431.summary: This is a tomb inscription set up by Antonia Modesta for her husband, Publius Otacilius Campanus, honoring his memory.

EDCS-11400432.translation: To the Divine Shades. To Julia Tucciena, incomparable wife, who lived 40 years, 10 months, 22 days. Athenodorus made this for [her], who deserved well.
EDCS-11400432.summary: A funerary inscription for Julia Tucciena, dedicated by her husband Athenodorus, likely from the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-11400433.translation: To the divine shades. To Quintus Caesius Semno, his father and patron, Quintus Caesius Castrensis, deserving well, [erected this].
EDCS-11400433.summary: A son dedicates this tombstone to his deserving father and patron, Quintus Caesius Semno.

EDCS-11400434.translation: To the divine shades. To Sextus Cellius Triphon, his deserving wife, Acilia Prima [erected this].
EDCS-11400434.summary: A wife, Acilia Prima, dedicates this tombstone to her deserving husband, Sextus Cellius Triphon.

EDCS-11400435.translation: To the divine shades. To Fabia Zosima, his deserving wife, Marcus Tattius Fructianus, her husband, took care to have [this made].
EDCS-11400435.summary: A husband, Marcus Tattius Fructianus, dedicates this tombstone to his deserving wife, Fabia Zosima.

EDCS-11400436.translation: To the divine shades. To Gabinia [---]
EDCS-11400436.summary: A fragmentary inscription dedicated to Gabinia.

EDCS-11400437.translation: To the divine shades. To Titus Helvius Comitas, son of Titus, from the Pomptina tribe, Titus Helvius Tertullus [erected this] to his most excellent father.
EDCS-11400437.summary: A son, Titus Helvius Tertullus, dedicates this tombstone to his excellent father, Titus Helvius Comitas.

EDCS-11400438.translation: May the gods and shades favour [you]. To Helvia Commoda, his dearest wife and most excellent guardian, Helvius Sabinianus made [this] deserving well.
EDCS-11400438.summary: Helvius Sabinianus dedicates this tombstone to his beloved wife and guardian, Helvia Commoda.

EDCS-11400439.text_edition: \n Otaciliae Doridi filiae dulcissimae quae vixit nnos VI menses VIII dies XXI Otacili Privatus et Apollonia parentes\n
EDCS-11400439.translation: To Otacilia Doridis, dearest daughter, who lived 6 years, 8 months, and 21 days. Otacilius Privatus and Apollonia, parents [erected this].
EDCS-11400439.summary: Parents Otacilius Privatus and Apollonia dedicate this tombstone to their daughter, Otacilia Doridis, who died at the age of 6.

EDCS-11400440.translation: To Hordionia Anna [---], [---]lia Demetria [---] to her mother.
EDCS-11400440.summary: A partially preserved inscription from a daughter to her mother, Hordionia Anna.

EDCS-11400441.translation: To the divine shades. To Licinianianus [---]
EDCS-11400441.summary: A fragmentary inscription dedicated to Licinianianus.

EDCS-11400442.translation: To the divine shades. To Luxsilia Statia, freedwoman of Chrusis. Luxsilia Olympias [erected this] to her deserving mother.
EDCS-11400442.summary: Luxsilia Olympias dedicates this tombstone to her deserving mother, Luxsilia Statia, a freedwoman.

EDCS-11400443.translation: To the spirits of the departed. To Magia Marciana, daughter of Marcus, Marcus Teltionius Iuvenalis made this for his incomparable wife.
EDCS-11400443.summary: This is a tombstone inscription dedicated to Magia Marciana by her husband, Marcus Teltionius Iuvenalis.

EDCS-11400445.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Minatius pater and Decidia Serena, his father and mother, made this for their dearest son, who lived for 13 years.
EDCS-11400445.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for a son who died at the age of 13, made by his parents.

EDCS-11400446.translation: To the spirits of the departed. The wicked father Acleitia made this for Peregrinus, his son, who lived for 18 years, deserving well.
EDCS-11400446.summary: This tombstone inscription records a son, Peregrinus, who died at 18, and is noted as being made by his father.

EDCS-11400447.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Luxilia Casta made this for her good son, Marcus Pompeius Constans, who lived for 30 years, 5 months, and 6 days.
EDCS-11400447.summary: This tombstone inscription records the death of Marcus Pompeius Constans, aged 30 years, 5 months, and 6 days, dedicated by his mother.

EDCS-11400448.summary: This is a funerary dedication to a son named Numerius Pontilius.

EDCS-11400449.translation: To the spirits of the departed. To Porcatius.
EDCS-11400449.summary: This is a funerary inscription, possibly to a person named Porcatius.

EDCS-11400450.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Antonius Felicianus, but the unhappiest husband, made this for his incomparable wife, with whom he lived for 35 years, 11 months, and 18 days.
EDCS-11400450.summary: This tombstone inscription records the death of a wife, dedicated by her husband who describes himself as 'unhappiest' after 35 years of marriage.

EDCS-11400451.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Marcus Tattius Fructianus and Tattia Prepusa made this for their well-deserving father, Marcus Tattius Fructianus, son of Marcus, of the tribe Pomptina.
EDCS-11400451.summary: This tombstone inscription is dedicated by children to their father, Marcus Tattius Fructianus.

EDCS-11400452.translation: To the spirits of the departed. [He] made this for Teltonia, his well-deserving concubine.
EDCS-11400452.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a concubine named Teltonia.

EDCS-11400453.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Tullia Septima made this for her well-deserving husband, Tullius Syrus.
EDCS-11400453.summary: This tombstone inscription records the death of Tullius Syrus, dedicated by his wife Tullia Septima.

EDCS-11400454.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Marcus Valerius Hilarus made this for his son Hilarus, who deserved well, who lived eighteen years. He made it for himself while alive.
EDCS-11400454.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by a father for his deceased son, and also for himself, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11400457.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Bruttius Castor made this for his brother Bruttius Vitalis, who deserved well, who lived 43 years, 8 months, and 21 days.
EDCS-11400457.summary: This funerary epitaph was erected by a brother for his deceased sibling, providing details of the deceased's lifespan, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11400458.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Quelia Capriola made this for her husband Gaius Quelius Priscus, who deserved well, with whom she lived 22 years, 3 months, and 15 days.
EDCS-11400458.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by a wife for her deceased husband, including the duration of their marriage, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11400459.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Amatistus and [Ia]nuaria made this for their son Ianuarius, who deserved well, who lived 28 years, [---] his [---] with his [---] his [---] his [---] his [---] his parents [---]
EDCS-11400459.summary: This incomplete funerary epitaph records the death of Ianuarius, and was set up by his parents Amatistus and Ianuaria, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11400460.translation: Pontilia Renata made this for her husband Aurelius Quintasius, who deserved well, who lived approximately 45 years and 4 months.
EDCS-11400460.summary: This funerary epitaph was erected by a wife for her husband, specifying his approximate age at death, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11400461.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Pullania Casta for Pompeius Stephano her husband and for herself.
EDCS-11400461.summary: This funerary epitaph records that Pullania Casta set up a monument for her deceased husband, Pompeius Stephano, and for herself, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11400463.translation: Gnaeus Flavius Priscus for the Genius of this place.
EDCS-11400463.summary: This inscription records a dedication made by Gnaeus Flavius Priscus to the Genius loci (spirit of the place), likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11400464.translation: Marcus Insteius Firmus, former four-man official (IIIIvir) and aedile, and four-man official with jurisdiction, and five-year quinquennial official, for his son Marcus Insteius Secundus, former four-man official with jurisdiction, a father of a most rare example, and for himself.
EDCS-11400464.summary: This is a complex funerary epitaph set up by a father for his son and himself, detailing the son's and the father's public offices in a Roman municipality, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11400465.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Decimus Haterius Priscus. His sons Priscus Amandus and Hateris Prisca had this made for their most devoted father, by their own will, for 1,500 sesterces, under the supervision of their excellent friend Viennius Severus.
EDCS-11400465.summary: This funerary epitaph records the purchase and erection of a monument for Decimus Haterius Priscus by his sons, detailing the cost and supervisor, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11400466.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. To Antonia Dorcada, daughter of Aulus, priestess of the Atinatium [tribe].
EDCS-11400466.summary: This funerary inscription honors Antonia Dorcada, a priestess of the Atinatium, and is likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11400467.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Arria Trais, his wife, and Insteius Candidus and Venusta, to Marcus Insteius Candidus, [having deserved] well.
EDCS-11400467.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated to Marcus Insteius Candidus by his wife and children, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11400468.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. To Marcus Insteius Iucundus. His wife Daphne made [this] for him who deserved well; he lived 40 years.
EDCS-11400468.summary: This funerary inscription records the life of Marcus Insteius Iucundus, who died at the age of 40, and was set up by his wife.

EDCS-11400469.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. To Pontius Faustus, dearest son. Pontius and Gavia, parents, made [this] for him who lived 13 years, a tragic death.
EDCS-11400469.summary: This funerary inscription commemorates Pontius Faustus, who died at the age of 13, and was erected by his parents.

EDCS-11400470.translation: To Quintilla, dearest tent-mate. Marcus Insteius Eserninus arranged for the burial.
EDCS-11400470.summary: This funerary inscription is for Quintilla, a 'contubernalis' (tent-mate or spouse), and arranged by Marcus Insteius Eserninus.

EDCS-11400471.translation: To Sextus Caesius Rufus, son of Publius, of the Pomptina tribe, [who lived] 10 years. Publius Caesius Priscus, son of Sextus, of the Pomptina tribe, and Pomponia Polla, daughter of Caius, for their dearest son and for themselves.
EDCS-11400471.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Sextus Caesius Rufus at age 10 and was erected by his parents, also for their own future use.

EDCS-11400473.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Marcus Insteius Nympheros, with permission, restored [this monument] to Nympherotes and Natalis, deserving parents.
EDCS-11400473.summary: This inscription indicates Marcus Insteius Nympheros restored a monument to his parents, Nympherotes and Natalis, likely during the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11400474.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Marcus Insteius Callistus, father, and Caudia Firmilla, mother, made [this] for their most dutiful and deserving son, Marcus Insteius Firminus, who lived 16 years, 9 months, and 16 days.
EDCS-11400474.summary: This funerary inscription honors Marcus Insteius Firminus, detailing his age at death (16 years, 9 months, 16 days), and was erected by his parents.

EDCS-11400475.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. To Marcus Manilius Fortunatus, dearest son, tribune, patron of the college, filled with all duty. He lived 21 years, 5 months. Fortunatus and Mon[---]nilla, parents.
EDCS-11400475.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Marcus Manilius Fortunatus at age 21, who held the titles of tribune and patron of a college, and was erected by his parents.

EDCS-11400476.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Manilia Autronia Urbica for her well-deserving father, Marcus Manilius Primus, son of Marcus, Roman knight of the Palatina tribe.
EDCS-11400476.summary: This funerary inscription honors Marcus Manilius Primus, a Roman knight, and was erected by his daughter Manilia Autronia Urbica.

EDCS-11400477.translation: To the departed spirits. Pierus and Silvina made this for their most dutiful daughter, Manilia Pieris, daughter of Marcus.
EDCS-11400477.summary: A funerary dedication by parents for their daughter.

EDCS-11400478.translation: To the departed spirits. Lucius Otacilius Silvanus made this for his most cherished and incomparable wife, Otacilia Nomia, deserving of all good things.
EDCS-11400478.summary: A funerary dedication by a husband for his wife, likely from the early imperial period.

EDCS-11400479.translation: To the departed spirits. Probus made this for his deserving fellow slave, Critonita, slave of Gavi Rufus, who lived 21 years.
EDCS-11400479.summary: A funerary dedication by a fellow slave for Critonita, a slave of Gavi Rufus.

EDCS-11400480.translation: To the departed spirits. Digitia Prisca made this for her husband Flavius Hila, deserving of all good things, with his children. He lived approximately 70 years, 7 months, and 10 days.
EDCS-11400480.summary: A funerary dedication by a wife for her husband and children, including details of his lifespan.

EDCS-11400481.translation: To the departed spirits. His wife Anthis and his son Pelorus placed this for Pelorus, son of Marcus Gavi Severus, a slave, who lived 75 years. Here he lies.
EDCS-11400481.summary: A funerary dedication by a wife and son for Pelorus, a slave.

EDCS-11400482.translation: Marcus Plotius Nico, freedman of Marcus.
EDCS-11400482.summary: A simple funerary inscription or dedication.

EDCS-11400483.translation: Caius Bovianus Celer, son of Caius, of the Pomptina tribe,edile and quinquennial magistrate with judicial power, had this constructed according to the formula of the will of Iulia Celerina, his wife.
EDCS-11400483.summary: A public building or monument commissioned by a magistrate according to his wife's will.

EDCS-11400485.translation: Porcatii Lucina, Marcianus, and Proculus made this for their father, Lucius Porcatius Faustinus, son of Lucius, a quinquennial magistrate with judicial power, deserving of all good things, who lived 45 years.
EDCS-11400485.summary: A funerary dedication by children for their father, a magistrate.

EDCS-11400486.translation: Caius Statius Primus the younger made this for his daughter, Statia Amanda, deserving of all good things, who lived 7 years, 7 months, and 15 days, his incomparable and most sweet daughter.
EDCS-11400486.summary: A funerary dedication by a father for his young daughter.

EDCS-11400488.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Augustus, son of the divine one, chief pontiff, consul for the 13th time, with tribunician power for the 21st time, father of the fatherland.
EDCS-11400488.summary: A dedication to Emperor Augustus, listing his titles and honors, likely from the late 1st century BC or early 1st century AD.

EDCS-11400489.translation: Agrippa Julius, son of Augustus, grandson of the divine [Augustus] Caesar.
EDCS-11400489.summary: This is a funerary inscription or monument identifying Agrippa, son of Augustus.

EDCS-11400490.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Valerius Licinianus Licinius, Pious, Fortunate, Unconquered Augustus, devoted Vulceian forces.
EDCS-11400490.summary: This is a dedication to Emperor Licinius, likely set up by military units or followers of the cult of Vulcianus.

EDCS-11400491.text_edition: \n I pretio VAE fundus Gentianus fundus Siccitianus fundus Cagatianus ffundi Silecia[ni ------\n
EDCS-11400491.translation: In price: the Gentianus farm, the Siccitianus farm, the Cagatianus farm, the Silecianus farm, [------]
EDCS-11400491.summary: This inscription appears to be a record of land ownership or sale, listing several named farms and their prices.

EDCS-11400493.translation: [To Titus Statilius Taurus, son of Titus, augur, consul for the second time, imperator for the third time, chief curio.
EDCS-11400493.summary: This is a dedication or epitaph for Titus Statilius Taurus, listing his distinguished public offices, likely from the late Republican or early Imperial period.

EDCS-11400494.translation: To Coelius Anicetus, soldier of the 2nd Praetorian Cohort, a select soldier of the tribune. For the hope of his advancement, the most sacred order of decurions freely offered him the honor of a position among the decurions. He lived 24 years, 5 months, 2 days. Coelia Prima, his most beloved mother, and Nymphicus Volceianorum, the treasurer, made this for him and for themselves.
EDCS-11400494.summary: This is a funerary monument for Coelius Anicetus, a praetorian soldier, honoring his potential advancement and commemorating his life and death.

EDCS-11400495.translation: Gaius Dexius, son of Gaius, Publius Villius, son of Publius, Marcus Accius, son of Marcus, the four magistrates with judicial authority, acting by decree of the Senate and from public funds and from a collection which the townsmen and inhabitants contributed of their own free will, undertook its construction and approved it.
EDCS-11400495.summary: This is a public works inscription recording the construction of a project by four magistrates, funded by both public money and voluntary contributions from the citizens.

EDCS-11400496.translation: To Lucius Haedinius Rufus, son of Lucius, quinquennial for the second time, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-11400496.summary: This is a dedication or epitaph for Lucius Haedinius Rufus, who held the office of quinquennial magistrate twice, honoring him by a decree of the local council.

EDCS-11400497.translation: To Gaius Mettius Rufinus, son of Marcus, four-magistrate, quinquennial, flamen of the divine Vespasian, prefect of the artificers, curator of the public affairs of the Volceiani. Gaius Mettius Aper, son of Gaius, to his most excellent father.
EDCS-11400497.summary: This is a funerary monument for Gaius Mettius Rufinus, listing his various public and religious offices, with a dedication from his son.

EDCS-11400498.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. To Publius Menius Volcanus, son of Publius, flamen. He lived 56 years, 10 months, 3 days. Manilia Amatista, his wife, made this for him who deserved well.
EDCS-11400498.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Publius Menius Volcanus, a flamen, detailing his age and erected by his wife.

EDCS-11400499.translation: From the will of Otacilius Gallus, his father. Having restored the Caesareum, which had collapsed from age, with his own money. At the dedication of this work, he gave to the decurions 30,000 sesterces, to the Augustales 20,000 sesterces, to the villagers 12,000 sesterces, to the wives of the decurions 16,000 sesterces, to the Augustales 8,000 sesterces, to the villagers 4,000 sesterces.
EDCS-11400499.summary: This inscription records the restoration of a public building (Caesareum) by Otacilius Gallus and details the significant sums of money he donated to various social groups upon its dedication.

EDCS-11400500.translation: To Publius Otacilius Rufus, son of Lucius, of the Palatine tribe, father, twice four-man official with power of jurisdiction, five-year official, perpetual priest of the deified Hadrian, honored by him with public equestrian rank, curator of the treasury of the municipality of Aeclanum, elected by the deified Pius, patron of the municipality. For his exceptional munificence, the council of decurions decreed that this monument should be erected at public expense. On the occasion of its dedication, he gave 3 denarii to the decurions, 2 denarii to the Augustales, and 1 denarius to the people.
EDCS-11400500.summary: This is a funerary and honorific monument erected by the decurions of Aeclanum for Publius Otacilius Rufus, a prominent local magistrate and official, due to his generosity.

EDCS-11400501.translation: To Quintus Poppaedius Cato, son of Quintus, of the Sergia tribe, quaestor, five-year official, [erected by] his freedmen.
EDCS-11400501.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by freedmen for their former patron, Quintus Poppaedius Cato, who held local magistracies.

EDCS-11400502.translation: To [....]ioni Sev[....], citizen of [....]o, in honor of his four-man magistracy; deceased, who lived 33 years. Ofilia Rufilla to her most devoted husband, erected this; she lived with him 5 years.
EDCS-11400502.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Ofilia Rufilla for her husband, who died at age 33 after 5 years of marriage, honoring his previous magistracy.

EDCS-11400503.translation: To Gaius Bruttius Dionysius, son of Dionysius, most beloved. He lived 9 years, 11 months, and 16 days. Erected by his father, Dionysius.
EDCS-11400503.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by a father, Dionysius, for his young son, Gaius Bruttius Dionysius, who died at the age of nine.

EDCS-11400504.translation: To the departed spirits. To Bruttia Helicenis, his incomparable wife. Erected by Dionysius, the manager.
EDCS-11400504.summary: This is a funerary monument dedicated to the departed spirits for Bruttia Helicenis, set up by Dionysius, likely her husband or manager.

EDCS-11400505.translation: To the departed spirits. To Ianuaria, the well-deserving wife. Quintianus, the manager, erected this.
EDCS-11400505.summary: This is a funerary monument dedicated to the departed spirits for Ianuaria, a deserving wife, erected by Quintianus, likely her husband or manager.

EDCS-11400506.translation: To Ianuarius, conductor, freedman of Gaius Titius Rufus Reccianus, who lived 36 years. Casinia Tallusa erected this for his merits, to her dearest comrade.
EDCS-11400506.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Casinia Tallusa for Ianuarius, a conductor and freedman, possibly her partner or close associate.

EDCS-11400507.translation: To the departed spirits. To Successus, his dearest son. Dexter Figelianus erected this.
EDCS-11400507.summary: This is a funerary monument dedicated to the departed spirits for Successus, erected by his father, Dexter Figelianus.

EDCS-11400508.translation: To Allidia Statuta, daughter of Gaius, [mother].
EDCS-11400508.summary: This is a funerary monument for Allidia Statuta, daughter of Gaius, erected by her child.

EDCS-11400509.translation: To the departed spirits. To Clementila, his well-deserving fellow slave. Comicus set this up.
EDCS-11400509.summary: This is a funerary monument dedicated to the departed spirits for Clementila, erected by her fellow slave Comicus.

EDCS-11400510.translation: To the departed spirits. Epictesidis lived 10 years and 24 days. Epictetus and Neme[sis], parents, [made this for their] most beloved daughter.
EDCS-11400510.summary: A funerary epitaph for a young girl named Epictesidis, set up by her parents, Epictetus and Nemesis.

EDCS-11400511.translation: To the departed spirits. For Fortunata, who lived 25 years and was [in] marriage for 7 years, whose youth and good character, grieving the EXA/[3]IIRMANIENSESV / [3]IANEIAI[3]A / [3]ate fe[3] / [3]III, [her husband] made [this monument] for his [wife].
EDCS-11400511.summary: A funerary epitaph for a woman named Fortunata, detailing her age at death and years of marriage, set up by her grieving husband.

EDCS-11400512.translation: For Iuventia Saturia, who lived 12 years. Iuventia Rufina, [her mother], made [this for her] most beloved daughter.
EDCS-11400512.summary: A funerary epitaph for a young girl named Iuventia Saturia, set up by her mother, Iuventia Rufina.

EDCS-11400513.translation: Martialis lived 28 years. Martialis and Restitu[t]a, parents, [made this].
EDCS-11400513.summary: A funerary epitaph for Martialis, set up by his parents, Martialis and Restituta.

EDCS-11400514.translation: For Postumius Silvanus. Postumia Maxima, with whom he lived 28 years, [made this].
EDCS-11400514.summary: A funerary epitaph for Postumius Silvanus, set up by Postumia Maxima, indicating their shared life of 28 years.

EDCS-11400515.translation: For Vintia Saturnia, daughter of Marcus. Marcus Vintius Acceptus, [her] freedman, [made this].
EDCS-11400515.summary: An inscription for Vintia Saturnia, daughter of Marcus, set up by her freedman, Marcus Vintius Acceptus.

EDCS-11400519.translation: For Publius Equitius Primanus, freedman of Publius, Augustalis of Potentia. Publius Equitius Primanus [made this for his] deserving father.
EDCS-11400519.summary: A funerary epitaph for Publius Equitius Primanus, a freedman and Augustalis, set up by his son of the same name.

EDCS-11400521.translation: Equitia Melpomene made this monument for Publius Equitius Pionius, freedman of Publius, her most beloved husband, and for herself and descendants.
EDCS-11400521.summary: A funerary monument set up by Equitia Melpomene for her husband, Publius Equitius Pionius, and for herself and their descendants.

EDCS-11400522.translation: To the departed spirits. For Quintus Maecilius Augustalis. Maecilia Secunda, mother, made [this for her deserving son] who lived 35 years. // To the departed spirits. For Maecilia Secunda.
EDCS-11400522.summary: A funerary epitaph for Quintus Maecilius Augustalis, set up by his mother, who also has a separate dedication to him, indicating his death at 35.

EDCS-11400523.translation: Publius Minatius Secundus, son of Publius, is buried here.
EDCS-11400523.summary: A simple burial inscription for Publius Minatius Secundus, son of Publius.

EDCS-11400524.translation: Gaius Octavius Marcion, lived 22 years, and Gaius Octavius Severus, lived 40 years and 9 months. Gaius Octavius Severus, father.
EDCS-11400524.summary: This epitaph records the ages at death of two individuals, likely father and son, and the paternal relationship.

EDCS-11400525.translation: Tattia Marcellus, lived 75 years. Tattia Hesperis made this monument for her well-deserving relative.
EDCS-11400525.summary: This epitaph records the age at death of Tattia Marcellus and that Tattia Hesperis erected a monument for her.

EDCS-11400526.translation: To the divine spirits. Marcus Utianus Onesimus made this for his well-deserving wife, Ulpia Sperata.
