EDCS-11400526.summary: This epitaph records that Marcus Utianus Onesimus erected a monument for his wife, Ulpia Sperata, as a dedication to the departed.

EDCS-11400527.translation: Quintus Volutius Ampliatus placed this for his well-deserving wife, Volutia Primigenia.
EDCS-11400527.summary: This epitaph records that Quintus Volutius Ampliatus placed a monument for his wife, Volutia Primigenia.

EDCS-11400529.translation: Fadia Felicula made this for her well-deserving husband, Fadius Dexter, at a cost of 15,000 sesterces, for which work the college of dendrophoroi contributed [---].
EDCS-11400529.summary: This epitaph records a funerary monument erected by Fadia Felicula for her husband Fadius Dexter, including its cost and a contribution from the college of dendrophoroi.

EDCS-11400531.translation: Sacred to the divine spirits. Prima, his wife, made this for her well-deserving husband, Martius.
EDCS-11400531.summary: This epitaph records that Prima made a monument for her husband, Martius, as a dedication to the departed.

EDCS-11400532.translation: Romulus made this for his well-deserving father, Aelius [---], an Augustalis.
EDCS-11400532.summary: This epitaph records that Romulus erected a monument for his father, Aelius [---], who held the position of Augustalis.

EDCS-11400533.translation: Grumentina, with her son, made this for her well-deserving patroness, Allia Danais.
EDCS-11400533.summary: This epitaph records that Grumentina and her son erected a monument for their patroness, Allia Danais, as a dedication to the departed.

EDCS-11400535.translation: The place was granted by decree of the decurions to Titus Flavius Silvanus, son of Titus, son of Fabius, patron of the Eburini, twice duumvir, quinquennalis, quaestor of the grain dole, curator of the grain dole. The college of dendrophoroi, because of his exceptional benevolence towards them and perpetual hope, erected a statue most worthy of a patron, in whose honor he, content, offered 8,000 sesterces to the aforementioned college, so that every year on his birthday, the Ides of December, it should be celebrated with attendance, and for the dedication of the statue, 20 sesterces to each patron of the college, and 20 sesterces to each quinquennalis, duumvir, and aedile, and 17.5 sesterces to each of the other decurions, and 12 sesterces to each Augustalis, and 1000 sesterces to each of the colleges of dendrophoroi and of artisans, and [---] sesterces to each plebeian for a banquet and the distribution of sacrificial meat. Dedicated the 5th day before the Kalends of April in the year of the duumvirs Caius Stlaccius [---] and Gnaeus Brinnius Steianus. To the prefect and master, the shining Flavius Delmatius, vir perfectissimus, corrector of the province of Lucania.
EDCS-11400535.summary: This extensive inscription records the granting of a burial place and the erection of a statue for Titus Flavius Silvanus, a municipal patron and official, by the college of dendrophoroi, detailing financial contributions and ongoing commemorative obligations, and is dedicated to Flavius Delmatius, corrector of Lucania.

EDCS-11400536.translation: Numerius Ahius Successus, Augustalis of Nuceria, for Marcia Meroe, his wife, and himself, with whom he lived 53 years.
EDCS-11400536.summary: This epitaph records the ages at death of Numerius Ahius Successus and Marcia Meroe, his wife, and the duration of their marriage.

EDCS-11400539.translation: Of the son of ... years 3. For Sallustius ... man.
EDCS-11400539.summary: This is a funerary inscription, likely for a child, naming Sallustius.

EDCS-11400540.translation: For Cominia Damianeti, who lived 21 years and 50 days, and for Cominia Olympias, his wife, Bivius Ampliatus made this in comparison to no one.
EDCS-11400540.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated by Bivius Ampliatus to his wife Cominia Olympias and another woman, Cominia Damianeti, likely a relative.

EDCS-11400542.translation: In God the Lord and the Holy Spirit. For Julian, holy bishop, who lived 50 years, 3 months, and 2 days. Felicianus made this for his well-deserving wife Julian and for his well-deserving children. Julian, in peace.
EDCS-11400542.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Bishop Julian, dedicated by his wife Felicianus and children.

EDCS-11400543.translation: For Augusta Iulia, daughter of Drusus, granddaughter of the deified Augustus.
EDCS-11400543.summary: This is a dedication to Iulia Augusta, daughter of Drusus and granddaughter of Emperor Augustus.

EDCS-11400544.translation: For Germanicus Caesar, son of Tiberius Augustus, grandson of the deified Augustus, great-grandson of the deified Julius, Augustus, consul for the second time, imperator for the second time.
EDCS-11400544.summary: This is a dedication to Germanicus Caesar, highlighting his imperial lineage and titles.

EDCS-11400545.translation: To the departed spirits. For Lucius Sempronius Priscus, son of Lucius, of the Pomptina tribe, who lived 25 years and 7 months. If cruel fate had not struck before the day, father and mother should have been buried before you.
EDCS-11400545.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lucius Sempronius Priscus, who died young, with a lament from his parents.

EDCS-11400546.translation: To the departed spirits. For Gaius Sextilius Oppius, quinquennial duovir, who lived 50 years. Claudia Potita made this for her most cherished husband.
EDCS-11400546.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Gaius Sextilius Oppius, a quinquennial duovir, dedicated by his wife Claudia Potita.

EDCS-11400552.translation: Brittius Praesens, a most distinguished man, the corrector, oversaw this.
EDCS-11400552.summary: This inscription records that Brittius Praesens, identified as a corrector (a governor or official), oversaw a project.

EDCS-11400553.translation: To the departed spirits. For Arrius Isidorus, the freedman. Silvanus made this for his well-deserving father, who lived 75 years, 6 months, and 8 days.
EDCS-11400553.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Arrius Isidorus, a freedman, dedicated by his son Silvanus.

EDCS-11400554.translation: To the departed spirits. For Flavia Commendata, who lived 60 years. Gnaeus Voluntilius Successus and Marcus Allienus Hedylus made this for their well-deserving wife.
EDCS-11400554.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Flavia Commendata, dedicated by her husband Gnaeus Voluntilius Successus and Marcus Allienus Hedylus.

EDCS-11400555.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Caius Julius Socrates made this for Caius Julius Saturninus, who deserved well.
EDCS-11400555.summary: A funerary dedication by a son to his father, Caius Julius Saturninus, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-11400556.translation: Caius Petronius Optatus, magistrate of the Mentis Bona cult, dedicated a statue, a base, and a reading desk.
EDCS-11400556.summary: A dedication of religious objects by a magistrate of a specific cult, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-11400560.translation: In the consulship of Flavius Felicianus and Fabius Titianus, on the day before the Kalends of May, the duoviri of the colony of Paestum, Antonius Allus and Oppius Silvester, made pronouncements. After the numerous decurions had attended in the Caesarean curia, they made speeches. We have long since, by our decree, offered the honor of patronage to Aurelius Gentianus, a most accomplished man, and promised a bronze tablet to follow. Therefore, it is best, most sacred fellow decurions, that we adhere to our pledge. Wherefore, the tablet of patronage is to be offered to the same Aurelius Gentianus, a most accomplished man. When he deigns to accept it, we hope that he will favour us and our fatherland in all things. It has been decreed by the order: it is approved, it is approved that we fulfill our pledge so that we offer the tablet of patronage, inscribed on bronze, to Aurelius Gentianus, a most accomplished man, which we believe he will gladly accept and favour us and our fatherland in all things.
EDCS-11400560.summary: A decree by the duoviri and decurions of Paestum granting honorary citizenship (patronage) to Aurelius Gentianus, likely in the late 3rd or early 4th century CE, as indicated by the consular dating.

EDCS-11400561.translation: In the consulship of Vulcatius Rufinus and Flavius Eusebius, on the Kalends of August, the duoviri of the colony of Paestum, Tullius Septimus and Digitius Antonius, made pronouncements. After the numerous decurions had attended in the Caesarean curia, they made speeches. We have long since, by our decree, offered the honor of patronage to Aquilius Nestorius and promised a bronze tablet to follow. Therefore, it is best, most sacred fellow decurions, that we adhere to our pledge. Wherefore, the tablet of patronage is to be offered to the same Aquilius Nestorius. When he deigns to accept it, we hope that he will favour us and our fatherland in all things. It has been decreed by the order: it is approved, it is approved that we fulfill our pledge so that we offer the tablet of patronage, inscribed on bronze, to Aquilius Nestorius, which we believe he will gladly accept and favour us.
EDCS-11400561.summary: A decree by the duoviri and decurions of Paestum granting honorary citizenship (patronage) to Aquilius Nestorius, likely in the late 3rd or early 4th century CE, as indicated by the consular dating.

EDCS-11400562.translation: To Helpidius, a fortunate man. May the god protect you. In the consulship of Flavius Leontius and Bonosus, on the sixth day before the Ides of April, when the numerous citizens of the colony of Paestum had assembled, they made pronouncements. We estimate that the state of the citizenry is made higher and more cultivated from no other source than that it is supported by the diligence of men. Therefore, most excellent citizens, let us offer patronage to Helpidius, a most honorable man, according to his dignity. We believe that he will deign to favour us and our fatherland in all things. To Helpidius. It is approved, it is approved, to offer the tablet of patronage to Helpidius, a most honorable man, whose great equity, tranquility, dignity, justice, innocence, and humanity are shown to be inherited from his lineage, and whose descendants are most holy and the glory and ornament of him. If he deigns to accept it, we hope that for the honor of his name, he will regard and favour us in all things with an equal and sincere spirit.
EDCS-11400562.summary: A decree by the citizens of Paestum granting honorary citizenship (patronage) to Helpidius, likely in the late 3rd or early 4th century CE, citing his virtues and lineage.

EDCS-11400563.translation: To Quintus Ceppius Longinus, son of Quintus (of the voting tribe Mae(cia)), pontiff (?), and designated duovir; he lived 20 years. To Quintus Ceppius Callimachus, his father, and Aviania, his mother.
EDCS-11400563.summary: A funerary epitaph for Quintus Ceppius Longinus, who died at age 20, also mentioning his parents. The presence of consular and senatorial titles suggests an Imperial date, possibly late Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-11400564.translation: Publius Claudius, son of Caius, and Caius Sexstilius, son of Lucius, duovirs, by decree of the senate.
EDCS-11400564.summary: An official dedication or record made by the two duovirs of a Roman colony, likely during the Republican or early Imperial period, referencing a senatorial decree.

EDCS-11400565.translation: To Quintus Numonius Valas, son of Caius, our patron.
EDCS-11400565.summary: An inscription dedicating something to a patron, Quintus Numonius Valas, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-11400567.translation: Marcus Tullius Cicero, son of Marcus, of the voting tribe Maecia, Roman equestrian, Laurens Lavinas, patron of the colony, dedicated this to his wife, Digitia Rufina, daughter of Lucius, for her exceptional chastity and modesty, spending from his own funds, with public expense remitted. The site was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-11400567.summary: A funerary monument erected by a prominent local official and Roman equestrian for his wife, Digitia Rufina, highlighting her virtues, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-11400568.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Rufus, son of [---] Vinicius, of the voting tribe Mae(cia), duovir, quinquennalis, patron of the colony. A father for his son, which the son ought to have done for his father.
EDCS-11400568.summary: A funerary dedication by a father for his son, Rufus, who held significant magistracies in the colony, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-11400569.translation: Publius Avianius, freedman of Publius, as magistrate of the Augustales, a Mercurialis.
EDCS-11400569.summary: This inscription records a freedman named Publius Avianius, who held the position of magistrate within the college of Augustales and was associated with the cult of Mercury.

EDCS-11400570.translation: To the departed shades. Primus, treasurer of the guild, to his wife Bennia Ephesia.
EDCS-11400570.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Primus, a guild treasurer, to his deceased wife Bennia Ephesia.

EDCS-11400571.translation: Marcus Caedius Nicephor, freedman of Marcus, a merchant; and Donnia Secunda, freedwoman of Marcus Aulus, his wife.
EDCS-11400571.summary: This inscription likely commemorates a married couple, Marcus Caedius Nicephor, a merchant, and his wife Donnia Secunda, both freedpersons.

EDCS-11400573.translation: To the departed shades. Iulius Iusinus Eu­frosinus made this for his most beloved wife Aurelia Olympias, a most chaste woman, who lived 33 years, 5 months, 26 days.
EDCS-11400573.summary: This is a funerary monument dedicated by Iulius Iusinus Eu­frosinus to his wife Aurelia Olympias, detailing her age at death and praising her virtue.

EDCS-11400574.translation: [Son?] of Caius. Caius Camurtio Apro, who lived 21 years.
EDCS-11400574.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Caius Camurtio Apro, who died at the age of 21.

EDCS-11400575.translation: To the departed shades. Eutychia, his wife, for Quintus Ceppius Optatus, well-deserving.
EDCS-11400575.summary: This funerary inscription is a dedication by Eutychia to her husband Quintus Ceppius Optatus.

EDCS-11400577.translation: To the departed shades. Dicitia Cemella made this for her husband Marcus Nanneius Quetianus, who lived 50 years, 3 months, 10 days, 3 hours; well-deserving.
EDCS-11400577.summary: This funerary monument was erected by Dicitia Cemella for her husband Marcus Nanneius Quetianus, specifying his age and lifespan details.

EDCS-11400578.translation: To Caius Petronius Bassus, son of Caius, of the Maecia tribe, his best friend. Digitius Praeses [made this].
EDCS-11400578.summary: This inscription is a dedication from Digitius Praeses to his esteemed friend Caius Petronius Bassus.

EDCS-11400579.translation: To the departed shades. Primigenius for his companion Quintilia, who lived 17 years, 7 months, well-deserving.
EDCS-11400579.summary: This funerary dedication was made by Primigenius for his female companion Quintilia, who died at the age of 17 years and 7 months.

EDCS-11400580.translation: To the departed shades. Modes­tus and Pri­miti­bus, sons, made this for their mother Salystia Fortunata, who lived 55 years, well-deserving.
EDCS-11400580.summary: This funerary inscription records Modes­tus and Pri­miti­bus dedicating a monument to their mother Salystia Fortunata, who lived 55 years.

EDCS-11400582.translation: To the departed spirits. Parents made this for their dearest Beneria, who lived for one year, a deserving daughter.
EDCS-11400582.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a child named Beneria, set up by her parents.

EDCS-11400583.translation: To the departed spirits. Optata made this for her most pious and most sacred husband, Succesus the baker, who lived for 60 years, 6 months, and 16 days, a deserving man.
EDCS-11400583.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Succesus, a baker, dedicated by his wife Optata.

EDCS-11400584.translation: To the departed spirits. Vinnius Amiantus and Lucia Herria, parents, made this for their sweetest daughter, Vinnia Amianis, who lived for 27 years and 12 days, a deserving daughter.
EDCS-11400584.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Vinnia Amianis, set up by her parents.

EDCS-11500484.translation: Gnaeus Cornelius Papia, freedman of Gnaeus, and Lucius Galonius Agathocles, freedman of Lucius, as magistrates, had this made at their own expense for the Bona Mens (Good Spirit).
EDCS-11500484.summary: This inscription records the erection of a monument to the spirit of Bona Mens by two magistrates.

EDCS-11600045.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription mentioning Quintus Herennius.

EDCS-11600046.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription mentioning Marcus Tressius Bassus.

EDCS-11600055.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, likely a dedication or ownership marker, mentioning Aufidius Fronto.

EDCS-12100881.inscription_type: diplomata militaria, tituli operum, tituli sacri
EDCS-12100881.text_edition: \n Ante diem VII Idus Februarias Appio Annio Atilio Bradua Tito Vibio Varo consulibus ex gregale Caio Iulio Seuthi filio Bitho Philippopolitano ex Thracia et Marciae Actiae Secundae uxori eius Italicae et Longino filio eius et Bitho filio eius et Iuliae filiae eius et Bendi filiae eius descriptum et recognitum ex tabula aerea quae fixa est Romae in muro post templum divi Augusti ad Minervam Marci Servili Getae Luci Pulli Chresimi Marci Sentili Iasi Tiberi Iuli Felicis Cai Belli Urbani Publi Graecini Crescentis Publi Ocili Prisci\n
EDCS-12100881.translation: On the seventh day before the Ides of February, in the consulship of Appius Annius Atilius Bradua and Titus Vibius Varus. Recorded and confirmed from a bronze tablet fixed to the wall in Rome, behind the Temple of the Divine Augustus, near the Minervam, belonging to Marcus Servilius Geta, Lucius Pullius Chresimus, Marcus Sentilius Iasius, Tiberius Julius Felix, Gaius Bellius Urbanus, Publius Graecinius Crescens, Publius Ocilius Priscus. From a legionary soldier, Gaius Julius Seuthius, son of Seuthius, a Bithynian from Philippopolis in Thrace, and his wife Marcia Actia Secunda, an Italian, and their son Longinus, and their son Bithus, and their daughter Julia, and their daughter Bendi.
EDCS-12100881.summary: This is a legal document, likely a record of property or citizenship, concerning a soldier and his family, attested by several witnesses in Rome.

EDCS-12300299.inscription_type: diplomata militaria, tituli operum, tituli sacri
EDCS-12300299.text_edition: \n Imperator Caesar divi Hadriani filius divi Traiani Parthici nepos divi Nervae pronepos Titus Aelius Hadrianus Antoninus Augustus Pius pontifex maximus tribunicia potestate XI imperator II consul IIII pater patriae nomina militum qui in praetorio meo militaverunt in cohortibus decem I II III IV V VI VII VIII IX X item urbanis quattuor X XI XII XIV subieci quibus fortiter et pie militia functis ius tribuo conubii dumtaxat cum singulis et primis uxoribus ut etiam si peregrini iuris feminas matrimonio suo iunxerint proinde liberos tollant ac si ex duobus civibus Romanis natos pridie Kalendas Martias Lucio Salvio Iuliano Caio Bellicio Torquato consulibus cohortis II praetoriae Caio Licinio Cai filio Menenia Probo Nuceria descriptum et recognitum ex tabula aerea quae fixa est Romae in muro post templum divi Augusti ad Minervam Imperator Caesar divi Hadriani filius divi Traiani Parthici nepos divi Nervae pronepos Titus Aelius Hadrianus Antoninus Augustus Pius pontifex maximus tribunicia potestate XI imperator II consul IIII pater patriae nomina militum qui in praetorio meo militaverunt in cohortibus decem I II III IV V VI VII VIII IX X item urbanis quattuor X XI XII XIV subieci quibus fortiter et pie militia functis ius tribuo conubii dumtaxat cum singulis et primis uxoribus ut etiam si peregrini iuris feminas matrimonio suo iunxerint proinde liberos tollant ac si ex duobus civibus Romanis natos pridie Kalendas Martias Iuliano et Torquato consulibus cohortis II praetoriae Caio Licinio Cai filio Menenia Probo Nuceria Luci Digiti Valentis Publi Aeli Alexandri Cai Equiti Rufini Cai Iuli Celeris Luci Fescennae Prisci Marci Ascani Domestici Luci Antoni Saturnini\n
EDCS-12300299.translation: On the day before the Kalends of March, in the consulship of Lucius Salvius Julianus and Gaius Bellicius Torquatus. The Emperor Caesar Titus Aelius Hadrianus Antoninus Augustus Pius, son of the Divine Hadrian, grandson of the Divine Trajan Parthicus, great-grandson of the Divine Nerva, Pontifex Maximus, holding tribunician power for the 11th time, Imperator for the 2nd time, Consul for the 4th time, Father of the Fatherland. I have listed below the names of the soldiers who served in my praetorian guard in the ten cohorts I, II, III, IV, V, VI, VII, VIII, IX, X, and also in the four urban cohorts X, XI, XII, XIV. To whom, having served their military duty bravely and piously, I grant the right of marriage, but only with one woman each, so that even if they marry women of peregrine status, they may have children in the same way as if born from two Roman citizens. Recorded and confirmed from a bronze tablet fixed to the wall in Rome, behind the Temple of the Divine Augustus, near the Minervam. The Emperor Caesar Titus Aelius Hadrianus Antoninus Augustus Pius, son of the Divine Hadrian, grandson of the Divine Trajan Parthicus, great-grandson of the Divine Nerva, Pontifex Maximus, holding tribunician power for the 11th time, Imperator for the 2nd time, Consul for the 4th time, Father of the Fatherland. I have listed below the names of the soldiers who served in my praetorian guard in the ten cohorts I, II, III, IV, V, VI, VII, VIII, IX, X, and also in the four urban cohorts X, XI, XII, XIV. To whom, having served their military duty bravely and piously, I grant the right of marriage, but only with one woman each, so that even if they marry women of peregrine status, they may have children in the same way as if born from two Roman citizens. On the day before the Kalends of March, in the consulship of Julianus and Torquatus. For Gaius Licinius Probus, son of Gaius, of the Menenia tribe, from Nuceria, of the 2nd Praetorian cohort; also for Lucius Digitus Valens, Publius Aelius Alexander, Gaius Equitius Rufus, Gaius Julius Celer, Lucius Fescennius Priscus, Marcus Ascanius Domesticius, Lucius Antonius Saturninus.
EDCS-12300299.summary: This is an imperial rescript issued by Emperor Antoninus Pius granting the right of legal marriage and legitimate offspring to soldiers of the praetorian guard, recorded on a bronze tablet.

EDCS-12800370.text_edition: \n Divae Paulinae Augustae Cai Iuli Veri Maximini Pii Felicis Imperatoris Augusti uxori Cai Iuli Veri Maximi matri nobilissimi Caesaris decreto decurionum pecunia publica\n
EDCS-12800370.translation: To the Divine Paulina Augusta, wife of Gaius Julius Verus Maximinus Pius Felix Augustus, and mother of the most noble Caesar. By decree of the decurions, at public expense.
EDCS-12800370.summary: This is a dedication to Empress Paulina Augusta, wife of the emperor Maximinus Thrax, erected by local authorities.

EDCS-13900340.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Flavia Alexandria, dearest wife, who lived 30 years. Titus Riarius Marcellinus, a special cavalryman, made this for a deserving woman.
EDCS-13900340.summary: A funerary epitaph for Flavia Alexandria, set up by her husband, Titus Riarius Marcellinus, who was a special cavalryman.

EDCS-15100127.inscription_type: senatus consulta, tituli operum, tituli sacri
EDCS-15100127.translation: Quintus Marcius, son of Lucius, and Spurius Postumius, son of Lucius, consuls, addressed the Senate on the Ides of October at the temple of Duelona. As scribes were Marcus Claudius, son of Marcus, Lucius Valerius, son of Publius, and Quintus Minucius, son of Caius. Concerning the Bacchanals, who were associated by federal law, they decreed thus: that none of them should wish to hold a Bacchanal; if there were any who believed it necessary for themselves to hold a Bacchanal, they were to come to Rome to the urban praetor, and about these matters, after their case had been heard, our Senate should decree, provided that at least 100 senators were present when the matter was considered. No citizen of Rome, nor of Latin name, nor any ally should approach for this, unless they had approached the urban praetor, and he, by decree of the Senate, provided that at least 100 senators were present when the matter was considered, had permitted them. They decreed that there should be no male priest, nor any magistrate, neither male nor female; nor should any of them possess money in common, nor should any male or female hold office or act in place of a magistrate. Nor thereafter should they conspire together, or swear together, or promise together, or make agreements together, nor should any of them give pledges to each other. No one should perform rites on a festival day, neither in public nor in private, nor outside the city, unless they had approached the urban praetor, and he, by decree of the Senate, provided that at least 100 senators were present when the matter was considered, had permitted them. No one should perform rites with more than five men and three women gathered together, unless by permission of the urban praetor and the Senate, as written above. That you announce these things in the assembly, so that you may know the Senate's decree, not less than three nundines. Their decree was thus: if there were any who acted contrary to what is written above, they decreed that their property should be confiscated, and that this should be inscribed on a bronze tablet, thus the Senate decreed, and that you order it to be fixed where it can be most easily seen, and that those Bacchanals, if any exist outside the city, or if anything sacred is there, be removed within 10 days from the day the tablets are given to you, in the territory of Teurania.
EDCS-15100127.summary: A senatorial decree, inscribed on a bronze tablet, regulating and restricting the practice of Bacchanalian rites, likely dating to the late 2nd century BCE, based on its archaic Latin and the mention of the urban praetor and Senate's authority.

EDCS-16000290.text_edition: \n Marco Tullio Primigenio Benneiani sic Laurentis Lavinatis liberto Augustali homini probissimo summa rudi suo studiosi iubenes sic ob plurima ac maxima beneficia eius in se conlata locus datus decreto decurionum Dedicata sextum Kalendas Apriles Imperatore Philippo Persico et Titiano consulibus curantibus Lucio Digitio Luci Celado\n
EDCS-16000290.translation: To Marcus Tullius Primigenius, freedman of Benneianus, Augustalis of Laurentum Lavinas, a most excellent man, of great learning. A place was granted by decree of the decurions, in honor of his many and great benefits conferred upon them. Dedicated on the sixth day before the Kalends of April, in the consulship of Emperor Philip Persicus and Titianus, under the care of Lucius Digitius Luci Celadus.
EDCS-16000290.summary: An honorary inscription granting a public space to Marcus Tullius Primigenius, a freedman and Augustalis, in recognition of his benefactions to the community, dated to the consulship of Philip Persicus and Titianus (likely in the 3rd century CE).

EDCS-16000291.text_edition: \n Marcus Tullius Venneianus IIvir quinquennalis patronus coloniae balneas nobas sic a solo sua pecunia extruxit et dedecavit sic Marcus Tullius Cicero Venneianus filius balneas easdem vi ignis multifaria corruptas sua pecunia restituit curantibus Tulliis Primigenio et Nedymo et contutoribus eorum et incolumes ad usum civium rei publicae tradidit\n
EDCS-16000291.translation: Marcus Tullius Venneianus, twice duovir for five years, patron of the colony, built the new baths from his own funds and dedicated them. His son, Marcus Tullius Cicero Venneianus, restored the same baths, which had been greatly damaged by fire, with his own funds, under the care of Tullius Primigenius and Nedymus and their assistants, and handed them over unharmed for the use of the citizens and the state.
EDCS-16000291.summary: An inscription detailing the construction of new public baths by Marcus Tullius Venneianus and their subsequent restoration by his son, Marcus Tullius Cicero Venneianus, highlighting their generosity to the colony.

EDCS-16201155.text_edition: \n LB SE COMT Severo et Victorino consulibus officina Commodiana caesura Iuli Gayri sub cura GRES Aug Ger tor Iulii Gayri OPH et Epictet\n
EDCS-16201155.translation: Workshop of Commodus, under the supervision of Iulius Gayrus, overseer of the Caesarean division. With Severus and Victorinus as consuls. Ger. Tor. of Iulius Gayrus. OPH and Epictetus.
EDCS-16201155.summary: An inscription mentioning a workshop, possibly related to imperial administration or production, active during the consulship of Severus and Victorinus (likely late 2nd or 3rd century CE), with named supervisors.

EDCS-16300246.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Lesbius Cornelius Sita IIIIvir aedilicia potestate IIIIvir iure dicundo quinquennalis perpetuus vixit nnos XXXII dies XVII parentes filio pientissimo\n
EDCS-16300246.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Lesbius Cornelius Sita, formerly a quadrumvir with aedilician power, quadrumvir for dispensing justice, perpetual quinquennial, lived 32 years and 17 days. For his most dutiful son.
EDCS-16300246.summary: A funerary epitaph for Lesbius Cornelius Sita, who held several significant magistracies in his community, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-16300403.text_edition: \n Loco II bracchi II COM I Severo et Victorino conssulibus caesura Modi Anacreontis subsub Iuli Quadrati\n
EDCS-16300403.translation: Second place, two sections, under the consulship of Severus and Victorinus, workshop of Modi Anacreontis, under the supervision of Iulius Quadratus.
EDCS-16300403.summary: An inscription indicating a location ('second place, two sections') and a date during the consulship of Severus and Victorinus (likely late 2nd or 3rd century CE), mentioning a workshop and a supervisor.

EDCS-16400336.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication by Caius Flavius Corinthus, likely for himself, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-16400337.summary: This inscription is a funerary dedication by Quintus Ambivius Firmus, likely for himself, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-17100222.text_edition: \n Manio Megonio Mani filio Mani nepoti Mani pronepoti Cornelia Leoni aedili IIIIviro lege Cornelia quaestori pecuniae publicae patrono municipii IIIIviro quinquennali decuriones Augustales populusque ex aere conlato ob merita eius Kaput ex testamento rei publicae municipium meorum si mihi statua pedestris in foro superiore solea lapidea basi marmorea ad exemplum basis quam mihi Augustales posuerunt prope eam quam mihi municipes posuerunt posita fuerit HS Ccentum milia nummum quae eis me vivo pollicitus sum dari volo ea autem condicione HS Ccentum milia nummum quae supra scripta sunt dari volo ut ex usuris semissibus eius pecuniae omnibus annis die natalis mei qui est X Kalendas Apriles distributio fiat decurionibus epulantibus |(denariorum) CCC deducto ex his sumptu strationis reliqui inter eos qui praesentes ea hora erunt dividantur item Augustalibus eadem condicione |(denarios) CL dari volo et municipibus Petelinis utriusque sexus ex more loci |(denarios) I omnibus annis dari volo item in cena parentalicia |(denarios) L et hoc amplius sumptum hostiae prout locatio publica fuerit dari volo a vobis optimi municipes peto et rogo per salutem sacratissimi principis Antonini Augusti Pii liberorumque eius hanc voluntatem meam et dispositionem ratam perpetuamque habeatis totumque hoc caput testamenti mei basi statuae pedestris quam supra a vos sic petiv<i=T> mihi ponatis inscribendum curetis quo notius posteris quoque nostris esse possit vel eis quoque qui munifici erga patriam suam erint admoniat sic \n
EDCS-17100222.translation: For Manius Megonius, son of Manius, grandson of Manius, great-grandson of Manius, by Cornelia Leona. Aedile twice, quaestor of public funds, patron of the municipality, quinquennial duovir, the decurions, the Augustales, and the people, from a joint contribution of bronze, for his merits. The head, from his will, I wish to be given to the municipality of my people, if a standing statue on a stone base with a marble plinth, in the upper forum, shall be placed according to the example of the base which the Augustales placed for me, near the one which the townsfolk placed for me. One hundred thousand sesterces, which I promised them during my lifetime, I wish to be given. However, on the condition that the one hundred thousand sesterces written above are given, so that from the interest at half a year's rate, each year on my birthday, which is the 10th day before the Kalends of April, a distribution shall be made to the decurions feasting, 300 denarii, after deducting the cost of maintenance; the remainder is to be divided among those who are present at that hour. Likewise, I wish 150 denarii to be given to the Augustales on the same condition, and to the townsfolk of Petelia, of both sexes, according to local custom, I wish 1 denarius to be given each year. Likewise, for the ancestral feast, 50 denarii and, in addition, the cost of sacrifices, as the public contract requires. I ask and beg you, best townsfolk, by the safety of the most sacred Prince Antoninus Augustus Pius and his children, that you may hold this my will and disposition valid and perpetual, and that you see to inscribing this whole clause of my will on the base of the standing statue which you shall place for me above, as I have requested, so that it may be known to our descendants and may also admonish those who are generous towards their fatherland.
EDCS-17100222.summary: This is a detailed will of Manius Megonius, a prominent local official, outlining the conditions for a statue, financial distributions for feasts and ceremonies, and his desire to be remembered by his community, dating to the reign of Antoninus Pius (AD 138-161).

EDCS-17600371.translation: To the Emperors Caesar Marcus Aurelius Valerius Diocletianus Pius Felix Invictus Augustus, and Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Valerius Maximianus Pius Felix Invictus Augustus, and Flavius Valerius Constantius, and Galerius Valerius Maximianus, the most noble Caesars.
EDCS-17600371.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the four rulers of the Tetrarchy (Diocletian, Maximian, Constantius, and Galerius), dating to their joint reign, likely between AD 293 and 305.

EDCS-17700814.translation: To our Lords, Constantine Maximus and Licinius Augusti, and to the most blessed Caesars, born for the good of the state. To our Lords, Magnus Maximus and Flavius Victor Augusti, born for the good of the state.
EDCS-17700814.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the emperors and Caesars of the early 4th century, initially mentioning Constantine and Licinius, with a later alteration or addition for Magnus Maximus and Flavius Victor, reflecting political changes.

EDCS-19800061.translation: Ofonia Primigenia lived 60 years; made by herself while alive. Tureius Salvius lived 114 years.
EDCS-19800061.summary: This inscription records the ages at death of Ofonia Primigenia and Tureius Salvius, with Ofonia having pre-deceased her monument's construction, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-20401457.translation: Sacred to the shades of the departed. Vibia Heuresis made this for her deserving husband, Titus Bathilius Metrobius, who lived 37 years.
EDCS-20401457.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated by Vibia Heuresis to her husband, Titus Bathilius Metrobius, recording his age at death, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-21800408.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Marcus Antoninus Gordianus Pius Felix Augustus, pontifex maximus, holding tribunician power for the 5th time, consul for the 2nd time, father of the fatherland, proconsul. He restored the road which extends from Nuceria to Salernum, completely ruined by prolonged neglect, by his foresight and by restoring the ordinary tax for its protection. To Claudius Iulianus Pius Felix semper Augustus, born for the good of the state.
EDCS-21800408.summary: This inscription records Emperor Gordian III's restoration of the road from Nuceria to Salernum, detailing his titles and dating to his reign (AD 238-244), with a dedication to Claudius Iulianus.

EDCS-21800409.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Valerius Maxentius Pius Felix Invictus and perpetual always Augustus, 6 Roman miles. Born for the good of the state.
EDCS-21800409.summary: This inscription commemorates a road improvement project, likely a milestone, attributing it to Emperor Maxentius and dating to his reign (AD 306-312).

EDCS-22500819.translation: Of the Caesars, Caius and Lucius.
EDCS-22500819.summary: This inscription is a brief dedication or reference to the Caesars Gaius and Lucius Caesar (sons of Marcus Aurelius), likely from the late 2nd century AD.

EDCS-22500825.translation: Of Gaius, son of Lucius, Caesar.
EDCS-22500825.summary: This inscription is a fragmentary dedication or ownership mark, likely referring to a person named Caesar, son of Lucius.

EDCS-22500842.translation: Quintus Laronius, consul, imperator, for the second time.
EDCS-22500842.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription recording the titles and repeated consulship of Quintus Laronius.

EDCS-23400023.text_edition: \n Have Megonia Euhodis vixit nnos XXVI sit tibi terra levis\n
EDCS-23400023.translation: Have Megonia Euhodis lived 26 years. May the earth lie lightly upon you.
EDCS-23400023.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Megonia Euhodis, who died at the age of 26, including a standard epitaphic wish.

EDCS-23400026.translation: Occius is buried here, Festus of the Mani lineage.
EDCS-23400026.summary: This is a tombstone inscription identifying the deceased as Occius, with a reference to his lineage through Festus.

EDCS-23400028.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Crescens and Ianuaria, freedmen, [dedicated this] to Publius Campuleius Blastus, Augustalis.
EDCS-23400028.summary: This is a funerary dedication by freedmen to their patron, Publius Campuleius Blastus, who held the position of Augustalis.

EDCS-23400034.translation: Titus Vettius, son of Quintus, of the Sergia tribe, architect, arranged for the colonnade to be built at public expense during the consulship of Aulus Hirtius and Gaius Vibius.
EDCS-23400034.summary: This is an architectural inscription detailing that Titus Vettius, an architect, oversaw the construction of a colonnade using public funds during the consulship of 69 BCE.

EDCS-23400036.translation: [...], son of Quintus, of the Pomptina tribe, Gallus, previously priest of the divine [...], rebuilt the temple of Jupiter at his own expense.
EDCS-23400036.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription recording that Gallus, son of Quintus, a priest, rebuilt the temple of Jupiter using his own money.

EDCS-23400038.translation: ... for [her] deserving husband Lucia, dearest wife, with whom he lived 20 years.
EDCS-23400038.summary: A fragment of a funerary inscription dedicated to a wife named Lucia by her husband, indicating they lived together for 20 years, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-23400043.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Antonius Gemellus [dedicated this] to his sweetest and most dutiful mother, Antonia Secunda.
EDCS-23400043.summary: This is a funerary inscription from a son, Antonius Gemellus, to his beloved mother, Antonia Secunda.

EDCS-23400044.translation: Hippolytus and Ursula made [this] for Modesta, their foster-child and well-deserving one, who lived 4 years, 5 months, and 10 days.
EDCS-23400044.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Modesta, a foster-child, with her life span and the names of her dedicators, possibly her guardians.

EDCS-23400045.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Puteolana, the mother, made [this] for her well-deserving daughter Picena, who lived 18 years.
EDCS-23400045.summary: This is a funerary inscription from a mother, Puteolana, to her daughter Picena, who died at the age of 18.

EDCS-23400046.translation: Gaius Albius Festinus, on account of the office of bisellius.
EDCS-23400046.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Gaius Albius Festinus concerning the honor of a bisellius, a type of seat.

EDCS-23400047.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Publius Allius Magnillianus lived for 32 years and three months. Publius Allius Annius, aedile and IIIIvir, and Nucerina, his wife, set this up for their well-deserving son and for themselves while alive.
EDCS-23400047.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Publius Allius Magnillianus, set up by his father and stepmother, dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-23400048.translation: To Lucius Haedinius Sanius Marcellus, son of Lucius, of the Pomptina tribe, aedile, IIIIvir for dispensing justice, second quaestor for the alimenta. Marcus Vaonius Haedinius Sanius Lucanus and Vaonia Sania Marcella set this up for their most devoted grandfather.
EDCS-23400048.summary: This funerary monument honors Lucius Haedinius Sanius Marcellus, detailing his various public offices, and was erected by his grandsons.

EDCS-23400049.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Lucius Bruttiius Hirpinianus, by the guild of dendrophoroi.
EDCS-23400049.summary: This funerary inscription records the dedication to Lucius Bruttiius Hirpinianus by his guild of tree-bearers.

EDCS-23400050.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Marcus Casinius Firmus, by the guild of dendrophoroi.
EDCS-23400050.summary: This funerary inscription records the dedication to Marcus Casinius Firmus by his guild of tree-bearers.

EDCS-23400051.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Andria Aucta, by the Geniales sodales.
EDCS-23400051.summary: This funerary inscription records the dedication to Andria Aucta by the Geniales association.

EDCS-23400052.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Herennia Successa. Herennia Syntaxis, her mother, and Curti(a)e Myrinene, her mother-in-law, set this up.
EDCS-23400052.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Herennia Successa, set up by her mother and mother-in-law.

EDCS-23400053.translation: For Marcus Isteius Dorophorus, by the sodales.
EDCS-23400053.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Marcus Isteius Dorophorus by his associates.

EDCS-23400054.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Iulia Felicula, by her colleagues.
EDCS-23400054.summary: This funerary inscription records a dedication to Iulia Felicula by her colleagues.

EDCS-23400055.summary: This inscription appears to be a dedication or memorial to Gaius Allius Cinnamus.

EDCS-23400056.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. To Casinia Quartilla, to her well-deserving mother Tattia Iucunda.
EDCS-23400056.summary: A funerary dedication by Casinia Quartilla to her mother, Tattia Iucunda.

EDCS-23400057.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Magnisia made this for her son Gaius Gruleius Rufinus, who lived 11 years.
EDCS-23400057.summary: A funerary dedication by Magnisia for her son Gaius Gruleius Rufinus, who died at age 11.

EDCS-23400059.translation: Sacred to the Spirits of the Departed. [This was made] for the well-deserving Thetis, slave of Savonius Rufus, and for Savonia [---]hilla, [her?] daughter.
EDCS-23400059.summary: A funerary dedication for Thetis, a slave, and her daughter Savonia [---]hilla.

EDCS-23400513.summary: An inscription identifying Quintus Salvidienus as Imperator, likely from the Civil Wars period.

EDCS-23400514.summary: An inscription identifying Quintus Salvidienus as Imperator, likely from the Civil Wars period.

EDCS-23400521.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Publicius Tallus lived 35 years; the collegium of the cannophori (reed-bearers) made this.
EDCS-23400521.summary: A funerary dedication for Publicius Tallus by his collegium of cannophori.

EDCS-23400523.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Lucius Aedinius Pretiosus [set this up] for his incomparable father Aedinius Pretiosus.
EDCS-23400523.summary: A funerary dedication by Aedinius Pretiosus for his father, also named Aedinius Pretiosus.

EDCS-23400524.translation: To the Spirits of the Departed. Aedinius Pretiosus made this for his daughter Aedinia Amanda.
EDCS-23400524.summary: A funerary dedication by Aedinius Pretiosus for his daughter Aedinia Amanda.

EDCS-23400525.translation: Sacred to Mercury Augustus. Caesetius Primus [son of ---]ius Perseus [and ---]ius [---].
EDCS-23400525.summary: A religious dedication to Mercury Augustus by Caesetius Primus, with partial names of his parents.

EDCS-23400526.translation: To Lucius Nonius Asprenas, son of Lucius, consul. The decuriones and municipals [honored their] patron.
EDCS-23400526.summary: An honorific inscription by the decuriones and municipals for their patron, Lucius Nonius Asprenas, a consul.

EDCS-26500784.translation: Publius Claudius, son of Caius, and Caius Sextilius, son of Lucius, duovirs appointed by decree of the Senate.
EDCS-26500784.summary: This inscription records the names of two duovirs, Publius Claudius and Caius Sextilius, who were appointed by senatorial decree, likely for a public building or function.

EDCS-26500791.summary: This is a simple dedication to Vibia Vesonia, daughter of Decimus, likely part of a tombstone or honorary monument.

EDCS-26500794.translation: Classicus, one of the four magistrates with judicial powers, [to Lucius] Licinius Crassus, son of Lucius, and Publius Al[---] Pollio, son of Quintus, Quintus Anicius, son of Lucius [---], Decidius Rufus, son of Caius, and Caius [---] to Caius Egnatius Rufus, son of Caius, [---] for the wall to be repaired.
EDCS-26500794.summary: This fragmentary inscription lists several officials, likely aediles or similar magistrates, and mentions the repair of a wall, suggesting a public works project from the late Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-29900306.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Arellia Attice lived 60 years. May the earth lie lightly upon you.
EDCS-29900306.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Arellia Attice, recording her age and a common wish for the deceased, indicating a burial from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-31300241.translation: Cornelia Severina Bassus, daughter of Marcus, to whom the order and people of the Regini Iulienses, because of her excellent service to them during her life and after, ordered statues and shields to be set up at public expense. Titus Flavius Severinus Cornelius Saturninus, son of Titus, of the Palatina tribe, her heir, erected this at public expense, remitting costs from his own funds. The place was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-31300241.summary: This dedicatory inscription honors Cornelia Severina Bassus, likely a prominent local woman, with public statues and shields, funded by the community and erected by her heir, Titus Flavius Severinus Cornelius Saturninus, indicating civic honors in the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-31300248.translation: To Lucilia Isaurica, daughter of Caius, by the townspeople of Petelia, from contributions. In her memory, Megonius Leo bequeathed 100,000 sesterces to the community.
EDCS-31300248.summary: This funerary inscription for Lucilia Isaurica, funded by contributions from the townspeople of Petelia, also records a significant bequest by Megonius Leo in her memory, suggesting a benefaction in the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-31300249.translation: To Caedicia Iridis, daughter of Lucius, by the townspeople, from contributions, in honor of the merits of her son, Megonius Leo. In her memory, Leo bequeathed 100,000 sesterces.
EDCS-31300249.summary: This inscription honors Caedicia Iridis, funded by townspeople's contributions and connected to her son Megonius Leo, who also made a substantial bequest in her memory, suggesting civic commemoration and family benefaction in the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-31300250.translation: Cornelius Gemellus, son of Lucius, of the Romilia tribe, [aedile?] twice, quaestor, IIvir iure dicundo twice, gymnasium master three times, four times IIvir iure dicundo.
EDCS-31300250.summary: This is a fragmentary list of magistracies held by Cornelius Gemellus, indicating a career in local government and possibly a role in public administration or supervision, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-32900012.translation: [---] of Lucius Rabilis, a soldier of the [---] cohort, of the century of Tif[---].
EDCS-32900012.summary: This is a fragment of a military inscription, likely identifying a soldier and his unit, possibly from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-34300257.translation: To Marcus Aemilius Julianus Latinianus, of the clarifying purity, our patron, who, although the Regini Iulienses had destined a statue for him with collected funds, was content with the honor and set it up at his own expense.
EDCS-34300257.summary: This inscription honors Marcus Aemilius Julianus Latinianus as a patron, noting that he preferred to fund his own statue after the community had intended to provide one, indicating civic relations and patronage in the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-34300258.translation: To Julia Callitta, daughter of Gaius, of the Aemilia tribe, a most distinguished woman, priestess, for her many merits, the citizens of Regium, at their expense, by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-34300258.summary: This is a dedication by the citizens of Regium to a distinguished priestess, Julia Callitta, honoring her many merits.

EDCS-34300261.translation: To the Good Spirits. Lartianus erected this for his well-deserving grandfather Chrysogonus at his own expense. He lived 75 years.
EDCS-34300261.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Chrysogonus, erected by his grandson Lartianus, who lived 75 years.

EDCS-34300263.translation: To the Spirits. Marital affection erected this for his wife, Laridia (?) Thallusa (?), who lived 40 years.
EDCS-34300263.summary: This is a funerary dedication from a husband to his wife, possibly named Laridia Thallusa, who lived 40 years.

EDCS-34300265.summary: This is an incomplete funerary inscription for Cornelia, daughter of Marcus.

EDCS-34300267.translation: Sacred to the Spirits. Iucunda lived 2 years, 3 months, and 11 days. Her father for his sweetest daughter.
EDCS-34300267.summary: This is a funerary dedication from a father to his daughter Iucunda, who died at a very young age.

EDCS-34300281.translation: Felixissimus lived 54 years. Manilia Fortunata erected this for her well-deserving husband.
EDCS-34300281.summary: This is a funerary dedication from Manilia Fortunata to her husband, Felixissimus, who lived 54 years.

EDCS-34300282.translation: Equitia Celerina lived 55 years. Allia Critonilla, her mother, erected this for her well-deserving daughter.
EDCS-34300282.summary: This is a funerary dedication from a mother, Allia Critonilla, to her daughter Equitia Celerina, who lived 55 years.

EDCS-34300283.translation: Felicula lived 6 years. Atimetus erected this for his dearest sister.
EDCS-34300283.summary: This is a funerary dedication from Atimetus to his beloved sister Felicula, who died at the age of 6.

EDCS-34300288.translation: The freedmen of Ceppia Iusta took care to erect [this monument] for their patron Quintus Ceppius Maximus, son of Quintus, patron of the colony.
EDCS-34300288.summary: This is a dedication by the freedmen of Ceppia Iusta to their patron Quintus Ceppius Maximus, a patron of the colony.

EDCS-34700139.translation: Vinius Aticinus. In the consulship of Galba and Agrippa.
EDCS-34700139.summary: This inscription records the name Vinius Aticinus and the consuls Galba and Agrippa, likely dating it to 32 AD or 69 AD.

EDCS-34700147.translation: Nonia Longina lived 19 years and 20 days.
EDCS-34700147.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Nonia Longina.

EDCS-34700150.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Sosia Germana, his wife, made this for her most beloved husband, Athenaeus, who lived 58 years, a well-deserving recipient.
EDCS-34700150.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Sosia Germana for her deceased husband, Athenaeus, noting his age and her devotion.

EDCS-38000194.summary: This is a funerary inscription identifying the owner of the tomb as Antiochus of Samaria.

EDCS-42400058.summary: This is a very brief inscription, possibly naming two individuals, perhaps associated with a tomb or dedication.

EDCS-44100281.translation: The senate dedicated this to Lucius Vinuleius Brocchus, son of Gaius, of the Maecia tribe, a quaestor of justice, a quinquennial aedile, and a pontifex.
EDCS-44100281.summary: This is a dedication by the senate to Lucius Vinuleius Brocchus, listing his civic and religious offices, likely from the late Republican or early Imperial period.

EDCS-44800288.translation: To Lucius Valerius Lucanus, veteran, duovir of justice.
EDCS-44800288.summary: This is a dedication to Lucius Valerius Lucanus, a veteran who served as a duovir (a high civic magistrate).

EDCS-44800326.translation: [...] and Pyrriche, with his own money, made [this for ---] of the divine Nerva [...]
EDCS-44800326.summary: This inscription records that someone, likely named Pyrriche, funded a monument or dedication, possibly related to the emperor Nerva.

EDCS-44800365.translation: Lucius Coelius Hymetus, twice Augustalis, made this with his own money.
EDCS-44800365.summary: This is a dedication made by Lucius Coelius Hymetus, who held the position of Augustalis twice, funded by himself.

EDCS-44800376.translation: To Marcus Opellius Diadumenianus, most noble Caesar.
EDCS-44800376.summary: This is a dedication to Marcus Opellius Diadumenianus, referring to him with the honorific title of Caesar.

EDCS-44800385.translation: To Emperor Caesar [Marcus Aurelius] [Antoninus Augustus] Maximus [...]
EDCS-44800385.summary: This is a fragmentary dedication to Emperor Marcus Aurelius, likely part of a larger inscription honoring him.

EDCS-44800397.translation: To Helion(?), patron of the colony(?), the Augustales(?) with their own money.
EDCS-44800397.summary: An inscription recording a dedication to Helion, likely a patron, by the Augustales, probably dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-51200117.translation: The Copian decurions, as a mark of honor by their decree, have granted to Tiberius Claudius Idomen, freedman of Tiberius Claudius Caesar, the things written below. Publius Blaesius Marianus, IIIIvir with quinquennial power, acting as judge for the second time, and Marcus Minucius Sota, Prefect, having consulted the senate in the Curia Vinuleia on the eighth day before the Kalends of April, with consular authority, were present for the writing. Titus Albius Sabinus [?], Publius Suavitius Reginus, Lucius Idumaeus Mela, Quintus Vibulenus Agrippa [?], when words were spoken concerning the honor of Tiberius Claudius Idomen, freedman of Tiberius Claudius Caesar, and what it might please to do concerning that matter, they thus decreed: Because Tiberius Claudius Idomen has conducted himself in such a way during his years in Copia, having served in our municipality among the townsfolk, he has greatly surpassed others with the utmost modesty and justice, and having been made free, he has pleased this most distinguished order with a similar clemency. By our decree, let him be created an Augustalis for this year, an honor which has never been granted before this time, and let him hold that rank and be preferred by census, according to the law, among all whom the senate has judged to be Augustales this year, so that it may be more evident that the republic has studied him, and it may seem that he has rightly received the reward due to his modesty. And therefore, admiring him, let others of similar fortune and experienced life wish to imitate him, the most ample judgment of the senate.
EDCS-51200117.summary: A lengthy decree by the decurions of Copia granting the honor of Augustalis to Tiberius Claudius Idomen, a freedman, for his distinguished service and conduct, likely dating to the early Imperial period.

EDCS-55702379.translation: Poppaedia Prima, freedwoman of a woman.
EDCS-55702379.summary: A simple dedication by Poppaedia Prima, a freedwoman, possibly to a deceased patron or for herself, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-55702380.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Fortuna Ma(?), wife, erected this for Gaius Julius Nepos, her deserving husband, who lived for 43 years.
EDCS-55702380.summary: A funerary inscription for Gaius Julius Nepos, erected by his wife Fortuna Ma, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-55702381.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Attus Firmus, who lived 3 years, 5 months, and 4 days.
EDCS-55702381.summary: A funerary inscription for Attus Firmus, likely a child, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-55702382.translation: Gaius Baebius Lupus and Marcus Baebius Maximus, sons, made this for their deserving father Gaius Baebius Lupus and their mother Trebia Maxima.
EDCS-55702382.summary: A funerary epitaph for Gaius Baebius Lupus and Trebia Maxima, erected by their sons, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-55702383.translation: Cypare made this for Gemellus, her fellow slave. He is buried here.
EDCS-55702383.summary: An epitaph for Gemellus, a fellow slave, erected by Cypare, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-55702384.translation: To the spirits of the departed. The collegium Spei erected this for Marcus Arrius Cresimus, a deserving colleague, who lived for 50 years and 7 months.
EDCS-55702384.summary: A funerary inscription for Marcus Arrius Cresimus, erected by his collegium (association) named Spei, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-55702385.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Lucius Vicirius Capito and his wife Cornelia Gemella erected this for Lucius Vicirius Rufus, son of Lucius, who was aedile and IIIIvir with power to judge, a deserving man.
EDCS-55702385.summary: A funerary inscription for Lucius Vicirius Rufus, a former magistrate, erected by his son and wife, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-55702388.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Tattia Procula [erected this] for her husband Lucius Tattius Pelopianus, who lived for 50 years, a deserving man.
EDCS-55702388.summary: A funerary inscription for Lucius Tattius Pelopianus, erected by his wife Tattia Procula, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-55702389.translation: To the departed spirits. Agilius and Victorinus. The father placed this for his brothers.
EDCS-55702389.summary: A funerary dedication by a father for his sons, Agilius and Victorinus.

EDCS-55702390.translation: To the departed spirits. Annia Felicula made this for her son and grandson, well-deserving, who lived 25 years.
EDCS-55702390.summary: A funerary dedication by Annia Felicula for her son and grandson, specifying the age of one of them.

EDCS-55702392.translation: To the departed spirits. Naevius Marcellus made this for his well-deserving wife Gargilia Marciana, who lived 41 years.
EDCS-55702392.summary: A funerary dedication by Naevius Marcellus for his wife, Gargilia Marciana, including her age at death.

EDCS-55702393.translation: To the departed spirits. Sabinus and his son made this for his wife Quintae, who lived 3 years, 3 months, and 30 days, well-deserving.
EDCS-55702393.summary: A funerary dedication by Sabinus and his son for his wife Quintae, providing details of her lifespan.

EDCS-55702394.translation: To the departed spirits. Lucius Postumius Aptus placed this for his most sweet and well-deserving wife Numisia. She lived 20 years and two months.
EDCS-55702394.summary: A funerary dedication by Lucius Postumius Aptus for his wife Numisia, detailing her age at death.

EDCS-56500295.summary: A very brief inscription, possibly a name and a status or location, with an uncertain date and context.

EDCS-57000037.translation: To the departed spirits. Trasius the father made this for Flavia Turina, who lived 3 years and 2 months.
EDCS-57000037.summary: A funerary dedication by Trasius for his daughter Flavia Turina, specifying her young age.

EDCS-57100040.translation: To Mercury. [---] to his well-deserving wife.
EDCS-57100040.summary: A funerary dedication to Mercury, likely by a husband for his wife.

EDCS-58500265.translation: Celadion of the troupe of Ionic pantomime actors, who lived 5 years. Pluto snatched him too soon to death, undeservedly, bringing unending grief to his father. Where, Celadon, are you to sacrifice to the gods, where to bring fitting garlands to the altars and pure offerings with incense? Pitiful Hades snatched him from the stage, bringing many tears and sorrows to his parents.
EDCS-58500265.summary: A Greek epitaph for a young pantomime actor named Celadion, lamenting his premature death and lamenting his lost performances.

EDCS-59400027.translation: Marcus Insteius Silvester and Gaius Luxilius Silvanus, as aediles and a board of four magistrates with judicial authority, supervised the restoration of the street of the Venausion district with public money.
EDCS-59400027.summary: A public inscription recording the restoration of a street by aediles and magistrates in the Venausion district.

EDCS-60600011.translation: Zosima, fellow freedwoman, made this for Lucius Marcius Hilarion, freedman of Lucius, and for herself.
EDCS-60600011.summary: A funerary dedication by a freedwoman for her deceased freedman husband and herself, likely dating to the 1st-3rd centuries CE.

EDCS-61700661.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Valerius Diocletian, the Invincible Augustus, and to the Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Valerius Maximian, the Pious, Fortunate, Invincible Augustus, and to Gaius Valerius Constantius and Galerius Valerius Maximian, most noble Caesars, [in honor of] our lord and saviour Augustus, Claudius Iovianus, well-born to the state, our lord, Claudius Flavius Iovianus Augustus, well-born to the state.
EDCS-61700661.summary: A dedication to the Tetrarchs, likely honoring Diocletian, Maximian, Constantius, and Galerius, and specifically to the emperor Claudius Iovianus, probably dating to the late 3rd or early 4th century CE.

EDCS-63600003.translation: To the Divine Shades. The Minervius collegium and the sodales made this, deservedly, for Lucius Romanus Abascantus, freedman of Numerius. He lived 80 years.
EDCS-63600003.summary: A funerary monument dedicated by a collegium and its members to a deceased freedman, Lucius Romanus Abascantus, who lived 80 years, dating to the 1st-3rd centuries CE.

EDCS-63600004.translation: To the Divine Shades. For Marcella, slave of Lucius Antonius. Her son Iseus and her preserved slave Hermes took care of it, and made it for her, deserving and most dutiful. She lived 35 years. She lies here.
EDCS-63600004.summary: A funerary dedication for Marcella, slave of Lucius Antonius, made by her son and another slave, who lived 35 years, dating to the 1st-3rd centuries CE.

EDCS-63600005.translation: To the Divine Shades? His preserved slave Musa and his son Stator made this for Stator, slave of Lucius Valerius Potitus, deservedly. He lived 35 years.
EDCS-63600005.summary: A funerary dedication for Stator, slave of Lucius Valerius Potitus, made by his slave Musa and son Stator, who lived 35 years, dating to the 1st-3rd centuries CE.

EDCS-63600006.translation: To the Divine Shades. Abascantus made this, deservedly, for Leuca, his preserved slave. She lived 40 years.
EDCS-63600006.summary: A funerary dedication by Abascantus for his slave Leuca, who lived 40 years, dating to the 1st-3rd centuries CE.

EDCS-63600007.translation: Primitiva lived 7 years. She lies here.
EDCS-63600007.summary: A simple funerary epitaph for Primitiva, who lived 7 years, dating to the 1st-3rd centuries CE.

EDCS-63600008.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Salvilla made this for her deserving husband Magno. She lived with him 30 years. He was 70 years old. He lies here.
EDCS-63600008.summary: A funerary dedication by Salvilla for her husband Magno, whom she lived with for 30 years, and who was 70 years old, dating to the 1st-3rd centuries CE.

EDCS-63600009.translation: To the Divine Shades. His mother Phoebe made this, deservedly, for Hermes. He lived 11 years.
EDCS-63600009.summary: A funerary dedication by Phoebe for her son Hermes, who lived 11 years, dating to the 1st-3rd centuries CE.

EDCS-63600010.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Eros made this for his deserving wife Prisca. He lived with her 10 years.
EDCS-63600010.summary: A funerary dedication by Eros for his wife Prisca, with whom he lived 10 years, dating to the 1st-3rd centuries CE.

EDCS-63600011.translation: To the departed spirits. Amyna made this for Festva, her freedwoman, who deserved well. She lived 40 years.
EDCS-63600011.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to a freedwoman named Amyna by her patron, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-63600012.translation: To the departed spirits, sacred. For Symferusa.
EDCS-63600012.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Symferusa, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-63600014.translation: Eminis Aprille dedicated this while alive.
EDCS-63600014.summary: This is a dedication made by Eminis Aprille for herself during her lifetime, likely an offering in a sanctuary, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-63700016.translation: Tallusa, his wife, made this for Hilarius, her incomparable husband.
EDCS-63700016.summary: This is a funerary inscription from the Roman Imperial period, where a wife named Tallusa dedicates a monument to her 'incomparable' husband, Hilarius.

EDCS-63700017.translation: To the departed spirits. Donnia Fortunata made this for her sweetest son, Donnius Fortunio, who lived 5 years, 10 months.
EDCS-63700017.summary: This is a funerary inscription from the Roman Imperial period, where Donnia Fortunata dedicates a monument to her young son, Donnius Fortunio.

EDCS-63700018.translation: An unhappy mother, Quinta, [dedicated this] for her children: for her father Hilarus, for her son Agathemerus, for her son Lucanus, for her son Cissus, for her daughter Iszmyrna.
EDCS-63700018.summary: This inscription, likely funerary, records a mother named Quinta dedicating a monument to her deceased children and possibly her husband, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-63700020.translation: Of Caius Egnatius Rufus, son of Spurius, of the Collina tribe.
EDCS-63700020.summary: This is a titulus, likely from a tomb or dedication, identifying Caius Egnatius Rufus, son of Spurius, of the Collina tribe, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-64400107.translation: To Titus Flavius Gavius, his father and son, and to Flavius Gavius, his sweetest son, who lived 23 years, 8 months, 9 days. Gavianus, his father, made this.
EDCS-64400107.summary: This is a funerary inscription from the Roman Imperial period where Gavianus the father dedicates a monument to his deceased son, Flavius Gavius, and also to his own father, Titus Flavius Gavius.

EDCS-64400429.translation: To the departed spirits. The son made this for Marcus Marrius Domitius, veteran, who lived 85 years, his well-deserving father.
EDCS-64400429.summary: This is a funerary inscription from the Roman Imperial period where a son dedicates a monument to his father, Marcus Marrius Domitius, a veteran.

EDCS-64400430.translation: To Quintus Valerius Sisenna Reginus, son of Lucius, of the Mae(cia) tribe, Roman knight, who died here while navigating ahead, in a place publicly granted. Caius Popillius Quartio, his father-in-law, [made this] with his own money.
EDCS-64400430.summary: This funerary inscription from the Roman Imperial period records the burial of Quintus Valerius Sisenna Reginus, a Roman knight, and notes that the plot was publicly granted and the monument funded by his father-in-law.

EDCS-64800426.translation: To the departed spirits. Aurelia Tertullina, his deserving wife, for whom he lived 15 years, 2 months, and 16 days. Aurelius Hesper, her husband.
EDCS-64800426.summary: A funerary epitaph dedicated by a husband to his deceased wife, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-64800427.translation: To the departed spirits. Aurelia Septimina, his deserving wife, who lived 29 years, 10 months, and 24 days. Impetratus, her husband, to his mother.
EDCS-64800427.summary: A funerary epitaph for Aurelia Septimina, dedicated by her husband Impetratus, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-64900537.translation: To the departed spirits. Gaius Aquillius Iulius lived 24 years, who perished in a shipwreck. Gaius Aquillius Iacchus, the caregiver, made this for him, deserving.
EDCS-64900537.summary: A funerary epitaph for Gaius Aquillius Iulius, who died in a shipwreck, dedicated by his caregiver, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-64900986.summary: A military inscription mentioning Salvidienus and the Tenth Legion, likely dating to the Roman Republican or early Imperial period.

EDCS-64901134.translation: Numestronia gave this as a gift.
EDCS-64901134.summary: A dedication of a gift by Numestronia, the context and date of which are unknown.

EDCS-65300057.summary: An inscription mentioning Salvidienus, possibly the general, and Quintus, with uncertain context and date.

EDCS-67400196.translation: To the departed spirits. To [3]ia Alexandra, [mother] most sweet. Iulianus and Marcia [3] [3] made this for her, deserving.
EDCS-67400196.summary: A funerary epitaph for a woman named Alexandra, dedicated by her children Iulianus and Marcia, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-67400198.summary: A fragment of an inscription potentially recording a dedication or funerary monument by Lucius Tatius, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-67700146.translation: Gaius Aullius Cilo Humanius, prefect, and Marcus Alfidius Philonicus, prefect, acting under the Petroni(an) law with censorship and power, carried out the construction by senatorial decree and approved it.
EDCS-67700146.summary: An official inscription detailing the construction work overseen by two prefects under specific legal and senatorial authority, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-67700147.translation: Gaius Marcius Silvanus fulfilled his vow willingly and deservedly to Isis.
EDCS-67700147.summary: A religious votive inscription by Gaius Marcius Silvanus to the goddess Isis, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-69200216.translation: Maximus, former governor of the province of Narbonensis. . .
EDCS-69200216.summary: This fragment appears to be part of a dedication or honorific inscription for Maximus, a former proconsul of Narbonensis, likely from the late Roman period.

EDCS-70700112.translation: To the gods of the underworld. Lucius Numisius Bassus lived 57 years. May the earth lie lightly upon you.
EDCS-70700112.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Numisius Bassus, who died at the age of 57, with a standard wishing him a peaceful afterlife.

EDCS-70700113.translation: To Gaius Flam[---]. Gamus [---] lived [---]. Felicla [---]
EDCS-70700113.summary: This is a fragmentary epitaph, possibly for multiple individuals including Felicla, with incomplete names and lifespans.

EDCS-70700114.summary: This is a simple greeting or dedication, possibly a funerary marker, to Pomponia Syntyce.

EDCS-70700115.translation: Trebia, freedwoman of Arche, for herself and her family. Auxesis died at 14 years old. Quintus [---]brius Bulla.
EDCS-70700115.summary: This epitaph records the death of a 14-year-old girl named Auxesis, set up by Trebia, a freedwoman, and possibly also by Quintus [---]brius Bulla.

EDCS-71000697.translation: To the gods of the underworld and to the memory of Urbana. . . Zosimus, her husband, lived 33 years, an exemplary spouse.
EDCS-71000697.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Zosimus for his wife Urbana, whom he describes as an exemplary spouse, dating likely to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-71000698.translation: To the gods of the underworld. Ampliatus, who lived 18 years, 3 months, and 5 days. His mother made this for her well-deserving son.
EDCS-71000698.summary: This funerary epitaph records the death of Ampliatus at the age of 18 and was erected by his mother.

EDCS-72300243.translation: To Sabinia, his wife. Victor made this for her, well-deserving.
EDCS-72300243.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by Victor for his wife Sabinia.

EDCS-72300244.translation: To the gods of the underworld. For Julia Salbia, mother, well-deserving, who lived 70 years.
EDCS-72300244.summary: This funerary epitaph records that Julia Salbia, mother, died at the age of 70 and was well-deserving.

EDCS-72300269.translation: . . . Marcella. They placed [this for him] who lived 5 years, 11 months, and 23 days.
EDCS-72300269.summary: This is a fragmentary epitaph recording the death of a child named Marcella (or for whom Marcella is associated), who died at the age of 5 years, 11 months, and 23 days.

EDCS-74800046.translation: From the will of Luxilia Rustica, her heirs Lucius Obinius Gratus, grandson Lucius Obinius Gratus, and great-grandson Lucius Obinius Gratus made the bathhouse.
EDCS-74800046.summary: This inscription records the construction of a bathhouse by heirs in accordance with a will, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-76300166.translation: Quintia Prima... I ask that my enemy... be moved... monuments and Rusticena... that she come to Lamia, I ask.
EDCS-76300166.summary: This fragmented inscription appears to be a curse or a request concerning the removal of monuments and the movement of individuals, possibly from the late Roman Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-76400055.summary: A simple dedication to Sextia Rufa, likely a tombstone or a dedication of a small object.

EDCS-76400059.translation: Freedmen set up [this monument] to their most deserving patron, Cattius Feroninus, IIvir quinquennalis.
EDCS-76400059.summary: This inscription is a dedication by freedmen to their patron, a prominent local magistrate (IIvir quinquennalis), likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-76600085.summary: This brief inscription in Greek records the maker of an object, likely a work of art or a craft item.

EDCS-76600336.translation: The council and people of Regini, for Cornelia Severina Bassus, daughter of Marcus, wife of Saturninus, who deserved exceedingly well of them both in public and private during her life and afterwards, ordered that statues and shields be publicly erected with money from the treasury; Titus Flavius Severinus Cornelius Saturninus, son of Titus, of the Palatine tribe, her heir, placed [them] at the expense of the state, the cost having been remitted from his own funds, the place having been granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-76600336.summary: This inscription honors Cornelia Severina Bassus, a woman praised for her public and private service, by her town Regini and her heir, who erected statues and shields using public funds, likely from the mid-Imperial period.

EDCS-76800074.translation: Marcus Caninius Alexander made this for himself and for Domitia Hyle, freedwoman of Publius, and for Titus Annio Loto, and for Cossutia Amaranthid and his own [family]; I lived faithfully with Domitia Faustus, freedwoman of Publius, most loving to my brother; this monument or external sepulchre will not follow an heir.
EDCS-76800074.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Marcus Caninius Alexander and his family, including freedmen and possibly a slave, specifying that the tomb does not pass to heirs, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-76800108.translation: By decree of the decurions, to the Emperor Caesar Publius Licinius Gallienus Augustus, chief priest, with tribunician power, consul for the second time, father of the country.
EDCS-76800108.summary: This is a dedication to Emperor Gallienus, likely erected by a local council (decurions), dating to his reign (260-268 CE).

EDCS-76900095.translation: To Antonia Prisca, daughter of Lucius Valerius Sura, triarch, who lived 17 years and 13 days. Lucius Valerius Sura, triarch, made [this] for his well-deserving wife.
EDCS-76900095.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Antonia Prisca at a young age and is dedicated by her husband, a triarch, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-78700047.translation: Coraeso, her husband, placed [this] for Porcatia Priscilla, his well-deserving wife, aged 50 years.
EDCS-78700047.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by a husband for his wife, indicating her age and that she was well-deserving, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-80200112.translation: To the spirit of the municipality of Atina, the altar. Latinius Lucanus the father placed it. Latinius Lucanus the son wrote it and dedicated it at his own expense. The place was given by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-80200112.summary: This is an altar dedicated to the genius of the municipality of Atina by Latinius Lucanus the father and son, likely in the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-80700088.translation: Lived 10 years. Most sweet Amanda made this for [him/her] well deserving.
EDCS-80700088.summary: This is a tombstone for Amanda, who lived 10 years, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-80700090.summary: This is a fragmentary tombstone likely for a person named Felix, with mentions of mothers Aureola and another woman, possibly from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-81800054.translation: To the departed spirits. For Marcello, son, father. He lived 13 years.
EDCS-81800054.summary: This is a tombstone for Marcello, son and father, who died at 13 years old, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-81800055.translation: To the departed spirits. Lucius Cornelius Helius rests here. He lived 41 years. Cornelia Tyche his mother and Caedia Nerais his most devoted companion placed [this] for [him]. If fate had placed [this] correctly, this tombstone of the mother ought to have been read before.
EDCS-81800055.summary: This is a tombstone for Lucius Cornelius Helius, placed by his mother and companion, likely from the Roman Imperial period, with a poignant note about his mother's potential earlier death.

EDCS-81800056.translation: Lived 21 years. Luxilia Potine, mother, made this for [her] son, well deserving.
EDCS-81800056.summary: This is a tombstone for a son who lived 21 years, dedicated by his mother Luxilia Potine, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-82000097.translation: Chresimus placed [this] for [his] well-deserving wife. Lived 80 years.
EDCS-82000097.summary: This is a tombstone for a wife who lived 80 years, dedicated by her husband Chresimus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-82000098.translation: To the departed spirits. [...]bio Barabianus [...]dia Elias [....
EDCS-82000098.summary: This is a fragmentary tombstone dedicated to the departed spirits, mentioning names like Barabianus and Elias, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-82000099.translation: To the departed spirits. Gaius Clodius Donatus placed this stone for his dearest son Clodius Festus.
EDCS-82000099.summary: This is a tombstone for Clodius Festus, placed by his father Gaius Clodius Donatus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-82000100.translation: To the departed spirits. For Caecilia Maxima. She lived 70 years. Clodia Prova made this for her well-deserving mother.
EDCS-82000100.summary: This is a tombstone for Caecilia Maxima, who lived 70 years, dedicated by her daughter Clodia Prova, likely from the Roman Imperial period.
