EDCS-82900085.translation: Gaius Dexius, son of Caius, Publius Vilius, son of Publius, and Marcus Accius, son of Marcus, as quinquennial magistrates with judicial authority, ensured that this was constructed from public and donated money, which the townspeople and residents contributed of their own free will, and they approved it.
EDCS-82900085.summary: This inscription records the construction of a public work by four magistrates in office, funded by both public money and private donations from the citizens.

EDCS-82900086.translation: Gaius Dexius, son of Caius, Publius Vilius, son of Publius, and Marcus Accius, son of Marcus, as quinquennial magistrates with judicial authority, ensured that this was constructed from public and donated money, which the townspeople and residents contributed of their own free will, and they approved it.
EDCS-82900086.summary: This inscription records the construction of a public work by four magistrates in office, funded by both public money and private donations from the citizens.

EDCS-03300091.summary: Fragment of an inscription mentioning a man's name, likely a funerary or honorific text.

EDCS-06600027.summary: This inscription records a dedication, likely funerary, made by an individual named Vasa.

EDCS-10700940.translation: To the departed spirits. Marcus N[---] [---] [---] erected [this].
EDCS-10700940.summary: A funerary inscription dedicating a monument to Marcus N[---] by an unknown person.

EDCS-11400462.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription that likely records a dedication or memorial for someone's mother.

EDCS-16201156.translation: Under the consulship of Lateranus and Ruphinus, under the supervision of the proconsul.
EDCS-16201156.summary: A fragmentary inscription indicating a date during the consulship of Lateranus and Ruphinus (likely mid-3rd century CE) and mentioning the supervision of a proconsul.

EDCS-16201157.translation: Third place, under the consulship of Victorinus and Severus, workshop of the bishop.
EDCS-16201157.summary: An inscription indicating a location ('third place') and referencing a workshop associated with a bishop during the consulship of Victorinus and Severus (likely late 2nd or 3rd century CE).

EDCS-16201158.translation: Third place, second section, under the consulship of Lateranus and Rufinus.
EDCS-16201158.summary: An inscription denoting a specific location ('third place, second section') and a date during the consulship of Lateranus and Rufinus (likely mid-3rd century CE).

EDCS-59800029.translation: [---]ilius for Ubionius(?), well-deserving, made this. He lived 18 years.
EDCS-59800029.summary: A fragmentary funerary dedication for a male individual who lived 18 years.

EDCS-03000130.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription identifying a person named Lucius Domitius.

EDCS-03000131.summary: This fragmentary inscription records a donation by Caius, grandson of someone named Venereus.

EDCS-06600018.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription identifying a person named Maraeus Deinius.

EDCS-06600023.translation: To the Divine Manes. Pontius and Gavia, parents, made this for their dearest son, Faustus Pontius, who lived 13 years, [died] by a wicked funeral.
EDCS-06600023.summary: This is a funerary dedication from parents to their beloved son, Pontius Faustus, who died at the age of 13.

EDCS-06600041.translation: To the Divine Manes. Pardus, father, made this for his well-deserving daughter, Herria Privata.
EDCS-06600041.summary: This is a funerary dedication from a father to his deserving daughter, Herria Privata.

EDCS-06600045.translation: Cnaeus Marcus and Vinucieis, son of Cnaeus, gave this gift willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-06600045.summary: This inscription records a voluntary gift given by Cnaeus Marcus and Vinucieis, son of Cnaeus.

EDCS-06600054.translation: DIO Atimetus made this monument for his deserving wife, Antea Diaonia.
EDCS-06600054.summary: This is a funerary dedication from a husband, DIO Atimetus, to his deserving wife, Antea Diaonia.

EDCS-06600055.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription recording a dedication made by Marcus Abuntantius to a loved one.

EDCS-06600067.translation: To Spedia Galla, daughter of Gaius Spedius, lived 2 years, 10 months. To Gaius Spedius Bassus, son of Gaius Spedius, lived 6 years, 10 months. To Bassus Spedius.
EDCS-06600067.summary: This is a funerary inscription for members of the Spedia family, recording the ages at death of two children.

EDCS-06600092.translation: Decumanus XIII, Kardo I. Gaius Sempronius, son of Tiberius; Appius Claudius, son of Gaius; Publius Licinius, son of Publius. Commissioners for judging and assigning lands.
EDCS-06600092.summary: This inscription identifies officials responsible for land allocation, likely from the Republican or early Imperial period.

EDCS-06600094.translation: To the departed shades. Caffius, twice consul, placed this white sword of Pomponius here. His wife and daughter did this.
EDCS-06600094.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Pomponius, indicating his wife and daughter erected the monument, possibly relating to a military career given the mention of a sword.

EDCS-06600106.translation: Quintus Poppaedius, freedman of Quintus, made this for Chrestion, with his own hand.
EDCS-06600106.summary: This is a dedication by a freedman, Quintus Poppaedius, for someone named Chrestion, likely a monument or artwork.

EDCS-07000348.translation: To the departed shades. To my dearest wife, who lived 20 years. Titus Aelius [---] son of Antinas, to his dearest daughter, who lived 10 years, 11 months, 5 days.
EDCS-07000348.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a wife and daughter, commissioned by Titus Aelius, likely their husband and father.

EDCS-07400247.translation: To the departed shades. Aurelia Marta made this for her well-deserving husband, Claudius Helion, who lived 64 years, 2 months.
EDCS-07400247.summary: This is a funerary epitaph erected by a wife for her husband, Claudius Helion.

EDCS-08400176.translation: Petronia, who departed on the 8th day before the Ides of August, is placed here, and Adeodata, who departed on the Nones of March.
EDCS-08400176.summary: This inscription records the death dates of two women, Petronia and Adeodata, indicating their burial place.

EDCS-08500223.translation: To our lord Flavius Claudius Julianus, victorious and triumphant, forever Augustus.
EDCS-08500223.summary: This is a dedication to the Emperor Julian, praising his military victories and titles.

EDCS-09001261.translation: To the departed shades. Benedicta to her well-deserving wife, Felix, who lived [---] months, two days.
EDCS-09001261.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Benedicta for her wife, Felix.

EDCS-09200229.translation: Iulia Crescentia and Furia Nemesis, grandmother and mother, arranged for this to be made for Lucius A[---]dulcius, who lived 12 years, 6 months, 26 days.
EDCS-09200229.summary: This is a funerary inscription commissioned by the grandmother and mother for Lucius A[---]dulcius, recording his age at death.

EDCS-09300192.translation: Publius Paquius Priamus, son of Publius, and Quintus Annius, son of Quintus, served as the IIII viri (board of four officials).
EDCS-09300192.summary: This inscription records the names and service of two men, Publius Paquius Priamus and Quintus Annius, as IIII viri, likely from Ostia or a similar Roman town.

EDCS-09400240.translation: Quintus Blattius Euplus lived 40 years. May the earth lie lightly upon you.
EDCS-09400240.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Quintus Blattius Euplus, who lived for 40 years, followed by a common wish for the deceased.

EDCS-09400241.translation: Hail Mani Meconi Aphrodisi, who lived 65 years. May the earth lie lightly upon you.
EDCS-09400241.summary: This funerary epitaph records the life of Mani Meconi Aphrodisi, who lived 65 years, followed by a common wish for the deceased.

EDCS-09400242.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Marcus Baebius Pudens lived 40 years. His wife, deserving of good things, made this. May the earth lie lightly upon you.
EDCS-09400242.summary: This funerary epitaph, dedicated to the Divine Spirits, records Marcus Baebius Pudens, who lived 40 years, and was honored by his wife.

EDCS-09400243.translation: Marcus Naevius Felicio lived 50 years. Sallustia Chione, from her own means.
EDCS-09400243.summary: This funerary epitaph records the life of Marcus Naevius Felicio, who lived 50 years, and was commemorated by Sallustia Chione at her own expense.

EDCS-09401406.translation: Lucius Numisius Classicus, son of Lucius Caius Musanus, son of Caius, and Lucius Licinius Crassus, son of Lucius, and Publius Allius Pollio, son of Quintus Anicius Lucius, undertook the contract for the construction of the IIII viri (city gates) and the repair of the walls.
EDCS-09401406.summary: This inscription records a public works contract awarded by officials of Ostia (implied by 'ostia in portas') concerning the construction of gates and repair of walls.

EDCS-09700115.translation: To Lucius Gavius, thanks to Fors Fortuna and such great courage, though plundered by the conventus from the excess of their virtue.
EDCS-09700115.summary: This fragmentary inscription appears to be a dedication or commendation to Lucius Gavius for his courage despite being wronged by a group ('conventus').

EDCS-09700118.summary: This very brief inscription likely records Pancarpus, a slave or freedman, belonging to a woman named Livia.

EDCS-09700941.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Insteia Lantenusa made this for her husband Decimus Dinnus Ariscon, who deserved well, who was buried without any fault of mine in that place where he lived for 17 years, 5 months, 17 days, and 12 hours.
EDCS-09700941.summary: This funerary epitaph, dedicated to the Divine Spirits, records that Insteia Lantenusa created it for her well-deserving husband, Decimus Dinnus Ariscon, detailing his age at death.

EDCS-09700942.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Manilius Iustus, son of Marcius, made this for his dearest wife, Numonia Marciana, daughter of Quintus.
EDCS-09700942.summary: This funerary epitaph, dedicated to the Divine Spirits, records that Manilius Iustus commissioned the monument for his beloved wife, Numonia Marciana.

EDCS-09800083.translation: Sextus Sextius, son of Sextius, Lucius Tatios, son of Lucius, Lucius Claudius, son of Trebius, Lucius Statius, son of Caius, quaestors, made this from the spoils.
EDCS-09800083.summary: This inscription records quaestors who made something from spoils, likely a public work or dedication.

EDCS-09800084.translation: Lucius Manius, son of Manius, Marcus Fadius, son of Marcus, Lucius Megonius, son of Caius, Caius Vibius, son of Caius, Olus Bracius, son of Vibus, quaestors, levied and made this.
EDCS-09800084.summary: This inscription lists several quaestors responsible for levying and creating something, possibly a tax or a public construction.

EDCS-09800085.translation: Lucius, son of Lucius, quaestors, gave this.
EDCS-09800085.summary: This brief inscription records a dedication made by a quaestor named Lucius.

EDCS-10700918.summary: This inscription likely records a dedication or dedication to two individuals named Quintus Celer and Maximus.

EDCS-10700922.translation: Sacred to the Divine Spirits. Lede Silvester made this for her deserving wife, with whom she lived for 65 years.
EDCS-10700922.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by Lede Silvester for her wife, recording their 65 years of life together.

EDCS-10700923.translation: To the Divine Spirits. For Quintiana, dearest daughter, who lived 36 years, her devoted mother Quinta made this.
EDCS-10700923.summary: This funerary epitaph records the death of Quintiana, a daughter cherished by her mother Quinta.

EDCS-10700927.translation: Marcus Baio made this for Secundus.
EDCS-10700927.summary: This inscription records a dedication made by Marcus Baio for someone named Secundus.

EDCS-10700932.translation: Decumanus, Kardo XIII. Caius Sempronius, son of Tiberius. Appius Claudius, son of Caius. Publius Licinius, son of Publius.
EDCS-10700932.summary: This inscription appears to record property boundaries or a division of land, listing several Roman citizens and a location identifier.

EDCS-10700936.translation: To the Divine Spirits. For Tundus, dearest wife, with whom I lived 20 years. For Antina, dearest daughter, who lived 10 years, 11 months, and 5 days.
EDCS-10700936.summary: This is a double funerary dedication from Titus Aelius to his wife Tundus and daughter Antina, specifying their lifespans.

EDCS-10700944.translation: To the Divine Spirits. For Ulpia Herais, dearest wife. Marcus Ma Das.
EDCS-10700944.summary: This funerary epitaph records the death of Ulpia Herais, for whom her husband Marcus Ma Das made a dedication.

EDCS-10701372.translation: Emperors Caesar Flavius Valentinianus, pious, fortunate, victorious and triumphant, ever Augustus, and Flavius Valens, pious, fortunate, victorious and triumphant, ever Augustus, and Flavius Gratianus, pious, fortunate, victorious and triumphant, ever Augustus, restored to their realms the baths which had collapsed from age and earthquake, returning them to a better condition and form under more fortunate auspices; the basilica of marbles, which had never possessed such beauty, was restored, and a new portico was added. Supervised by Pontius Atticus, a most distinguished man, corrector of Lucania and the Bruttii, dedicated on the fourth day before the Kalends of July, during the consulship of our lord Gratianus Augustus for the third time and Flavius Equitius, a most distinguished man.
EDCS-10701372.summary: This inscription records the restoration of public baths and a basilica of marbles in Lucania and the Bruttii by the emperors Valentinian I, Valens, and Gratian, dedicated during the consulship of Gratian and Equitius.

EDCS-10701390.translation: This price of life: Restutus, having drunk, the protection of his parents.
EDCS-10701390.summary: This inscription is a short epitaph for Restutus, possibly commemorating his life or death, with a focus on parental protection.

EDCS-10701710.summary: This is a simple dedication or funerary inscription from Hedyl to Hedylius.

EDCS-10701713.summary: This inscription identifies Artemo as the freedman of Minatius Trebius.

EDCS-10801425.translation: My mistress Victoria died on the second day before the Kalends of March, on the day of the Sabbath. [Written by] Geminus, her husband.
EDCS-10801425.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Victoria on a specific date and mentions her husband, Geminus.

EDCS-10801426.translation: Here rests [---] who lived more or less [---] years, laid to rest on the sixth day before the Ides of February, after the consulship of Paullinus the Younger.
EDCS-10801426.summary: This epitaph records the burial of an individual after the consulship of Paullinus the Younger, with lacunae indicating missing information.

EDCS-10801427.translation: To the memory of Macedo, the presbyter, who lived [---]
EDCS-10801427.summary: This funerary inscription is a memorial to Macedo, identified as a presbyter, with an incomplete record of his life.

EDCS-10801428.translation: Sacred to a good memory: faithful Criscentia, who lived for more or less 70 years, 5 months, and 8 days. Her children treated her well. She departed in peace.
EDCS-10801428.summary: This epitaph commemorates Criscentia, recording her age and noting that her children treated her well, indicating she departed in peace.

EDCS-10801430.translation: Gaudentia, laid to rest in peace, on the fourteenth day before the Kalends of October.
EDCS-10801430.summary: This epitaph records the peaceful rest of Gaudentia on a specific date.

EDCS-10801431.translation: Here rests Gloriosa, who lived for Christ for more or less five years.
EDCS-10801431.summary: This funerary inscription records the life of Gloriosa, who lived for Christ for approximately five years.

EDCS-10801432.translation: Ianuarius, who lived about 35 years, for whom his wife and sons did well.
EDCS-10801432.summary: This epitaph commemorates Ianuarius, indicating his lifespan and that his wife and sons erected it.

EDCS-10801433.translation: Ianuarius, faithful, of good memory, who lived for [unspecified number of] years.
EDCS-10801433.summary: This is a fragmentary epitaph for a man named Ianuarius, noting his faithfulness and good memory.

EDCS-10801434.translation: Ianuarius, faithful, of good memory, lived in peace for about 50 years; his wife did well for him; departed on the third day before the Kalends of September.
EDCS-10801434.summary: This epitaph records the death of Ianuarius, specifying his lifespan, that his wife memorialized him, and the date of his passing.

EDCS-10801435.translation: Marcuana, faithful, who lived 30 years and 9 months; to whom her husband and parents did well.
EDCS-10801435.summary: This epitaph records the death of Marcuana, detailing her lifespan and that she was memorialized by her husband and parents.

EDCS-10801436.translation: Marciana, faithful, of good memory, who lived 45 years, 7 months, and 8 days; for whom her brother and sons did well; departed in peace.
EDCS-10801436.summary: This inscription honors Marciana, specifying her age at death and that she was memorialized by her brother and sons.

EDCS-10801438.translation: Prima, faithful, of good memory, who lived about 70 years, 9 months, and 7 days; for whom Firmus did well; departed in peace.
EDCS-10801438.summary: This epitaph records the death of Prima, detailing her lifespan and that Firmus memorialized her.

EDCS-10801439.translation: Primenia, faithful, of good memory, lived 30 years, 5 months, and 10 days; for whom her father and husband did well.
EDCS-10801439.summary: This epitaph honors Primenia, specifying her lifespan and that she was memorialized by her father and husband.

EDCS-10801441.translation: Quintus, faithful, of good memory, lived 80 years; rests in peace, well.
EDCS-10801441.summary: This inscription records the death of Quintus, stating his lifespan and that he rests in peace.

EDCS-10801442.translation: Veneriana, of good memory, who lived eight years; for whom her parents did well in peace.
EDCS-10801442.summary: This epitaph records the death of the child Veneriana, specifying her age and that her parents memorialized her.

EDCS-10801454.translation: To Rufo, of good memory, who lived six years and fifteen days, parents to their most sweet son Rufo, of good memory, who lived six years and fifteen days, parents to their most sweet son.
EDCS-10801454.summary: This epitaph is a double inscription for a young boy named Rufo, emphasizing his parents' love and his short lifespan.

EDCS-11400088.translation: A sacred offering to Isis and Serapis: Quintus Fabius Ingenuus, freedman of Titianus, as Augustalis, and Fabia Candida, dedicated with their own money.
EDCS-11400088.summary: This is a religious dedication to Isis and Serapis, made by Quintus Fabius Ingenuus and Fabia Candida, likely in the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-11400096.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Epagatus lived 70 years; he made this threshold, preserving his respect.
EDCS-11400096.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Epagatus at the age of 70 and commemorates his piety.

EDCS-11400097.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Sextus Fabius Celsus lived 29 years, 5 months, and 1 day; his parents and brothers made this in pious devotion.
EDCS-11400097.summary: A funerary inscription for Sextus Fabius Celsus, who died at the age of 29 years and 5 months, erected by his parents and brothers.

EDCS-11400102.translation: If God is for us, who can be against us? Dionisi, may you live in God.
EDCS-11400102.summary: This inscription, likely Christian, invokes divine protection and expresses a wish for eternal life.

EDCS-11400114.translation: Aurelius Annius, son, made this for his father, and Aurelia Ora for her mother, well-deserving.
EDCS-11400114.summary: This is a dedication for parents by their children, Aurelius Annius and Aurelia Ora.

EDCS-11400118.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription mentioning Maria Velania, possibly a funerary dedication or a commemoration.

EDCS-11400121.translation: Rufus made this for the deserving, according to his will, the augur...
EDCS-11400121.summary: This fragment indicates a dedication made by Rufus according to his will, possibly by or for an augur.

EDCS-11400124.translation: Leporius, who lived 40 years and 6 months more or less, departed in peace on the 7th day before the Kalends of August, when Flavius Tatianus and Aurelius Symmachus, most excellent consuls, were in office.
EDCS-11400124.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Leporius, who lived 40 years and 6 months, and provides the consular date of his death to 391 CE.

EDCS-11400129.translation: Tiberius Claudius Caesar Augustus Germanicus, son of Drusus, chief priest, with tribunician power for the 11th time, consul for the 5th time...
EDCS-11400129.summary: This is a fragment of an imperial inscription, likely honoring Emperor Claudius, listing his titles and powers.

EDCS-11400149.translation: Caius Alfidius Chrysantus, freedman of Caius and his wife, lived 11 years.
EDCS-11400149.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Caius Alfidius Chrysantus, who died at the age of 11.

EDCS-11400186.translation: To Gaudentius, a faithful one, of good memory, who lived about 65 years, 3 months, and 10 days; his wife and daughters treated him well.
EDCS-11400186.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Gaudentius, commemorating his life and the affection shown by his family.

EDCS-11400187.translation: Paulus the infant rests here, during the 6th indiction, who lived 3 years, 8 months, and was buried happily on the Kalends of October.
EDCS-11400187.summary: This epitaph records the death and burial of a young child named Paulus, noting the date within the 6th indiction.

EDCS-11400188.translation: To this tomb, of good memory, rests Peregrinus the deacon, in peace, who lived about 50 years, who was buried on the 4th day before the Ides of October in the 15th indiction, ten years after the consulship of the most illustrious consul Bassilus.
EDCS-11400188.summary: This epitaph records the burial of Peregrinus, a deacon, with specific dating information relative to a consulship and indiction.

EDCS-11400189.translation: To Saturninus, of good memory, who lived 60 years, 5 months, and 10 days; his wife, with their sons, treated him well. He departed in peace.
EDCS-11400189.summary: This tomb inscription honors Saturninus, detailing his lifespan and noting the care provided by his wife and sons.

EDCS-11400191.translation: Father and Claudia Ico, mother, made [this] for their most dutiful son.
EDCS-11400191.summary: This is a funerary dedication from parents to their son, likely a tombstone or a memorial plaque.

EDCS-11400198.translation: To the Emperor Nerva Trajan Caesar Augustus Germanicus Dacicus, Quintus Fidubius Alcimus, because of the honor of Augustalitas, which he was the first of all to earn after the Kalends of August from the Senate and the consenting people, he received the bisellium; by decree of the decurions, here, for the same honor, he gave 4,000 sesterces to the Augustales, 2 sesterces to the people individually, and 1 sestertius; by the same decree of the decurions, a place was also given to him, and furthermore, he erected a statue of Emperor Caesar Trajan Augustus.
EDCS-11400198.summary: This inscription commemorates Quintus Fidubius Alcimus's public honors, including receiving the prestigious bisellium and generous donations to the community, granted by the decurions and related to his Augustalitas under Emperor Trajan.

EDCS-11400202.translation: To the Divine Shades. Ave Aufidia Heuresis lived 8 years. Her father made [this]. May the earth lie lightly upon you.
EDCS-11400202.summary: This is a funerary dedication from a father to his young daughter, Aufidia Heuresis, with a common wish for a light earth covering.

EDCS-11400203.translation: To the Divine Shades. Caius Marius Leo lived 33 years. May the earth lie lightly upon you.
EDCS-11400203.summary: This epitaph records the death of Caius Marius Leo, who died at the age of 33, and includes a standard wish for a light earth.

EDCS-11400204.translation: To the Divine Shades. Secundo, Primus and Laudamia made [this] for their most dutiful son. He lived 17 years, 7 months, and 26 days. May the earth lie lightly upon you.
EDCS-11400204.summary: This funerary inscription from parents Primus and Laudamia commemorates their son Secundo, detailing his age at death and expressing a wish for his repose.

EDCS-11400205.translation: To the Divine Shades. Luceso made [this] for his well-deserving brother. He lived 36 years.
EDCS-11400205.summary: This inscription is a dedication by a brother to his deserving deceased brother, Luceso, stating his age at death.

EDCS-11400206.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. Eutropus and Mirallys, parents, [dedicated this to] Valentina, their daughter, who lived 2 years.
EDCS-11400206.summary: A funerary epitaph for a two-year-old girl named Valentina, dedicated by her parents.

EDCS-11400208.translation: To the departed spirits. Maximius Kafon, 12 years, 3 months old. Maximius Kaflius Sal, most devoted parents.
EDCS-11400208.summary: A funerary epitaph for a twelve-year-old boy named Maximius Kafon, with his parents identified.

EDCS-11400209.translation: Quintus Minucius, son of Lucius. Publius Magius, son of Publius Iuncus. As censors, they supervised the construction of the basilica, by decree of the Senate.
EDCS-11400209.summary: An inscription recording the completion of a basilica by two censors, commissioned by a Senate decree.

EDCS-11400210.summary: A dedication by Lucius Titius to someone named Vicia, likely a funerary or votive inscription.

EDCS-11400214.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. To Venviania Zoeni, who lived 60 years, 4 months, [and some days]. Caius Caevius Paeder placed [this] for his well-deserving wife.
EDCS-11400214.summary: A funerary epitaph set up by Caius Caevius Paeder for his wife Venviania Zoeni.

EDCS-11400215.translation: Sacred to Ceres and Vertumna. Bovia Maxima, priestess, member of the college of fifteen, IASAAI.
EDCS-11400215.summary: A religious dedication to Ceres and Vertumna by Bovia Maxima, a priestess and member of a college of fifteen.

EDCS-11400218.translation: Caius Mamius Bassus, son of Sextus. Caius Eppius. A gift to Mefitis Utiana.
EDCS-11400218.summary: A votive offering to the goddess Mefitis Utiana, made by Caius Mamius Bassus and Caius Eppius.

EDCS-11400219.translation: Sacred to Mefitis Utiana. Publius Meneius, son of Caius, and Cnaeus Babullius Restitutus, as a board of four, with their own money.
EDCS-11400219.summary: A religious dedication to Mefitis Utiana funded by two officials, Publius Meneius and Cnaeus Babullius Restitutus.

EDCS-11400222.translation: To the departed spirits. Calpurnius Vaesio, the father, and Maesia Optata, to their well-deserving son, Lucius Calpurnius Faustinus, aedile, quaestor, who lived 25 years, made [this].
EDCS-11400222.summary: A funerary epitaph for Lucius Calpurnius Faustinus, aedile and quaestor, erected by his parents.

EDCS-11400223.translation: To Publius Plaetorius, son of Publius, of the Pomptina tribe. Urso, aedile, a board of four, judge, pontiff, augur. By decree of the decurions, the ministers of the Lares Augusti and the patron were given this place.
EDCS-11400223.summary: A funerary inscription indicating that a plot of land was granted by local decree to Urso, an official and priest, and others.

EDCS-11400224.translation: To the divine spirits of the underworld. Iulia Corinthias placed this for her husband, Marcus Valerius Crescentianus, son of Marcus, of the Pomptina tribe, aedile and one of the four men judging law, who lived 41 years and 10 months, a deserving husband.
EDCS-11400224.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Marcus Valerius Crescentianus, who held various magistracies, set up by his wife.

EDCS-11400226.translation: To the divine spirits of the underworld. His mother placed this for her most unfortunate son, Cnaeus Papirius Claudianus, scribe of the public affairs of the people of Potentia.
EDCS-11400226.summary: A funerary dedication for Cnaeus Papirius Claudianus, a scribe, set up by his mother.

EDCS-11400228.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Numerius Acerronius Puteolanus, with an abbreviation that is not fully clear.

EDCS-11400229.translation: Titus Mettius Potitus lived 18 years. The guild of muleteers and ass-drivers.
EDCS-11400229.summary: This inscription records the age of Titus Mettius Potitus and is associated with the guild of muleteers and ass-drivers.

EDCS-11400230.translation: To the divine spirits of the underworld. For Acerronius.
EDCS-11400230.summary: A short funerary dedication for someone named Acerronius.

EDCS-11400231.translation: To the divine spirits of the underworld. Acerronius Celer for his dearest son, Acerronius.
EDCS-11400231.summary: A funerary dedication by Acerronius Celer for his son, also named Acerronius.

EDCS-11400232.translation: Lucius Afarius Memor placed this for his deserving companion, Mummia Iconis.
EDCS-11400232.summary: A funerary dedication set up by Lucius Afarius Memor for his companion Mummia Iconis.

EDCS-11400234.translation: The wretched mother made this monument for herself and her sons, Annius Rufus, son of Publius, of the Sempronia tribe, and Annius Rufus, son of Publius. She will not be succeeded by an heir.
EDCS-11400234.summary: A funerary monument set up by a mother for herself and her sons, with a clause regarding inheritance.

EDCS-11400235.translation: To the divine spirits of the underworld. Silvinus and Firmilla made this for their deserving son, Apronianus, who lived 6 years.
EDCS-11400235.summary: A funerary dedication for the young Apronianus, set up by his parents.

EDCS-11400236.summary: This appears to be a fragmentary inscription mentioning Anius Bassus and possibly a location or group.

EDCS-11400237.translation: To Gaius Brittius Primigenius, who lived 3 years. Brittius Primigenius [made this monument].
EDCS-11400237.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a child named Gaius Brittius Primigenius, likely set up by his parent with the same name.

EDCS-11400238.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Calpurnius Coluber and Fortunata [set this up] for their son Pomponius, who lived 15 years and 10 days.
EDCS-11400238.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a young man named Pomponius, dedicated by his parents, Calpurnius Coluber and Fortunata.

EDCS-11400239.summary: This is a dedicatory or funerary inscription for Lucius Calpurnius Laetus Faustinus.

EDCS-11400240.summary: This is likely a funerary or dedicatory inscription for Publius Campusius.

EDCS-11400241.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. For Cisatia Polla, who lived 38 years and 9 months, [this monument was set up by] Figelius Atimetus, her husband with whom she lived 27 years and 11 months, and also for Figellia Procula, [her] daughter, to a mother who deserved well.
EDCS-11400241.summary: This funerary inscription commemorates Cisatia Polla and her daughter Figellia Procula, dedicated by her husband Figelius Atimetus, mentioning their long marriage.

EDCS-11400242.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. For Gaudentius, a husband who deserved well, who lived approximately 30 years. His wife Erclania made this.
EDCS-11400242.summary: This funerary inscription honors Gaudentius, who lived about 30 years, and was dedicated by his wife Erclania.

EDCS-11400243.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. For Gavia Prima, who lived 20 years and 2 months. Her mother Amanda made this for her dearest daughter, who deserved well.
EDCS-11400243.summary: This funerary inscription is for Gavia Prima, who died at 20 years and 2 months, dedicated by her grieving mother, Amanda.

EDCS-11400244.translation: Hermes lived. [This is a funerary inscription.]
EDCS-11400244.summary: This brief funerary inscription records the life of an individual named Hermes.

EDCS-11400245.translation: Marcus Insteius Meleager for himself and for his son Marcus Insteius Firmus.
EDCS-11400245.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Marcus Insteius Meleager and his son Marcus Insteius Firmus, likely intended as a family tomb.

EDCS-11400246.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Cornelia Restituta placed [this] for her husband Iulius Claudius Leonidas, who deserved well.
EDCS-11400246.summary: This funerary inscription was dedicated by Cornelia Restituta to her deserving husband, Iulius Claudius Leonidas.

EDCS-11400247.translation: To the Divine Manes. Marcus Appius Primi freedman, for Luxilia, wife of Marcus, his freedwoman, and for Luxilia, wife of Dec, his freedwoman, mother and fellow-soldier, placed this, they who deserved well.
EDCS-11400247.summary: This is a funerary dedication by a freedman for his freedwoman wife and another freedwoman, likely a relative, possibly from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-11400249.translation: To the Divine Manes. Neapolis Potentina lived 1 year and 4 months. Marcus Helvius Acceptus [dedicated this].
EDCS-11400249.summary: A funerary inscription recording the short life of Neapolis Potentina and dedicated by Marcus Helvius Acceptus, likely from the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-11400250.translation: 28th day of the month of August. Nicostratia made this for Veni, her sister, who deserved well.
EDCS-11400250.summary: A funerary dedication made by Nicostratia for her sister Veni, with a specific date noted, possibly from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-11400251.translation: To the Divine Manes. Publius Pletorius Flavus. Pletorius Cres [dedicated this].
EDCS-11400251.summary: A funerary inscription for Publius Pletorius Flavus, with the dedicator likely being Pletorius Cres, possibly from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-11400252.translation: For Pletoria Nigrina, his deserving wife. Annius Restitutus placed this for her and for himself while he was alive.
EDCS-11400252.summary: A funerary dedication set up by Annius Restitutus for his wife Pletoria Nigrina and himself, indicating he planned for his own burial, likely from the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-11400253.translation: To the Divine Manes. For Vatia Potita. For Metius Potitus, her dearest brother.
EDCS-11400253.summary: A funerary inscription dedicated to Vatia Potita, and also mentioning her brother Metius Potitus, likely from the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-11400254.translation: To be made for Thymele, daughter of Damalinus. You owed me.
EDCS-11400254.summary: An inscription suggesting a funerary monument was commissioned or intended, possibly with a note of resentment or obligation, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-11400255.translation: For Numerius Vibius, son of Novius. For Pomptina Flacca, daughter of Publius.
EDCS-11400255.summary: A funerary inscription listing two individuals, Numerius Vibius and Pomptina Flacca, possibly a couple, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE, and mentioning consuls Numerius Vibius Novi and Cossutius Publius.

EDCS-11400256.translation: To the Divine Manes. For Vibina Felicia, who lived 17 years. Vesonia, her mother, placed this for her deserving daughter.
EDCS-11400256.summary: A funerary inscription by a mother, Vesonia, for her 17-year-old daughter Vibina Felicia, likely from the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-11400258.translation: Numerius Vitellius Pacatus, son of N. [arranged for] the making.
EDCS-11400258.summary: A funerary inscription where Numerius Vitellius Pacatus arranged for the monument's construction, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-11400259.translation: To Umbennonia Felicianena, his wife, with whom he lived for 45 years, and to his descendants, he made this.
EDCS-11400259.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated by a husband to his wife and posterity.

EDCS-11400260.translation: She lived for 20 years, 8 months, and 9 days; one day took her life and body. She was cremated and lies in ashes, and her grieving companions placed this last tribute for her amongst the ashes.
EDCS-11400260.summary: This funerary epitaph records the death of a young woman and the sorrow of her companions who cremated her and buried her remains.

EDCS-11400264.translation: Here lies in peace Simplex, named Livania, who lived under the incomparable grace of Paulus Iustus for 13 years, during which neither day nor night found him angry, and she died aged more or less 30 years, on the Ides of July, in the 6th indiction, after the consulship of Mabortius and his colleague; and she forbids on the day of the tremendous judgment anyone ever to dare violate this tomb.
EDCS-11400264.summary: This funerary epitaph identifies the deceased Simplex (Livania), notes her virtuous life, provides her age and date of death, and includes a curse against tomb violators.

EDCS-11400266.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. The patron ordered this made for Bruttio Lupercus, who deserved well.
EDCS-11400266.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by a patron for his deserving freedman, Bruttio Lupercus.

EDCS-11400267.translation: Bruttius Sabinus to his dearest wife, with whom he lived for 25 years, 3 months, and 4 days, who lived for 41 years, 6 months, and 5 days. I made this memorial of piety for an eternal home.
EDCS-11400267.summary: This funerary inscription commemorates Bruttius Sabinus's wife, detailing her lifespan and their years together.

EDCS-11400268.translation: To the Divine Shades. Calpurnius Ursio made this for his deserving mother, Calpurnia Rufina, who lived 41 years and 6 months.
EDCS-11400268.summary: This funerary epitaph records a son's dedication to his deceased mother, including her lifespan.

EDCS-11400270.translation: To the Divine Shades. Clodia Urbica to her dearest son, Titus Helvius Heufemio, who lived 18 years, 3 months, and 7 days.
EDCS-11400270.summary: This funerary inscription is a dedication by a mother, Clodia Urbica, to her deceased son, Titus Helvius Heufemio, noting his age at death.

EDCS-11400271.translation: Quintus Dinius Vemes and Clodia Amicissima, mother and father, to their dearest son, Quintus Dinius Amicissimus, who lived 11 years and 10 months; he rested too late.
EDCS-11400271.summary: This funerary epitaph is a joint dedication by parents to their young son, Quintus Dinius Amicissimus, noting his age at death.

EDCS-11400272.translation: Publia Tertia, daughter of Publius Dirvitius, to herself, and to her father, Publius Dirvitius Silon, son of Publius, and to her mother, Annia, daughter of Quintus.
EDCS-11400272.summary: This is a self-dedicatory funerary inscription that also includes the deceased's parents.

EDCS-11400273.translation: Hercuens and Mimara made this for their most beautiful daughter, Faustae TIM, their dearest daughter.
EDCS-11400273.summary: This funerary inscription is a dedication by parents, Hercuens and Mimara, to their beloved daughter, Faustae.

EDCS-11400275.translation: Fortunatiano Laberius, his caretaker, made this for him, who deserved well.
EDCS-11400275.summary: This is a dedication by Fortunatiano Laberius to his caretaker.

EDCS-11400276.translation: Marcellus made this for him, who deserved well.
EDCS-11400276.summary: This is a dedication by Marcellus, likely to someone who deserved well.

EDCS-11400277.translation: Felicissima made this for her most sweet and incomparable husband Maecius Vitalis, who deserved well, with whom she lived for 25 years, 7 months, and 15 days.
EDCS-11400277.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Maecius Vitalis, set up by his wife Felicissima, with details of their shared life.

EDCS-11400278.translation: Pactumeius Primus made this for his daughter Pactumeia Prima, who lived for 5 years, 12 months, and 4 days.
EDCS-11400278.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Pactumeia Prima, set up by her father Pactumeius Primus, with her age at death.

EDCS-11400279.translation: Bigilia made this for her deserving son Probincio, who lived for 35 years, fulfilling her duty as a mother.
EDCS-11400279.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Probincio, set up by his mother Bigilia, noting her fulfillment of maternal duty.

EDCS-11400280.summary: This inscription identifies the mother of someone named Quarti Lentonis.

EDCS-11400281.translation: Quintus and Siumus made this for their deserving father Quintiliano, who lived for 70 years and 4 months.
EDCS-11400281.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Quintiliano, set up by his sons Quintus and Siumus, with his age at death.

EDCS-11400282.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits. T. Stabilio ordered this to be made for himself from his will, for T. [---]lan, who lived 61 years.
EDCS-11400282.summary: This is a tombstone inscription, set up by T. Stabilio for himself according to his will, for a person named T. [---]lan who lived 61 years.

EDCS-11400283.translation: Vrsulus, the patron, made this for his deserving freedman Hilarianus, who lived for 27 years and [---] months.
EDCS-11400283.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Hilarianus, a freedman, set up by his patron Vrsulus, with his age at death.

EDCS-11400284.translation: Zena made this for her dutiful brother Zenon.
EDCS-11400284.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Zenon, set up by his sister Zena, noting his dutiful nature.

EDCS-11400285.translation: Cimus, freedman of Quintus, and Ionius, freedman of Quintus, his brother, made this.
EDCS-11400285.summary: This is a funerary inscription by two freedmen for themselves, possibly on a tomb or monument.

EDCS-11400290.translation: To Sol Invictus Mithras, Titus Flavius Saturninus, evocatus of our Augusti.
EDCS-11400290.summary: This is a dedication to the god Sol Invictus Mithras by Titus Flavius Saturninus, an evocatus, likely a soldier or former soldier, during the reign of the emperors.

EDCS-11400291.translation: Quintus Vibiedius Philargyrus, minister of the Lares Augustorum and Mercurialis Augustalis, made this stone table and altar to the god Silvanus, fulfilling a vow from a vision, at his own expense.
EDCS-11400291.summary: This is a religious dedication of a table and altar to the god Silvanus by Quintus Vibiedius Philargyrus, who held religious offices, fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-11400297.translation: The people, with money collected, gave this gift to Gaius Passienius, son of Gaius, of the Scaptia tribe, Cossonius Scipio Orfitus, a most distinguished man, augur of the Roman People, admitted among the patricians, a candidate for praetor, curator of the state of the Sutrini, urban quaestor, decemvir for settling lawsuits, and a Roman knight of the sixth turma.
EDCS-11400297.summary: This is a public dedication by the people of Sutrium to Gaius Passienius Cossonius Scipio Orfitus, honoring his distinguished career and public service.

EDCS-11400298.translation: Rullus Festus, a most distinguished man, corrector of Lucania and Bruttium, placed this for the adornment of the baths.
EDCS-11400298.summary: This inscription records Rullus Festus, an official overseeing Lucania and Bruttium, commissioning decorative elements for the baths.

EDCS-11400302.translation: Aurelius Asdula, a soldier of the 5th praetorian cohort, to his well-deserving brother who labored with me for 12 years, and Frunino. He is in the provinces.
EDCS-11400302.summary: This is a funerary inscription by a soldier of the Praetorian Guard for his deceased brother, noting their shared service and the brother's presence in the provinces.

EDCS-11400303.translation: To Publius Titius Ampliatus, freedman of Publius, a cornicen of the 1st Cohors Aticta, his well-deserving comrade, made this, and for himself. He lived 35 years.
EDCS-11400303.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by a comrade for Publius Titius Ampliatus, a cornicen in the Cohors I Aticta, who also made provision for himself.

EDCS-11400305.translation: Gaius Bruttius, son of Gaius, of the Sergia tribe, as aedile acting as quaestor, arranged for 200 feet of wall to be constructed at his own expense, during the consulship of Publius Cornelius and Quintus Caecilius.
EDCS-11400305.summary: This inscription records an aedile, Gaius Bruttius, financing the construction of a wall during a specific consular year.

EDCS-11400306.translation: Sextus Quintus, son of Sextus, of the Poppaediei family, of the Sergia tribe, and Gaius Aebutius, son of Gaius, of the Galeria tribe, as aediles, arranged for 1200 feet of wall to be constructed at their own expense, during the consulship of Servius Sulpicius and Marcus Marcellus.
EDCS-11400306.summary: This inscription records two aediles, Sextus Quintus and Gaius Aebutius, jointly financing the construction of a significant section of wall during a specific consular year.

EDCS-11400307.translation: Quintus Pettius, son of Quintus, of the Tromentina tribe, and Gaius Maecius, son of Gaius, of the Oufentina tribe, as praetors and duoviri, arranged for the construction of baths from public funds by decree of the decurions; Quintus Pettius, son of Quintus, approved it.
EDCS-11400307.summary: This inscription details the construction of public baths, commissioned by two praetors/duoviri and approved by one of them, Quintus Pettius.

EDCS-11400309.translation: To Marcus Aurelius, son of Marcus, of the Pomptina tribe, Felicissimus, a splendid Roman knight.
EDCS-11400309.summary: This is an honorary inscription dedicated to Marcus Aurelius Felicissimus, a Roman knight.

EDCS-11400310.translation: To Manius Otacilius Bassus, son of Manius, of the Pomptina tribe, aedile. He lived 26 years. Manius Otacilius Quintus, son of Manius, of the Pomptina tribe, made this for his most dutiful son.
EDCS-11400310.summary: This funerary inscription records the life and death of Manius Otacilius Bassus, an aedile, and was erected by his father.

EDCS-11400311.translation: Silvinus, aedile. For the people of the mulsum.
EDCS-11400311.summary: This is a brief inscription mentioning Silvinus as an aedile, possibly related to the distribution of mulsum (sweetened wine).

EDCS-11400313.translation: To Gaius Turcius Nebro, son of Gaius, of the Pomptina tribe, aedile, praetor, twice duovir, quaestor. Allidia Nebris, freedwoman of Gaius, his mother, made this for her most dutiful son.
EDCS-11400313.summary: This funerary inscription honors Gaius Turcius Nebro, who held several magistracies, and was erected by his mother.

EDCS-11400315.translation: To [---]tius, son of Quintus, of the Pomptina tribe, decurion. To Aucta, freedwoman of Quintus, his mother. For him, his life was...
EDCS-11400315.summary: This inscription honors a decurion and his mother, with the remaining text indicating a dedication or epitaph.

EDCS-11400316.translation: Lucius Magius Myrtilus and Gaius Opsius Optatus (dedicate this) to Hercules Augustus.
EDCS-11400316.summary: This is a dedication to the god Hercules Augustus, made by Lucius Magius Myrtilus and Gaius Opsius Optatus.

EDCS-11400318.translation: Lucius Turcius Dafnus, Augustalis, Mercurialis, (dedicated this) for himself and for Turcia Attica, his wife.
EDCS-11400318.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by Lucius Turcius Dafnus for himself and his wife, Turcia Attica.

EDCS-11400322.translation: The workshop of Appius Rullus, the workshop of Appius Rullus.
EDCS-11400322.summary: This inscription simply records the name of the workshop belonging to Appius Rullus.

EDCS-11400323.translation: To Gamo, the steward. For Vera, his incomparable wife, with whom he lived 2 years and 4 months. He himself lived 40 years. He made this for her, who deserved well.
EDCS-11400323.summary: This funerary inscription commemorates Vera, the wife of Gamo the steward, and records their lifespans and marriage duration.

EDCS-11400324.translation: To Canius Iudius, his brother. Buscinus, slave of the most distinguished man Lucius Bruttius Crispinus, the manager, made this for him, who deserved well, who lived 40 years and 4 months.
EDCS-11400324.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Canius Iudius and was erected by Buscinus, a slave and manager for Lucius Bruttius Crispinus.

EDCS-11400325.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Luccia Prima made this for her well-deserving son Gnaeus Ampudius Custos.
EDCS-11400325.summary: A funerary dedication by a mother for her son.

EDCS-11400326.translation: To Anneia Secunda, daughter of Publius, as heir according to the will and at the discretion [of the testator].
EDCS-11400326.summary: A dedication by an heir to Anneia Secunda, likely funerary or commemorative, established by a will.

EDCS-11400327.translation: Gaius Annius Rufinus, son of Gaius, of the Pomptina tribe, made this for his brother Gaius Annius Priscus, son of Gaius, of the Pomptina tribe.
EDCS-11400327.summary: A funerary dedication by a brother for his deceased sibling.

EDCS-11400329.translation: S(extus) Aquilius Montanus. Aquilia Ianuaria made this for him as well-deserving.
EDCS-11400329.summary: A funerary dedication by Aquilia Ianuaria for Sextus Aquilius Montanus.

EDCS-11400330.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Aquillia Mumma made this for her most dutiful father Aquillus Prepontis, who lived 70 years.
EDCS-11400330.summary: A funerary dedication by a daughter for her father.

EDCS-11400331.translation: Marcus Artorius Hilarus, freedman of Marcus, for himself and for Marcus Artorius Scindalamus, his patron, freedman of Marcus, and for Artoria [his freedwoman].
EDCS-11400331.summary: A funerary dedication for a freedman, his patron, and a freedwoman, possibly a family group.

EDCS-11400332.translation: For Quintus Attius Restitutus, son of Quintus, of the Curvae [tribe]. His mother Baebia made this for her son, as the son owed to do for his mother, the mother has done for her son.
EDCS-11400332.summary: A funerary dedication by a mother for her son, who had a reciprocal duty of care.

EDCS-11400333.translation: For Auctus, slave of Publius Gavi, who lived 25 years. His mother Posilla made this for her son.
EDCS-11400333.summary: A funerary dedication by a mother for her son, who was a slave.

EDCS-11400334.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. For Aurelia Hermione, her sweetest daughter, who lived 13 years, 7 months, and 9 days. Her father Impetratus erected this for his daughter.
EDCS-11400334.summary: A funerary dedication by a father for his young daughter.

EDCS-11400335.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Bruttius Oriens made this for his well-deserving wife Bruttia Apollonia.
EDCS-11400335.summary: A funerary dedication by a husband for his wife.

EDCS-11400336.translation: To himself and to Tertia, freedwoman of Marcus, daughter of Deutrolius Primogenianus.
EDCS-11400336.summary: This inscription is a dedication by an unknown individual to himself and his freedwoman, Tertia.

EDCS-11400337.translation: Burtzi and Domitianus made this for the well-deserving, who lived 30 years.
EDCS-11400337.summary: This inscription records a dedication made by Burtzi and Domitianus for a deceased individual who lived 30 years.

EDCS-11400338.translation: To the spirits of the underworld: Fabricius Lucanus made this for his well-deserving son Lucius Fabricius Lucanus, who lived 5 years and 3 days.
EDCS-11400338.summary: This is a tombstone inscription by a father, Fabricius Lucanus, for his son Lucius Fabricius Lucanus.

EDCS-11400339.translation: Fortunata and Renatus made this for their well-deserving wife, with whom she lived for years...
EDCS-11400339.summary: This inscription is a dedication from Fortunata and Renatus to a deceased wife and mother, recording her lifespan.

EDCS-11400340.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld: Prote made this for her well-deserving husband Ferullus Fabucius, who lived 33 years and 11 months, with whom she lived 8 years and 8 months.
EDCS-11400340.summary: This is a tombstone inscription by a wife, Prote, for her husband Ferullus Fabucius, detailing their lifespans.

EDCS-11400341.translation: Fortunata made this for her well-deserving son Decimius.
EDCS-11400341.summary: This inscription is a dedication by Fortunata for her son Decimius.

EDCS-11400342.translation: Sacred to the spirits of the underworld: Fundania Gallitana made this for her well-deserving husband Bruttius Maximus, with whom she lived 4 years, and he himself lived 27 years.
EDCS-11400342.summary: This is a tombstone inscription by Fundania Gallitana for her husband Bruttius Maximus, stating their lifespans.

EDCS-11400343.translation: Multasia Aequitas, mother, for her son Gemellus Minicius Crocus, what the son ought to have made for his mother; he lived 15 years.
EDCS-11400343.summary: This inscription is a posthumous dedication by a mother, Multasia Aequitas, for her son Gemellus Minicius Crocus.

EDCS-11400344.translation: For Geminus, a most faithful and incomparable sweetest son, well-deserving, Geminus and Victorina made this; he lived 4 years, 9 months, and 18 days.
EDCS-11400344.summary: This tombstone inscription is from parents, Geminus and Victorina, for their young son Geminus.

EDCS-11400345.translation: Publius Lapillanus Phi; the heirs of Lapillana, by the judgment of...
EDCS-11400345.summary: This inscription seems to concern the property or burial of Publius Lapillanus Phi, managed by the heirs of Lapillana.

EDCS-11400346.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. His colleagues and brothers made this for Liberalis, who lived 40 years and 5 months, a deserving man.
EDCS-11400346.summary: A funerary dedication for Liberalis, made by his colleagues and brothers.

EDCS-11400347.translation: Lucius Magius Myrtilus willingly made this.
EDCS-11400347.summary: A dedication made by Lucius Magius Myrtilus, likely a tombstone or offering.

EDCS-11400348.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. His father and Arria, his mother, made this for their deserving son, who lived 18 years.
EDCS-11400348.summary: A funerary monument for a son, erected by his parents.

EDCS-11400349.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Papiria Stabilita made this for her deserving son Numerius, who lived 18 years and six months.
EDCS-11400349.summary: A funerary dedication by Papiria Stabilita for her son Numerius.

EDCS-11400350.translation: For Philargyrus, slave of Marus Bassus.
EDCS-11400350.summary: A dedication for a slave named Philargyrus, owned by Marus Bassus.

EDCS-11400351.translation: Made for his deserving wife, who lived 30 years.
EDCS-11400351.summary: A funerary dedication for a wife, made by her husband.

EDCS-11400352.summary: An inscription possibly related to a construction project, mentioning Gnaeus Pin.

EDCS-11400353.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Pinarius Callitanus made this for his deserving daughter Pinaria Marcella, who lived 30 years.
EDCS-11400353.summary: A funerary monument for Pinaria Marcella, erected by her father Pinarius Callitanus.

EDCS-11400354.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Quintilianus the father made this memorial for his deserving son Quintilius, from the ranks of the equites of the Sixth Dalmatian cohort, who lived 31 years.
EDCS-11400354.summary: A funerary monument for Quintilius, a member of the equestrian order and the Sixth Dalmatian cohort, erected by his father.

EDCS-11400356.translation: Stabilita made this for her deserving mother Agilena, who lived 50 years.
EDCS-11400356.summary: A funerary dedication by Stabilita for her mother Agilena.

EDCS-11400357.translation: To Montanus, freedman of Gaius, son of Tertia, freedwoman of Tarula.
EDCS-11400357.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Montanus, a freedman.

EDCS-11400358.summary: This is a funerary epitaph fragment for Lurchilla.

EDCS-11400359.translation: To Chionissa, freedwoman of Publius, wife of Titus.
EDCS-11400359.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Chionissa, a freedwoman.

EDCS-11400360.translation: Philelma, freedwoman of Cnaeus, lived 25 years. Cnaeus Vettius Anteros, a fellow freedman, had this made at his own expense.
EDCS-11400360.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Philelma, a freedwoman, funded by a fellow freedman.

EDCS-11400361.translation: Aria, freedwoman of Decimus, made this for herself and for her deserving husband Gaius Avidius Paederos.
EDCS-11400361.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Aria and her husband, commissioned by Aria.

EDCS-11400362.translation: Vivedia Silvana made this for her deserving husband Titus Vivedius Velicus, with whom she lived 16 years.
EDCS-11400362.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Titus Vivedius Velicus, funded by his wife.

EDCS-11400363.translation: Praetumeus Chrestillus made this for his deserving wife Lucilla, who lived 40 years.
EDCS-11400363.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucilla, funded by her husband.

EDCS-11400364.translation: For the divine spirits of Henia, mother Felicao and Octabiana, who deserved well. They made this.
EDCS-11400364.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Henia, Felicao, and Octabiana.

EDCS-11400375.translation: Decumanus, son of Gaius; Gaius Sempronius, son of Tiberius; Appius Claudius, son of Gaius; Publius Licinius, son of Publius, three-men board for judging and assigning lands, cardo V.
EDCS-11400375.summary: This inscription lists members of a commission (III viri) responsible for land distribution.

EDCS-11400377.translation: Marcus, son of Niger, quaestor, contracted for the repair of seven small chapels, according to the decree of the decurions, using money from those listed below: [amounts specified]... Lucius Gaius, son of Trebius, [amount specified]... Marcus Satrius, son of Numerius, [amount specified]... Lucius Oppius, son of Marcus Birbatus, [amount specified]... Lucius Decumius, son of Lucius Aprius, [amount specified]... Lucius Attius, son of Gaius, [amount specified]... Gaius Lucretius, son of Marcus, [amount specified]... Marcus Aesquillius, son of Paquius Rufus, [amount specified]... Sextus Teltonius, son of Lucius Stichus, [amount specified].
EDCS-11400377.summary: This inscription records the contract for repairing public chapels, funded by a quaestor and several individuals, likely local officials or wealthy citizens.

EDCS-11400378.translation: Marcus Minatius Sabinus, son of Marcus, of the Pomptina tribe, undertook the construction of a tower with his own funds and a wall with contributed funds, and he approved it.
EDCS-11400378.summary: This inscription records a private individual, Marcus Minatius Sabinus, who funded and oversaw the construction of a tower and a wall.

EDCS-11400391.translation: To the spirits of the underworld: [His] mother Luc made [this] for herself for Marcella.
EDCS-11400391.summary: This is a funerary dedication from a mother, Luc, to her deceased daughter, Marcella, paid for by the mother.

EDCS-11400396.translation: To the spirits of the underworld: Irpinia Avia made [this] for her dearest son, Gaius Buculeius Pontorus, son of Gaius, who lived for 13 years, 11 months, and 20 days; oh, wretched mother that I am, I could not bring you to the honors, you suddenly deceived me, leaving me, miserable and desolate.
EDCS-11400396.summary: This is a funerary epitaph from a mother, Irpinia Avia, to her young son, Gaius Buculeius Pontorus, expressing grief over his premature death.

EDCS-11400413.translation: Anicia Coma made [this] for her well-deserving son, Cominus, who lived for 8 years, 3 months, and 4 hours, buried on the third day before the Kalends of January.
EDCS-11400413.summary: This is a funerary epitaph from a mother, Anicia Coma, for her son Cominus, also recording his age and date of burial.

EDCS-11400417.translation: Carus willingly dedicates this sacred offering to the household gods, as is deserved.
EDCS-11400417.summary: This is a dedication of a sacred offering to the household gods (Lares) by an individual named Carus.

EDCS-11400444.translation: To Publius Magnus, son of F., wretched.
EDCS-11400444.summary: This is a very brief inscription, likely a tombstone, commemorating a deceased individual named Publius Magnus.

EDCS-11400455.translation: To the spirits of the underworld: The associates of Marcus Valerius Horus.
EDCS-11400455.summary: This funerary inscription records that associates (sodales) dedicated something to Marcus Valerius Horus.

EDCS-11400472.translation: Lucius Manneius, son of Quintus, the physician, made [this] while alive. By nature, Menekrates Demetriou of Tralles, the physician and wine-giver, made [this] while alive. Maxsuma Sadria, daughter of Spurius, good, respectable, thrifty, greetings.
EDCS-11400472.summary: This inscription is complex, featuring funerary sentiments for Lucius Manneius, a physician, and a Greek inscription for Menekrates, also a physician and wine-giver, possibly indicating a shared burial or monument, along with a greeting to Maxsuma Sadria.

EDCS-11400484.summary: This is a dedication or memorial for Iulia Celerina.

EDCS-11400517.translation: To the spirits of the underworld: Marcus Arrius Marcellinus, son of Marcus, of the Pomptina tribe, quinquennial duovir, son of Marcus Arrius Marcellinus, son of Marcus, quinquennial duovir of Potentia, to his dearest son, who lived 38 years. Marcus Arrius Marcellinus, son of Marcus, of the Pomptina tribe, quinquennial duovir of Potentia.
EDCS-11400517.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Marcus Arrius Marcellinus, son of Marcus, a quinquennial duovir, and is dedicated by his father of the same name and office.

EDCS-11400541.translation: He lived more or less [X] years, buried on the 8th day of the 3rd indiction, under the consulship of the most distinguished Flavius Justinus.
EDCS-11400541.summary: This inscription records the burial of an individual during the consulship of Flavius Justinus, likely from the 6th century CE.

EDCS-11400550.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Lucius Valerius Susceptus, son of Marcus, lived 40 years, [no days]. Titus Cominius Susceptus and Publilia Andrea [placed this] for their dearest son.
EDCS-11400550.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Valerius Susceptus, dedicated by his parents, Titus Cominius Susceptus and Publilia Andrea.

EDCS-11400551.summary: This is a dedication to the goddess Ceres by Voconia Severa.

EDCS-11400581.translation: Aulus Scalponius, freedman of Pacius, of the Quirina tribe.
EDCS-11400581.summary: This inscription records the name and tribal affiliation of Aulus Scalponius, a freedman.

EDCS-11400585.translation: Ovius [son of] Caisis, Ovius Trebius, [son of] Platorius Trebius.
EDCS-11400585.summary: This inscription seems to record the names and patronymic/filial relationships of at least two individuals, possibly Ovius and Ovius Trebius.

EDCS-11400587.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by Lucius Villius for himself during his lifetime.

EDCS-11400588.summary: This inscription simply records the name Marcus Afarius Ampliatus, possibly an epitaph or a dedication.

EDCS-11400590.summary: This inscription likely records a numerical increase or growth, possibly related to an economic or agricultural context.

EDCS-11400591.translation: To the Divine Shades. Salbius, [her] father, well-deserving, placed [this] for Successus. Potiolana, [his] wicked mother, [placed this] for [her] son Salbius.
EDCS-11400591.summary: This complex funerary epitaph records the death of Salbius, dedicated by his mother Potiolana, who also refers to herself negatively in relation to her son.

EDCS-11600033.translation: To Gaius Allidius Choroebus, magistrate of the Augustales of Herculaneum, for himself and for Eppia Rhodina, his companion.
EDCS-11600033.summary: This inscription is a dedication by Gaius Allidius Choroebus, a magistrate of the Augustales at Herculaneum, for himself and his companion Eppia Rhodina.

EDCS-11600034.translation: To the deified Severus, by public decree.
EDCS-11600034.summary: This inscription is a public dedication to the deified emperor Severus, likely dating to the period after his death.

EDCS-11600035.translation: To Lucius Saturius, legate; to Bruttia, daughter of Publius; to Lucius Saturius, son of Lucius; to Saturia, daughter of Lucius. B.
EDCS-11600035.summary: This is a funerary inscription for several individuals named Lucius Saturius and Bruttia and Saturia, likely family members, with a reference to a legate.

EDCS-11600036.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Sabidius the actor was buried here, who lived 38 years, 8 months, 10 days.
EDCS-11600036.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Sabidius, an actor, providing his age at death, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11600038.translation: To the spirits of the departed. To Junius the nurse, incomparable, who lived 17 years, 11 months, 12 days. Pollux and Speudusa, [slaves] of Bruttius Crispinus.
EDCS-11600038.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a young individual named Junius, who lived 17 years, and was commemorated by Pollux and Speudusa, slaves of Bruttius Crispinus.

EDCS-11600039.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Minatius Campanus made [this] for his wife Helvia Asterope and his brother Mamius Amandus, well-deserving. She lived 25 years.
EDCS-11600039.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Minatius Campanus for his wife Helvia Asterope and brother Mamius Amandus, recording the wife's lifespan.

EDCS-11600040.translation: To the spirits of the departed. To Ianuarius Passienus Licinianus, slave of Passienia.
EDCS-11600040.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Ianuarius Passienus Licinianus, identified as a slave belonging to Passienia.

EDCS-11600048.translation: Eperastus made [this] for Titius Stasius Culius.
EDCS-11600048.summary: This inscription records that Eperastus made a monument for Titius Stasius Culius.

EDCS-11600049.summary: This is a simple inscription identifying Meniscus as the son of Aulus Vibius, possibly on a tombstone or property marker.

EDCS-12800162.summary: This inscription identifies Apronius as a freedman.

EDCS-12800164.translation: Gnaeus Cornelius Marcellinus, consul, and Marcus Aquilius, propraetor of Sicily, by decree of the Senate.
EDCS-12800164.summary: This inscription records an action or decree undertaken by the consul Gnaeus Cornelius Marcellinus and the propraetor Marcus Aquilius in Sicily, acting on a senatorial decision.

EDCS-13302662.translation: The Senate and the people of Veli (honored) Gaius Iulius Nason, son of Gaius, for his excellence and good deeds.
EDCS-13302662.summary: This inscription is a public honorific monument from the Velians honoring Gaius Iulius Nason for his merits.

EDCS-13600406.translation: Titus Annius, son of Titus, praetor, (set this up) for 260 (years/units).
EDCS-13600406.summary: This inscription records Titus Annius, son of Titus, who held the office of praetor, with an unclear numerical designation possibly related to time or units.

EDCS-13900339.translation: Lucius Decimius Secundio made the grade of the road at his own expense.
EDCS-13900339.summary: This is a private dedication by Lucius Decimius Secundio for the construction of a road grade at his own expense.

EDCS-13900589.translation: I, the grandfather, set this up for my well-deserving granddaughter who lived for 3 years.
EDCS-13900589.summary: This private epitaph records a grandfather setting up a memorial for his granddaughter who died at the age of three.

EDCS-15700022.translation: The board of four men, quinquennial officials, took care that this (was made) for Jupiter Best and Greatest, by decree of the Senate, and they approved it.
EDCS-15700022.summary: This inscription records a public works project commissioned by the quinquennial officials for Jupiter Optimus Maximus, authorized by the Senate.

EDCS-16100247.translation: To Quintus Maecius Valentinus of Salona, his friend Felix, who deserved well.
EDCS-16100247.summary: This is a private dedication from Felix to his friend Quintus Maecius Valentinus of Salona, expressing goodwill.

EDCS-16100248.translation: To the Divine Shades. Hedistes lived 13 years, 5 months. Bithus and Successa, her parents, set this up for their most dutiful daughter; the provincials arranged for the erection of this (monument) for their dearest comrade.
EDCS-16100248.summary: This epitaph records the death of Hedistes at a young age and was erected by her parents and provincial companions.

EDCS-16300245.translation: Amethus, slave and also colonus of our Caesar, lived 52 years, 2 months. Olimpias set this up with her son for her deserving husband; he is buried here.
EDCS-16300245.summary: This epitaph records the life of Amethus, a slave and colonus of Caesar, and was erected by his wife Olimpias and son.

EDCS-16800413.translation: Publius Titius Nicephor, freedman of Publius, Mercurial Augustan magistrate, for himself and for Marcus Picacilius Philargyrus, freedman of the woman, Mercurial Augustan magistrate, and for Titia Philemation, freedwoman of Publius, his mother.
EDCS-16800413.summary: This is a funerary inscription setting up a monument for the dedicator, his associate, and his mother, all holding positions as Mercurial Augustan magistrates.

EDCS-20100263.translation: Gaius Sempronius, son of Tiberius; Appius Claudius, son of Gaius; Publius Licinius, son of Publius, the board of three men for judging and assigning lands, Cardo VII.
EDCS-20100263.summary: This inscription records the names of a board of three men responsible for land allocation, possibly related to a specific administrative division (Cardo VII).

EDCS-21800411.translation: To our lords Valentinian and Valens, Augusti, beneficial to the state.
EDCS-21800411.summary: This is a dedication to the emperors Valentinian and Valens, likely from the late Roman period.

EDCS-21900272.translation: Trypho and Mercurius made this for their mother Irenene.
EDCS-21900272.summary: A funerary dedication made by Trypho and Mercurius for their mother, Irenene.

EDCS-21900273.translation: To the spirits of the dead. Claudia Laetina made this for Tiberius Claudius Africanus, who lived 5 years, 8 months, and 25 days, a well-deserving freedman.
EDCS-21900273.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Tiberius Claudius Africanus, set up by his freedwoman Claudia Laetina.

EDCS-21900274.translation: To the spirits of the dead. Hermes made this for Helena, aged 3 years and 6 months, his dearest daughter, and for his most cherished wife, Ampeledus.
EDCS-21900274.summary: A funerary epitaph for Helena and Ampeledus, set up by Hermes, presumably their husband and father.

EDCS-22500818.translation: Of Lepida, wife of Marcus Silanus.
EDCS-22500818.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Lepida, wife of Marcus Silanus.

EDCS-22500821.translation: During the reign of our lord Theoderic, the good ruler of Rome.
EDCS-22500821.summary: This inscription records a date during the reign of Theoderic, the Ostrogothic king of Italy.

EDCS-22500823.summary: This inscription appears to record a quantity of 100 marks associated with the name Marcian, possibly related to a transaction or measurement.

EDCS-22500831.summary: This inscription appears to record a quantity of 100 marks associated with the name Marcian, possibly related to a transaction or measurement.

EDCS-22500833.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Marcus Camillus Vitalis.

EDCS-22500837.summary: This inscription identifies Faustus as the son of Titus Nonius.

EDCS-22500839.summary: This is a funerary inscription identifying the deceased as Felix, son of Lucius Titus.

EDCS-22500841.summary: This is likely a dedication or funerary inscription naming Gaius Julius of Brundisium.

EDCS-22500844.summary: This inscription likely records a dedication or names individuals, Lepida and Agrippina.

EDCS-22500845.translation: Of Lepida, wife of Marcus Silanus.
EDCS-22500845.summary: This inscription likely records a dedication or names Lepida, wife of Marcus Silanus.

EDCS-22500851.summary: This inscription likely records a dedication or names Gaius Numisius Faustus.

EDCS-22500857.summary: This inscription likely records a dedication or names Pamphilus, freedman of Caerellius.

EDCS-22500860.summary: This is likely a funerary inscription identifying the deceased as Sphaerus, a slave belonging to Nonius.

EDCS-22500863.summary: This inscription likely records a dedication or identifies Publicus, possibly related to Gaius Staius Rufus.

EDCS-22500865.translation: Marcus Tuccius, son of Lucius, of the Tromentina tribe, called Caponus.
EDCS-22500865.summary: This inscription is a full Roman name identifying Marcus Tuccius Caponus, son of Lucius, and member of the Tromentina tribe.

EDCS-22500876.summary: This inscription likely records a dedication or refers to a freedman of the emperor Augustus.

EDCS-22900569.summary: This is a personal name, likely an owner or addressee on a monument.

EDCS-22900585.summary: This is a genitive personal name, indicating possession or origin, likely on a monument related to Gaius Iunius Draco.

EDCS-22902069.summary: This is a genitive personal name, indicating possession or origin, likely on a monument related to Gaius Cornelius Ursus.

EDCS-23000005.summary: This is a genitive personal name, indicating possession or origin, likely on a monument related to Lucius Tettius Samias.

EDCS-23000060.summary: This inscription appears to record a name, possibly Hilario, with a cognomen or family name fragment, suggesting ownership or dedication.

EDCS-23000102.summary: This is a genitive personal name, indicating possession or origin, likely on a monument related to Lucius Tettius Samias.

EDCS-23000103.summary: This is a genitive personal name, indicating possession or origin, likely on a monument related to Lucius Rasinius Pisanus.

EDCS-23000207.summary: This inscription identifies Aulus Titius by name and profession as a potter, likely related to a funerary monument or workshop.

EDCS-23000209.translation: Of Priamus, son of Aulus Sestius
EDCS-23000209.summary: This inscription identifies Priamus and his father Aulus Sestius, likely for a funerary monument or a record of lineage.

EDCS-23000212.summary: This is a genitive personal name, indicating possession or origin, likely on a monument related to Lucius Tettius Samias.

EDCS-23000215.summary: This is a funerary inscription honoring Publius, son of Publius.

EDCS-23000222.summary: This is a dedication to Blandus by Statilia.

EDCS-23300014.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Quintus Vocontius Pollio Victor.

EDCS-23300056.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Titus Aurelius Felix.

EDCS-23300057.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Gaius Numisius Cleans.

EDCS-23300059.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Marcus Vipsanius Amerimnus.

EDCS-23300060.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Vitellius Lucius Clemens.

EDCS-23400011.translation: To Caturia, from the workshop of Celer.
EDCS-23400011.summary: This is a dedication to Caturia, likely from a craftsman named Celer.

EDCS-23400012.translation: Sacred to a good memory. Hirene, faithful in Jesus Christ, who lived 65 years, 8 months, and 10 days. Her husband, who did good for her, preceded her, laid to rest in peace on the 14th day before the Kalends of May, who was the conductor of the Trapezian estate.
EDCS-23400012.summary: This is a Christian funerary inscription for Hirene, who died on April 18th and managed a property known as the Trapezian estate.

EDCS-23400013.translation: Sacred to the good memory of Hirenis the faithful, who lived 40 years, 8 months, and 9 days; her husband and sons did well for her; she departed in peace.
EDCS-23400013.summary: This epitaph records the death of Hirenis, with her husband and sons as dedicators, likely from the late Roman period.

EDCS-23400014.translation: To the good memory of Fortunula, who lived about 60 years; her daughter and husband did well for her.
EDCS-23400014.summary: This epitaph commemorates Fortunula, with her daughter and husband as dedicators, likely from the late Roman period.

EDCS-23400015.translation: Sacred to the good memory of Leta the presbytera, who lived 40 years, 8 months, and 9 days; her husband did well for her; she departed in peace on the Ides of May.
EDCS-23400015.summary: This epitaph records the death of Leta, a presbytera, with her husband as dedicator, likely from the late Roman period.

EDCS-23400016.translation: Sacred to the good memory of Monses the presbyter, who lived 60 years, 8 months, and 9 days; his sons did well for him; he departed in peace on the Kalends of December.
EDCS-23400016.summary: This epitaph records the death of Monses, a presbyter, with his sons as dedicators, likely from the late Roman period.

EDCS-23400017.translation: Sacred to the good memory of Paternus, who lived 40 years, 5 months, and 18 days; his own brother did well for him.
EDCS-23400017.summary: This epitaph records the death of Paternus, with his brother as dedicator, likely from the late Roman period.

EDCS-23400018.translation: To the good memory of Primitiva, who departed on the third day before the Ides of January, aged about 50 years; her sons did well for her.
EDCS-23400018.summary: This epitaph commemorates Primitiva, with her sons as dedicators, likely from the late Roman period.

EDCS-23400020.translation: Sacred to the departed spirits; Hail Copia Successa.
EDCS-23400020.summary: This is a short epitaph invoking the departed spirits for Copia Successa, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-23400027.translation: To the departed spirits. Sabia Marciane lived 50 years; Magius Felicio made this for his well-deserving wife.
EDCS-23400027.summary: This epitaph records the death of Sabia Marciane, with her husband Magius Felicio as dedicator, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-23400029.translation: To the departed spirits. Mart lived 60 years; the collegium, presided over by SOD, [made this?].
EDCS-23400029.summary: This epitaph records the death of Mart, with the collegium as dedicator, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-23400030.translation: io verna lived 36 years; Felicula made this for her well-deserving fellow slave.
EDCS-23400030.summary: This epitaph records the death of io verna, with Felicula as dedicator, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-23400031.translation: To the spirits of the departed Arrius son of Titus.
EDCS-23400031.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Arrius son of Titus, honoring the deceased.

EDCS-23400032.translation: To Marcus Aurelius Clyminus, a father who lived 72 years; his son Aurelius Clyminus made this for him deserving of merit.
EDCS-23400032.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by a son for his father, Marcus Aurelius Clyminus, who lived 72 years.

EDCS-23400033.translation: Claudia Marcella made this for her husband Julius Hermogenes, deserving of merit, who lived 40 years. She lived 50 years.
EDCS-23400033.summary: This epitaph records the death of Julius Hermogenes, husband of Claudia Marcella, and provides their ages at death.

EDCS-23400035.translation: To the spirits of the departed Helion. His parents, Helion the father and Hilaria the mother, made this for their son who lived 4 years and 2 months.
EDCS-23400035.summary: This is a tombstone inscription set up by parents for their young son Helion, who died at the age of 4 years and 2 months.

EDCS-23400494.translation: Neri lived 80 years and 4 months. Asyll made this for his dearest father.
EDCS-23400494.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Asyll for his father Neri, who lived 80 years and 4 months.
