EDCS-42500115.translation: Parmenides Pyretos Ouliades, the natural philosopher.
EDCS-42500115.summary: This inscription identifies Parmenides Pyretos Ouliades as a natural philosopher, likely a gravestone or a dedication by the individual himself.

EDCS-44800208.summary: This inscription appears to be a very fragmentary dedication or name listing, possibly for Caius A.

EDCS-44800299.translation: Nius A. O. nus Quintus G. us Quintus G. dus Caius ius Marcus us Tiberius Iu Quintus Ac Marcus Ca. Marcus A. Quintus Lucius Lucius Di. Titus Be. Caius Eb. Quintus Ceppius Valerius Gene. Marcus Iulius Sexti. Publius Loteius Epaphroditus. Caius Cassius Zosimus.
EDCS-44800299.summary: This inscription is a complex list of Roman names, possibly from a funerary monument or a record of citizenship, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-44800300.translation: To Petronius, from Athenonice, his wife (?) of the third order.
EDCS-44800300.summary: This inscription is a dedication to a Petronius by Athenonice, likely his wife, possibly indicating a social or religious status for her, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-44800309.summary: This inscription is a simple name, likely a dedication or epitaph for Quintus Greanius.

EDCS-44800310.summary: This inscription consists of two fragmented names, Cnaeus Co. and Lucius Ca., possibly part of a larger dedication or list.

EDCS-44800312.summary: This inscription contains two fragmented names, Caius T. and Marcus C., likely part of a dedication or epitaph.

EDCS-44800348.translation: To Cnaeus Pompeius, freedman of Cnaeus, of Castor and Pollux.
EDCS-44800348.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Cnaeus Pompeius, a freedman of Cnaeus, possibly associated with the cult of Castor and Pollux, dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-44800362.summary: This inscription indicates a group of priests, the flamines Augustales, likely from a public building or a dedication related to the imperial cult.

EDCS-44800375.translation: ] to Augustus [unknown] / [unknown] and Getae [unknown] / [unknown] Titus Flavius Philippus(?).
EDCS-44800375.summary: This fragmentary inscription is likely a dedication to imperial figures and Geta, with Titus Flavius Philippus possibly named as a dedicator or official.

EDCS-44800388.translation: Under the consulship of Publius Caius and Gaius, by decree of the town councillors, with public funds.
EDCS-44800388.summary: This inscription records a public works project funded by the town council, likely dating to the Imperial period given the consular dating formula.

EDCS-45300153.translation: Publius Claudius, son of Caius, and Gaius Sextilius, son of Lucius, as duovirs, by decision of the senate.
EDCS-45300153.summary: This inscription records the names and office of two duovirs, Publius Claudius and Gaius Sextilius, appointed by senatorial decree.

EDCS-47300123.summary: This inscription likely records the filiation (parentage) of individuals, identifying them as sons of Titius Cornelius.

EDCS-47300125.summary: This inscription appears to be a dedication or ownership marker belonging to Vagellius Marcianus.

EDCS-51200118.translation: Greetings, Egloga Fabricia, sweet little bee, and farewell; you lived 8 years. Fabricia Quarta, excellent woman, may you rest well. Lived by Lucius Fabricius Anteros, Lucius Fabricius Anthus.
EDCS-51200118.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a young girl named Egloga Fabricia, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period, which also records the names of those who erected the monument.

EDCS-53600201.translation: Of Lucius Gellius, son of Lucius, and Lucius Sempronius.
EDCS-53600201.summary: This inscription lists the names and filiations of two individuals, Lucius Gellius and Lucius Sempronius.

EDCS-53600229.translation: Of Lucius Rasius, son of Piso.
EDCS-53600229.summary: This inscription records the name and filiation of Lucius Rasius, son of Piso.

EDCS-53600231.summary: This inscription records the name of Lucius Titus Thyrsus.

EDCS-53701554.translation: May the angel Gabriel, who protects you, give judgment and your justice to Romuald, duke, Gunperga, king, and your son, king.
EDCS-53701554.summary: This inscription appears to be a religious or protective invocation, possibly related to a legal or judicial context, directed towards several named individuals including dukes and kings, likely from a medieval period.

EDCS-55702391.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription mentioning the name Cornelius, likely a Roman cognomen or nomen gentilicium, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-56500283.summary: This inscription is a simple dedication naming Caius Bruttius Praesens.

EDCS-56500284.summary: This inscription is a simple dedication naming Caius Bruttius Praesens.

EDCS-56500293.translation: Felicia made this for her well-deserving father; she lived 40 years.
EDCS-56500293.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a father, erected by his daughter Felicia, who also records her own lifespan.

EDCS-56500294.summary: This is a dedication to Augusta Moderata.

EDCS-57000025.translation: To Augustus Hadrian Augustus, by decree of the town council.
EDCS-57000025.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Emperor Hadrian (Augustus) made by a local town council.

EDCS-57000036.translation: L. L. repaired the gates, rebuilt and covered them.
EDCS-57000036.summary: This inscription records the repair and rebuilding of gates by an individual or individuals identified by the initials L. L.

EDCS-57000038.translation: Lucius Vinicius, son of Caius, and his associate.
EDCS-57000038.summary: This inscription appears to be a fragmentary dedication or legal statement involving Lucius Vinicius and Caius.

EDCS-61000041.summary: This is a fragmentary epitaph recording the name and age of Lucullus, indicating he lived 22 years.

EDCS-61000042.summary: This inscription is a standard Roman naming formula, identifying Marcus Apuscius as the son of Marcus.

EDCS-61000044.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Lucius Atilius Parthenius.
EDCS-61000044.summary: This is a funerary dedication ('Dis Manibus') for Lucius Atilius Parthenius.

EDCS-62501258.translation: Gaius Fulonius Verus, son of Quintus.
EDCS-62501258.summary: This is a name inscription, likely from a funerary monument, for Gaius Fulonius Verus.

EDCS-62900238.translation: To Furia Faustina, his mother-in-law, Furius Rufininus, for her well-deserving. She lived 70 years.
EDCS-62900238.summary: This is a funerary dedication from Furius Rufininus to his mother-in-law, Furia Faustina, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-63000029.translation: Under Menalkes, the city used, by decree of the council and people, from the god, for the community, the king, from the year of Menalkes, month of Apellaios, talents, staters, pounds, ounces, and from the Boukatian fund, talents, and from the Athanaios fund, talents, pounds, and from the Dionysios fund, talents, staters, pounds, ounces, and from the Damatrios fund, talents, staters, pounds, ounces, and from the Panamion fund, talents, staters, pounds, ounces. Total of the loan: talents, staters, pounds, ounce.
EDCS-63000029.summary: This inscription records a financial transaction by the city, likely related to a loan or expenditure, overseen by various officials, with sums of money accounted in talents, staters, pounds, and ounces, during the year of Menalkes and month of Apellaios, possibly in the Hellenistic or Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-63000030.translation: Under Charixenus, the hieromnamons holding office, for the treasury, Thra Eukleidas, Thraso, Tiw Protohenes, Ameinokritos, Phawo Kallippos, Aristippos, proboloi; Oumb Theron, Arkesilas, Mna Thestoris, Amynandros, Log Agathocles, Agathola, prodikoi; Anx Aineas, Aineidas, Sowt Formio, Zoippos, Log Philostratus, Phinton, the city used, by decree of the council and people, from the god, the first installment, talents, and from the council and people, talents, and the second, by decree of the council, talents, and from the people, talents, staters, talents, staters, and the third, by decree of the council, staters, pounds, and from the people, talents, staters, pounds, pounds, and from the fourth, by decree of the council and people, talents, total: talents, staters, pounds.
EDCS-63000030.summary: This inscription details financial accounts and officials of the city, recording multiple installments of funds used for unspecified purposes, likely related to public works or religious festivals, overseen by various magistrates, under the year of Charixenus.

EDCS-63000031.translation: Under Neaithon, proboloi, presiding, Psath Satyros, Aristokritos, Tiw Ameinokritos, Protohenes, Ank Onaios, Zoiilos, prodikoi; Kob Eucholas, Aristeos, Kra Chairelas, Chairedamos, Str Archippos, Eukeladas, hieromnamones, for the treasury, Thra Phinton, Herakleitos, Kra Gniphon, Kalinos, Pyr Eukamides, Philonis, wall builders; Lak Philippos, Philakos, Tiw Euphroniskos, Lyson, Gag Samion, Hieros, with these we used for the construction of the tower for the god, talents, staters, ounces, overseers Ska Alkias, Alkimus, Menedamos, Ekekrates, for these, other talents, by decree of the council and people.
EDCS-63000031.summary: This inscription lists various officials, including proboloi, prodikoi, hieromnamones, and specific craftsmen like wall builders, involved in a construction project ('tower building') for the god, detailing financial expenditures in talents, staters, and ounces, under the presidency of Neaithon.

EDCS-63000032.translation: Under Euphrainetos, proboloi, presiding, Gaps Diogenes, Agathocles, Dys Euthymos, Philistos, Alch Socrates, Philippos, prodikoi; Thra Eufron, Sauronos, Dys Dorkion, Euphroniskos, Pet Herakleitos, Eufron, it seemed good to the council and the people that the hieromnamones in bronze write the loan of Tel upon the arrival of Euthymidas for the grain, the collected tribute, the price not paid by the archons of Phawo, in the year of Neodamos, talents, talents, staters.
EDCS-63000032.summary: This decree orders that a financial transaction concerning grain and tribute, specifically an unpaid price, be recorded in bronze by the hieromnamones, under the authority of the council and people, during the archonship of Neodamos and Euphrainetos, with sums recorded in talents and staters.

EDCS-63000033.translation: Under Euphrainetos, proboloi, presiding, Gaps Diogenes, Agathocles, Dys Euthymos, Philistos, Alch Socrates, Philippos, hieromnamones for the grain; Oumb Eugenidas, Philokrates, Kyl Soton, Sosichares, Ank Deinarchos, Charripos, under these, it seemed good to the council and the people that the hieromnamones for the grain write the remainder of the price of the wheat and the vetch, the price for the wheat: talents, for the vetch: talents, staters, pounds, ounces. Total: talents, staters, pounds, ounces. The city owes this to Zeus.
EDCS-63000033.summary: This decree records a debt owed to Zeus by the city, specifying amounts in talents, staters, pounds, and ounces for wheat and vetch, and ordering the hieromnamones to record this remainder of the price.

EDCS-63000034.translation: Under Protohenes, son of Kallikrates, hieromnamones, for the treasury, Oumb Theron, Sosikrates, Kra Phaikon, Charmondas, Alch Eupolius, Phaikion, proboloi; Kob Charixenus, Onaion, Dys Zoilos, Sosippos, Pro Kleosthenes, Timasipolios, prodikoi; Gaps Agathocles, Diogenes, Kyl Teledamos, Aischylos, Phawo Menedamos, Lagiskos, the city used, by decree of the council and people, for the construction of the tower, talents.
EDCS-63000034.summary: This inscription details financial expenditures by the city, using funds for tower construction, as recorded by various officials including hieromnamones, proboloi, and prodikoi, under the presidency of Protohenes.

EDCS-63000035.translation: Under Euthymiskos, hieromnamones, for the treasury, Kob Aristippos, Glaukippos, Sowt Sosippos, Simos, Log Philostratos, Phinton, proboloi, presiding, Gaps Kallippos, Poigenes, Ast Euphroniskos, Gorgidas, Agph Thraso, Gnthios, prodikoi; Thra Euphanetos, Menedamos, Tiw Protarchos, Deinarchos, Ank Gorgias, Herakleitos, the hieromnamones used, by decree of the council and people, for the fortification of the city, talents, talents, on condition that we repay to the god as seems good to the council and the people, and whenever it seems good.
EDCS-63000035.summary: This inscription records financial allocations by the hieromnamones, proboloi, and prodikoi for the fortification of the city, with the repayment terms to the god subject to the decision of the council and people.

EDCS-63000036.translation: Under Onaies, proboloi, presiding, Eur Neaithon, Charixenus, Mna Euphrastos, Xenon, Log Aristeidas, Arkesilas, prodikoi; Gaps Euphrastos, Eukleidas, Tel Charidamos, Chairelas, Aga Onaies, Phrasilas, hieromnamones, for the treasury, Psath Philistion, Philiskos, Dys Chairesilas, Platon, Pro Timasipolios, Kleosthenes, the city used, by decree of the council and people, for the cotysian expense, gold of Corinthian standard, for the images, the phylarch in charge of the leaders, month of Apellaios, Oumb Aristodamos, Aristippos, to be repaid when it seems good to the council and the people.
EDCS-63000036.summary: This inscription details a financial transaction for a 'cotysian expense' related to images, with the city using gold of Corinthian standard, overseen by various officials, and repayment conditional on the council and people's decision.

EDCS-63000037.translation: Under Philodamus, the prodykes, Thra, Philodamus, Sottus, Menedamus, Pyrrhus, Philonidas, the probouloi, the proarchontes, Lac., Aristodamus, Mna., Athanipus, Ag., Tharrymachus, the Locrians paid back to Olympian Zeus the money they had borrowed by decree of the council and people. Under Philodamus, talents, staters, pounds, ounces; and from the old debts, talents, talents, pounds, ounces. They paid back in bronze, by weight, talents, pounds, for the bronze doors of Olympian Zeus, for them to make in the temple, for both yokes, each talent of weight, in talents of silver, by decree of the council and people.
EDCS-63000037.summary: This inscription records a financial transaction by the Locrians to Olympian Zeus, involving repayment of borrowed money and funds for bronze doors, under the oversight of various officials.

EDCS-63000038.translation: Under Euphrastus, the hieromnamones, under the treasurer, Ski., Sosippus, Tio., Ameinokritos, Pha., Menedamus, the prodykes, Tun., Zoilus, Sottus, Sosippus, Pyrrhus, Eucarpus, the probouloi, Eur., Xenainetus, Cyl., Phaikylus, Str., Nikodamus, the city borrowed from the god for the construction of towers, by decree of the council and people, from the land, two substructures, talents, staters, pounds; and other talents, total, talents, staters, pounds.
EDCS-63000038.summary: This inscription details a loan taken by the city from a deity for building fortifications, with specific officials overseeing the transaction.

EDCS-63000039.translation: Under Arche demos, the hieromnamones, under the treasurer, Ski., Sophroniskos, Kallidamus, Dys., Zoilus, Sosippus, Pro., Aristokrates, son of Menon, the probouloi, Eur., son of Dorkion, Dorkippus, Tio., son of Samion, Onasimus, Pha., Theon, Theodotus, the prodykes, Psath., Zoilus, Onasimus, Cyl., Euphares, Nikodamus, Alch., Philo nikos, Philonidas, the city borrowed from the god, by decree of the council and people, for the construction of towers, silver, talents, staters, the two substructures.
EDCS-63000039.summary: This inscription records a loan of silver by the city from a god for tower construction, managed by various officials.

EDCS-63000040.translation: Under Timodamus, the hieromnamones, under the treasurer, Eur., Agesidamus, Heria, Cyl., Xenares, Zoilus, Pyr., Archippus, Onaeus, the probouloi, the proarchontes, Lac., Philistion, Sosippus, Sottus, Nikodamus, Timon, Alch., Nikasikrates, Phryniscos, the prodykes, Thra., Glaucia, Sosibius, Mya., Kallippus, Kallikrates, Alch., Phaikion, Eupolius, by decree of the council and the people, borrowed from Zeus for the construction of towers, talents, talents, staters, pounds.
EDCS-63000040.summary: This decree records a loan from Zeus by the city, overseen by numerous officials, for the purpose of building fortifications.

EDCS-63000041.translation: Under Hippon, the probouloi, the proarchontes, Thra., Krates, son of Therōn, Tio., Polystratus, Philonidas, Gag., Thrasyllus, son of Philochares, the prodykes, Omb., Evanthus, son of Eukleiskos, Dys., Emmenidas, son of Aristēs, Pro., Damasippus, son of Timaios, the hieromnamones, under the treasurer, Thra., Eufrastus, son of Eufroniskos, Tēl., Phaiskos, son of Phāōn, Pha., Simylus, son of Menotios, under these, the city borrowed from the king, for the festival/service, Bukatius, talents, staters, pounds, ounces; other, Agrius, talents, staters, pounds, ounces; other, Hippodromius, talents, staters, total, talents, pounds, ounce.
EDCS-63000041.summary: This inscription details the city's borrowing of funds from a king for a festival or service, with various officials named as supervisors and distinct sums allocated for different purposes.

EDCS-63000042.translation: Under Euphrastus, the hieromnamones, under the treasurer, Thra., Thrasōn, Sottus, Onasimus, Pyrrhus, Olympis, we used the funds of the god, by decree of the council and people, for the phatarchia, the probouloi, the proarchontes, Thra., Thrasydamus, Boos, Phaion, Ag., Gnathius, the prodykes, Tun., Timon, Tēl., Theon, Pyrrhus, Philonidas, talents, staters, pounds, ounces; the jars having been sold, talents, staters, pounds.
EDCS-63000042.summary: This decree records the use of temple funds for a 'phatarchia' and the sale of jars, overseen by various officials.

EDCS-63000043.translation: Under Cheiredamos, the hieromnamones, under the treasurer, Lac., Zoilus, Theon, Tēl., Nikias, Thrasymachus, Alk., Xenon, Sosippus, the probouloi, the proarchontes, Anx., Euphon, son of Zoippus, Mna., Onaeus, son of Zoippus, Ank., Antidoros, Krates, the prodykes, Psath., Euphon, Platon, Boos, Damokles, Arkeidas, Pha., Archela, Euthymiskos, they lent, by decree of the council and the people of Zeus, for the construction of towers, talents, talents, staters; another, placed for the loan, for the substructures, talents, staters, pounds, pounds, ounces, ounces; another, from the liquid fruits, the tenth, talents, staters, pounds, ounces; another, from the grain sold daily, the tenth, talents, staters, pounds, ounce; another, the price of pitch, for the jars, of rough pitch, total talents, 250.
EDCS-63000043.summary: This decree records loans made by the city from various sources including grain, fruits, and pitch for tower construction and other purposes, under the authority of council and people.

EDCS-63000044.translation: Under Sosinos, the probouloi, the proarchontes, Lac., Eufrastus, Sosipolios, Cyl., Simias, Simiskos, Gag., Philocrates, Aristarchus, the prodykes, Thra., Thrasōn, Eukleidas, Tēl., Dorkion, Kallinōs, Pro., Samion, Sosikrates, the hieromnamones, under the treasurer, Gaps, Aristomachos, son of Aristēs, Ska., Sosilas, Simia, Pyrrhus, Klēisarchos, son of Aristēdas, under these, the city borrowed from the god, by decree of the council and people, for the construction of towers, for the first measure, talents, talents, staters, pounds; for the second measure, talents, stater, pound; for the third, talents, staters, pounds, ounces; total of those in the phatarchion, talents, stater, pounds, ounces; and for the tenth of the grain, the tenth part, in measures of barley, and the measure of barley for the perimeter feeders, price of the medimnos, stater, pounds; total price, talents, talents, stater, pounds.
EDCS-63000044.summary: This inscription documents a loan from a god by the city for tower construction, with detailed accounting of funds used for different measures and grain tithes.

EDCS-63000045.translation: Under Silanos, the hieromnamones, under the treasurer, Thra., Philokles, Simo, Sottus, Silōnos, Charmondas, Pro., Echedamos, Zoilus, the probouloi, the proarchontes, Psath., Damōn, Sosandros, Tēl., Phaiskos, son of Phāōn, Pha., Menedamus, Lagiskos, the prodykes, Lac., Charixen, Euphiletos, Duo, Philistion, Arkeidas, Pha., Theon, Theodotus, they lent, by decree of the council and people, for the construction of towers of the god, talents, talents, staters, pounds; another decree, talents.
EDCS-63000045.summary: This decree records loans made by the city from a god for tower construction, with two separate decrees mentioned for financial allocations.

EDCS-63000046.translation: Under Euphoratios, the hieromnamones, under the treasurer, Tun., Archippus, Arche dāmos, Sottus, Aristarchus, Aristēs, Pha., Menestratus, Emmenidas, the probouloi, the proarchontes, Psath., Zoilus, Onasimus, Cyl., Euphares, Nikodamus, Ank., Aristokles, Theon, the prodykes, Ski., Sophroniskos, Kallidamus, Duo, Megakles, Euphon, Pha., Onaeus, Charila, the city borrowed from the god, by decree of the council, and for the construction of towers, talents; other, the city borrowed from the god, for the other administration, by decree of the council and people, talents.
EDCS-63000046.summary: This inscription details two separate loans by the city from a god, one for tower construction and another for general administration, overseen by various officials.

EDCS-63000047.translation: Under Kratippos, the hieromnemon, and Tun Ones, Zoilos son of Tios, Protogenes, Kallikrates, and Gag Charidamos son of Kekiniades, the probouleutai, and Ana Euphraineto, Platios, Mna Chariseno son of Euphron, Pro Philiarchos, Herakleitos, the predikoi, and Tun Herakleides, Theonda, Ska Sosila, Simias, Gag Chairelos son of Damophontas, the tax collectors, the city used talents from the god for the construction of a tower, by decree of the council and the people.
EDCS-63000047.summary: A decree of the city council and people records the use of talents from the god for building a tower, listing various officials and their roles during the term of Kratippos as hieromnemon.

EDCS-63000048.translation: Under Onasimos son of Nearchos, the panamos, and Lak Neaithos, Gorgidas, Dys Philonos, Eukleidas, Ank Phintonos son of Sosistratos, the probouleutai, and Omb Charikleos son of Charibbos, Ast Archipou, Aristidas, Pet Chariseno, Chairelos, the predikoi, and Tun Timonos son of Kallikrates, the polemarchs, and Kra Eukleidas son of Silanos, Ank Sosippos son of Aristophanes, the phatarchoi, the amount was repaid to the hieromnamon Skia Aristeias son of Simon, Ast Theodoros son of Pyramos, Alk Timasipolis son of Timasipolis, by decree of the council and people, from the necessary funds owed from previous years to the god, in talents.
EDCS-63000048.summary: A record of repayment of funds to the hieromnamon by decree of the council and people, specifying officials and the amount owed to the god from previous years.

EDCS-63000049.translation: Under Onasimos, the gold was repaid for the shield that was set up in the Olympieion in the council chamber by the repairers Thra Euareos, Phao Dorkippos, Gag Theodoros, in the presence of the probouleutai Proarches Kob Aristokrates, Dys Euthydamos, Agph Echekrates, the predikoi Thra Ariston, Ast Agesandros, Ala Onasimos, the polemarchs Kob Kallippos, Boos Onasimos, Phao Kritolas, Theukolos, Ana Kleomenes. The weight of the gold repaid and placed with the shield was eight minae, with evboic measures for the clippings, one mina with evboic measures. It was repaid to the probouleutai Kob Aristokrates, Dys Euthydamos, Agph Echekrates. This was deposited in the treasury.
EDCS-63000049.summary: A record of the repayment of gold for a shield dedicated in the Olympieion, specifying weights and officials, and its subsequent deposit in the treasury.

EDCS-63000050.translation: Under Euphraineto, the probouleutai: Proarches Gaps Diogenes son of Agathocles, Dys Euthymos son of Philistos, Alk Sokrates son of Philippos; the predikoi: Thra Euphron son of Sauron, Dys Dorkion son of Euphroniskos, Pet Herakleitos son of Euphron; the hieromnamon, for the treasury: Thra Agesidamos son of Ainisidamos, Kra Eudamos son of Timon, Phao Philon son of Gnathios. Under these officials, the city used from the treasury of Zeus, by decree of the council and people, to be repaid as deemed appropriate. Palamnaios, the recipient, received talents. Phatarchos was Philistion son of Lexias, son of Dionysios, received talents. Phatarchos was Sosidamos son of Agreios, received talents. Phatarchos was Aristippos son of Aristoteles, son of Damatrios, received talents, litrai. Phatarchos was Onasimos son of Arkeidas, son of Herakleios, received talents. Phatarchos was Sotirichos son of Euphroniskos, son of Panamou, received talents. Phatarchos was Philostratos son of Onasimos, received talents, litrai.
EDCS-63000050.summary: A decree of the city council and people records the use of funds from the treasury of Zeus for unspecified purposes, listing officials and recipients of talents and litrai.

EDCS-63000051.translation: Under Diognetos, the hieromnamon, Psath Dorimachos, Zoilos, Ast Menalkes, Gorgidas, Str Timon son of Timokles, the probouleutai: Proarchon Gaps Samonos son of Samippos, Tel Kallistratos son of Thrasymachos, Pyr arkeidas son of Sosippos, the predikoi: Lak Xenanetos son of Kleutheres, Kra Proxenos son of Sathyon, Gag Euthymos son of Euthymiskos. The city used from the god, the king, for the festival, from the agyrtmos, silver in talents, staters, litrai, unciae, and from the revenues, through the tamiai and phatarchoi, in talents, staters, of wheat in medimnoi, with the price of the medimnos being staters, total talents. Talents, staters, of barley in medimnoi, with the price of the medimnos being staters, litrai, unciae, total talents, litrai, unciae. Of liquid fruits, talents, staters. Of dry goods, a mixture according to the decree, talents. Of free gifts, for the benefit of the needy, talents. The total owed by the city to the god, under Diognetos, in talents, staters, litrai, unciae.
EDCS-63000051.summary: A decree detailing the city's use of various funds and resources from the god and revenues for a festival and other expenses, including wheat, barley, and liquid fruits, listing numerous officials.

EDCS-63000052.translation: Under Kallippos, the probouleutai: Proarchon Thra Philippos son of Philiarchos, Kra Epigono son of Ariston, Pro Sosippos son of Sosikrates; the predikoi: Lak Euphrastos son of Sosipolis, Ti Kallikrates son of Protogenes, Str Kallippos son of Kallias; the hieromnamon, for the treasury: Anx Euthymos son of Oneos, Dys Euphroniskos son of Sosippos, Pyr Ameinoeles son of Chairexilas. Under these officials, the city used, by decree of the council and people, from the god, for the construction of a tower, Artemitios, in talents, litrai. Palamnaios, in talents, staters, litrai, unciae. Dionysios, in talents, talents, staters, litrai, unciae. Hippodromos, in talents, staters, litrai, unciae. And for the iron, its price, in talents, total talents, staters, litrai, unciae.
EDCS-63000052.summary: A decree records the city's use of funds from the god for building a tower and for various items including iron, listing officials during the term of Kallippos as probouleutes.

EDCS-63000053.translation: Under Gniphos, the probouleutai: Proarchon Tun Lykon son of Lykidas, Ti Euphroniskos son of Lyson, Gag Onasimos son of Sosikrates; the predikoi: Thra Krates son of Therones, Sot Nikodamos son of Timon, Str Timon son of Timokles; the hieromnamon, for the treasury: Ana Koprion son of Euphanos, Tel Orthos son of Silanos, Log Nikippos son of Philistion. Under these officials, the city used from Zeus, by decree of the council and people, silver in talents, litrai, unciae, and for the grain, the tenth part which the king received as its price, one talent. The loan was for the fortification of the city and for weapons.
EDCS-63000053.summary: A decree records the city's use of funds from Zeus for fortifications and weapons, specifying silver and grain prices, and listing officials during the term of Gniphos.

EDCS-63000054.translation: God. Alk, under Phaixion, the hieromnamon, for the treasury: Psath Sosistratos son of Philokrates, Boos Sosippos son of Philykos, Pyr Menippos son of Silon, the probouleutai: Proarchon Thra Euphanous son of Menedamos, Ti Kallikrates son of Protogenes, Alk Xenon son of Sosippos, the predikoi: Eur Dorkion son of Dorkippos, Kra Euthymos son of Aristippos, Log Epainetos son of Simias. We used, by decree of the council and the people, from the god, for the construction of the tower, talents, talents, staters, litrai, as down payments, two. Phaixion, Sosistratos, Sosippos, Menippos.
EDCS-63000054.summary: A decree of the council and people records the use of funds from the god for tower construction, listing officials and down payments, under the hieromnamon Phaixion.

EDCS-63000055.translation: Kul, under Nikodamos, the probouleutai: Proarchon Thra Glaukias son of Sosibios, Ti Neaithos son of Charilas, Ank Philykos son of Zoilos; the predikoi: Kob Sosikrates son of Sosippos, Ska Alkia son of Alkimous, Ank Leonidas son of Apios; the hieromnamon, for the treasury: Lak Sosikrates son of Apheman, Boos Ariston son of Philon, Phao Oneos son of Charilas. Under these officials, the city used from the spoils in talents, staters, litrai, unciae.
EDCS-63000055.summary: A decree of the city council and people records the use of spoils in talents, staters, litrai, and unciae, listing officials during the term of Nikodamos.

EDCS-63000056.translation: Kob, under Euchales, the probouleutai: Proarchon Thra Thraso son of Eukleidas, Mna Euphroniskos son of Amynandros, Gag Alikidas son of Eukleidas; the predikoi: Lak Theon son of Kallippos, Ska Simias son of Leontos, Pyr Euphraios son of Charilas; the hieromnamon, for the treasury: Psath Satyros son of Aristokritos, Mna Sosiilas son of Athanipos, Phao Menedamos son of Lagiskos. Under these officials, the city used from Zeus, for the grain, which was the price, talents, staters, litrai. For other grain that the city used, medimnoi, with the price of the medimnos being staters, total talents, litrai. And for wheat, medimnoi, the price of which was talents, staters, litrai. The total amount of bronze held is talents, staters, litrai.
EDCS-63000056.summary: A decree records the city's use of funds from Zeus for grain, wheat, and bronze, listing officials during the term of Euchales.

EDCS-63000057.translation: Under Sosippos, when Hieromnamones, for the treasury, Psath, Sosandros, Boos, Philonidas, Str., Sosippos, Proboloi, Gaps, Agathocles, Dys, Megacles, Phaos, Archela, Prodikeontes, Thra, Euphrastos, Ast., Thrasones, Pyr., Ameinocles. The city made use, by decree of the council and people, from the god, for the construction of the tower, of the two payments, talents, staters, litrai.
EDCS-63000057.summary: This inscription records the financial transactions of a city, likely for public works like tower construction, specifying amounts of money and officials involved.

EDCS-63000058.translation: Under Philondas, Proboloi, Proarchontes, Ana, Chairedames, Phaikylos, Ti., Simias, Antiochus, Gags, Philocles, Philondas, Prodikeontes, Tun, Theondas, Theodotos, Sk., Philippos, Satyros, Log., Pellius, Epainetos, Hieromnamones, for the treasury, Thra, Glaukia, Sosibios, Ti., Kallias, Kallippos, Ank., Antidoros, Kratos. The city made use, by decree of the council and people, from the god king, for the completion, from the agyrmoi, of Boukaties, talents, litrai, unciae; of Athanas, talents, litrai, unciae; of Diosis, talents, staters; from the tolls, talents, staters; of liquid produce, talents, staters, litrai; of grain, of wheat, talents, staters, litrai; of barley, talents, staters, litrai; of sacred mixtures, talents, as a gift; of interest on the aged, talents, staters; of the price of clay bricks, talents, staters, litrai; of the total amount which the city owes to the god, of Lak., under Philondas, talents, staters, unciae.
EDCS-63000058.summary: This inscription details a city's financial accounts and obligations to a god, including expenditures for various purposes and the collection of taxes and tolls, under a specific set of officials.

EDCS-63000059.translation: Under Ones, Proboloi, Proarchontes, Eur., Neaithos, Charixenus, Mna., Euphrastos, Xenon, Log., Aristides, Arkesilaos, Prodikoi, Gaps, Euphrastos, Eukleidas, Tel., Charidamus, Charila, Agphs., Ones, Phrasilas, Hieromnamones, for the treasury, Psath, Philistion, Philiskos, Dys., Chairesilas, Platon, Pro., Timasipolios, Kleosthenes. The city made use, by decree of the council and people, from the god, for the completion, from the payments, of Artamatios, talents, litrai; of Palamnais, talents, staters, litrai; of Agreios, talents, staters; of Hippodromios, talents, staters, litrai, unciae; of supplementary payments, talents, staters, litrai, unciae; of sacred dues, talents, litrai; of sacred mixtures, according to the decree, talents, as a gift; of interest on the aged, talents, and from the tolls, talents, staters, litrai; and of the grain, of wheat, measured in medimnoi, the price per medimnos of all the wheat, talents, staters, litrai; of barley, measured in medimnoi, the price per medimnos of all the barley, staters, talents, litrai, unciae; of liquid produce, talents, staters, litrai, unciae; of the total amount, talents.
EDCS-63000059.summary: This inscription itemizes a city's expenditures and financial dealings with a god, including payments for various purposes and materials, under a specific list of officials.

EDCS-63000060.translation: Under Epainetos, it seemed good to the council and the people that the Hieromnamones, who are in charge of the treasury, should deposit in the treasury, after inscribing in bronze, the debt that the city incurred from the god. Hieromnamones in charge of the treasury who made the use: Gaps, Samon, Samippos, Dys., Apiadas, Aristides, Alch., Ariston, Mnasones. Proboloi, Proarchontes: Psath, Gnathis, Phrynion, Ti., Kallippos, Kallias, Pro., Nikias, Pyrrhon. Prodikoi: Kob., Agies, Charixenus, Tel., Amanitos, Philomeles, Alch., Menon, Euphrainetos. Logistes: Thra., Phrasilas, Philistion, Ti., Filiarchos, Philodamos, Phaos, Euphrastos, Charmidas.
EDCS-63000060.summary: This decree instructs the treasurers (Hieromnamones) to inscribe the city's debt to a god in bronze, listing the officials responsible for the treasury and other administrative roles.

EDCS-63000061.translation: Under Euthymidas, Proboloi, Proarchontes: Kyl., Agelochos, Alexandamos, Gags, Samion, Hieros, Prodikoi: Ski., Sosinos, Zoippos, Tel., Thrasymachos, Nikias, Timaios. Hieromnamones in charge of the treasury: Ski., Eu., Ast., Archelas, Kleandros, Pyr., Xenochairs, Phalacros. Under these officials, the city made use from the treasury of gold, talents, of the following amount: It repaid under the same officials a bronze bowl, engraved, amounting to thirty talents. The remainder of the debt, talents, talents.
EDCS-63000061.summary: This inscription records a city's expenditure of gold from the treasury under specific officials and notes the repayment of a bronze bowl, detailing the remaining debt.

EDCS-63000062.translation: Under Herakles, in charge of the treasury, Aristodamos, Ast., Kallippos, Ank., os. Prodikoi: Omb., Teleokles, Boos, Phaos, los. Proboloi, Proarchontes: aios, Sot., Simos, Ank., Sosikrates. By decree of the council and people, for the Fatarches of the twelve, for the month Dionysion, to Philonidas, talents. Also, for the Fatarches of the twelve, for the month Agrion, to Silos, talents. Also, for the Prostatai, for the month Panamon, for the Fatarches of the twelve, to Archippos, talents. The total amount which the city incurred, under Herakles, talents.
EDCS-63000062.summary: This inscription details funds allocated by the city council and people to specific officials (Fatarches, Prostatai) for particular months, under the supervision of treasury officials, likely as payments or expenses.

EDCS-63000063.translation: Under [---], Proboloi, Proarchontes: [---], Agisidamos, Ska, [---]aios, Oneos, Chairedamos. Prodikoi: WS, Kyl., Agelochos, Alexidamos, Agphs., Gnathis, Thrasones. Hieromnamones in charge of the treasury: Ski., Zoippos, Aristonumos, Mna., Kossuros, Phaikiones, Alch., [---]os, Philonda. Under these officials, the city made use of double Corinthian gold and twenty-five litrai, talents, talents, staters, litrai, litrai; of Zeus, talents, staters, litrai, unciae; and of kotian, talents, staters, litrai, unciae.
EDCS-63000063.summary: This inscription records the city's use of gold and other funds from the treasury under a specific set of officials, likely for expenditures or payments.

EDCS-63000064.translation: Under Charila, Hieromnamones in charge of the treasury: Kob., Charixenus, Oneos, Tel., Glaukippos, Euthymos, Pro., Anthionos, Anthippos. Proboloi, Proarchontes: Kob., Eucholas, Aristeus, Kra, Sathyones, Phaikylos, Pyr., Ameinokles, Chairesilas. Prodikoi: Gaps, Aristomachos, Aristeus, Kra, Epigonos, Ariston, Pro., Pheidiadides, Deinomenes. We made use from the god of the three payments for the construction of the tower and the fortification of the city, by decree of the council and people, talents, litrai. We will repay this when it seems good to the council and the people.
EDCS-63000064.summary: This inscription records a city's decision, made by decree of the council and people, to use funds from a 'god' for fortifications and to repay the amount later.

EDCS-63000065.translation: Under Sosikrates, Proboloi, Proarchontes: Lak., Formion, Menos, Mna., Philon, Charip., Pyr., Peithias, Onasimos. Prodikoi: Psath., Euthymos, Zoilou, Dys., Eutymos, Philistos, Gags, Sosikrates, Klenias. Hieromnamones in charge of the treasury: Kob., Damainetos, Protogenes, Ti., Kallikrates, Protogenes, Agphs., Deinarchos, Kalippos. Under these officials, the city made use from the god for the construction of the tower, by decree of the council and people: three years, talents, staters, litrai; of Apellaios, satiros, of Boukation, month, talents, staters, litrai, unciae; of Athanas, talents, staters, litrai; of Dionysios, Damatrios, talents, staters, litrai, unciae. Total amount, talents, staters.
EDCS-63000065.summary: This inscription documents a city's financial expenditure for building a tower, authorized by the council and people, and lists the officials and specific funds used, including payments for certain months.

EDCS-63000086.translation: Sacred offerings of Aphrodite. Philon dedicated.
EDCS-63000086.summary: This is a dedication inscription, stating that Philon dedicated sacred offerings to the goddess Aphrodite.

EDCS-63000100.summary: This inscription records a dedication to the goddess Persephone by Xenodoca.

EDCS-63000101.summary: This inscription records a dedication to an unnamed goddess by Phrasiadas.

EDCS-63000102.summary: This inscription records a dedication to an unnamed goddess by Timareos.

EDCS-63000103.summary: This inscription records a joint dedication by Kaparos and Proxenos.

EDCS-63000113.translation: Aeneas dedicated [this] to Jupiter the Savior.
EDCS-63000113.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Jupiter the Savior by Aeneas.

EDCS-63000114.translation: And to Hermes, and to Gaia, and I dedicate to you, Philton, the devoted sister, and Nouila Taisina, and Nouia Pakyla, Leukoin son of Taisinos, devoted brother.
EDCS-63000114.summary: This is a complex dedication to multiple deities (Hermes, Gaia) and individuals, likely from the Roman period given the names.

EDCS-63000115.translation: Thestias Kallikrates Gnathis, the other dedicator, and if anyone else dedicates to us.
EDCS-63000115.summary: This inscription seems to record a dedication by Thestias Kallikrates Gnathis and potentially others who might add dedications.

EDCS-63000120.translation: God, according to Proxenos, Kratippos: two talents. Standard of a new [coinage?].
EDCS-63000120.summary: This inscription appears to record a financial transaction or donation, possibly related to a new currency or standard, mentioning Proxenos and Kratippos.

EDCS-63000129.summary: This inscription identifies Stephanos as the bishop of Nikos, likely a late Roman or early Byzantine period ecclesiastical inscription.

EDCS-64800038.summary: This inscription records a dedication by Aristeis.

EDCS-64800039.translation: Cleombrotus, son of Dexilaos, dedicated to the Olympians as an offering, having won, a tenth part of both length and thickness, having made a vow.
EDCS-64800039.summary: This is a dedication by Cleombrotus to the Olympians, likely commemorating an athletic victory and a vow, dated to the Hellenistic period.

EDCS-64800057.translation: Apollodoros Xyllas dedicates. Volchas brought. Apollodoros of Onatas, Nixes dedicates. Hybrichos Parmynios dedicates.
EDCS-64800057.summary: This inscription lists several individuals dedicating something, possibly related to trade or local offices, likely from the Hellenistic period.

EDCS-64800063.translation: Phau llos sat by Zeus of Melichios.
EDCS-64800063.summary: This inscription records Phau llos sitting by Zeus of Melichios, possibly indicating a cultic or commemorative marker from the Hellenistic period.

EDCS-64800064.summary: This is a simple name inscription, likely identifying an individual, possibly from the Hellenistic period.

EDCS-64800065.summary: This inscription consists of a title or descriptor 'Ak anthropos' followed by the name Theognios, its exact meaning and purpose are unclear but likely from the Hellenistic period.

EDCS-64800066.translation: Pe, Onatas the damiurgos, has the house of Simes in charge of all things, both alive and dead, xenoi, two, Philip, son of Xan, Dorkeus.
EDCS-64800066.summary: This inscription appears to be a legal or administrative document concerning property or duties assigned to Onatas the damiurgos, possibly dating to the Hellenistic period.

EDCS-64800067.translation: The god Tyche, during the damiurgos Kalliphaon, gives all things, both alive and dead, to Philōn and his wife Zao tycha.
EDCS-64800067.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the god Tyche by Philōn and his wife Zao tycha, mentioning the damiurgos Kalliphaon, likely from the Hellenistic period.

EDCS-64900695.summary: This is a dedication by Xenodoka to the goddess Persephone, likely from the Hellenistic period.

EDCS-64900697.summary: This is a dedication by Phrasiadas to an unnamed goddess, likely from the Hellenistic period.

EDCS-64900701.summary: This is a joint dedication by Kaparos and Proxenos, likely from the Hellenistic period.

EDCS-64900800.summary: This is a Greek inscription identifying a person by name and filiation.

EDCS-64900802.translation: Calon of the Valeioi made me for his family, Glaukios son of Lykkides, for you, Hermes of Rhegion.
EDCS-64900802.summary: This is a Greek inscription dedicating a statue or monument to the god Hermes, made by Glaukios for his family.

EDCS-67700148.translation: Publius Paquius Priamus and Quintus Annius Pomponianus, the board of four officials.
EDCS-67700148.summary: This Latin inscription records the names of two officials (duumviri or similar) from a Roman colony, likely of the late Republican or early Imperial period.

EDCS-70700107.summary: This is a Latin funerary inscription dedicating a grave or monument to Tita.

EDCS-70700109.summary: This is a Greek inscription, likely a dedication or funerary marker, from Phileros to Tita.

EDCS-70900877.summary: This is a Greek inscription providing a person's name and his father's name.

EDCS-75100003.translation: Ephoros Sopholis dedicated these things to Damas, himself and herself.
EDCS-75100003.summary: This Greek inscription records a dedication by Ephoros Sopholis to Damas, possibly a deity or a person, for himself and his wife.

EDCS-76000109.translation: Philemena, daughter of Nikonas, and her family and her descendants, a vow to Damas.
EDCS-76000109.summary: This Greek inscription is a votive offering to Damas made by Philemena, her family, and descendants.

EDCS-76000113.translation: To Istieos son of Aristos, for Artemis Soteira (the Saviour).
EDCS-76000113.summary: This Greek inscription is a dedication to the goddess Artemis Soteira, possibly made by Istieos.

EDCS-76000115.summary: This is a dedication to the goddess Damas by Sodamos.

EDCS-76000116.summary: This is a dedication to the goddess Damas by Sopyriscus.

EDCS-76000117.translation: Ephoros Hagylos entrusts Petallis, herself to her Damas.
EDCS-76000117.summary: This is a dedication or entrustment involving Ephoros Hagylos and Petallis to the goddess Damas.

EDCS-76000118.translation: Ephoros Archias, in the month of Hes...
EDCS-76000118.summary: This inscription seems to record a date or event involving Ephoros Archias during an unspecified month.

EDCS-76200205.translation: To our Lord Flavius Claudius Julianus, Ever Augustus.
EDCS-76200205.summary: This is a dedication to the Roman Emperor Julian, likely from the 4th century CE.

EDCS-76400042.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription with partially legible names and letters, possibly a dedication or epitaph.

EDCS-76600083.translation: Under Lucius Hor[...] and Nouius Ele[...]
EDCS-76600083.summary: This inscription appears to record officials or magistrates, possibly in a public context, during an unspecified period.

EDCS-76800066.translation: [...]us Titus Graius Marcus Fabricius Marcus Nonius
EDCS-76800066.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription listing several Roman names, possibly part of a longer text like a list of donors or a family inscription.

EDCS-78500012.summary: This is likely a funerary dedication from Pancarpus to Livia, possibly his wife or daughter.

EDCS-79600086.translation: Pactumeia, daughter of Publius, called Gemina, to Lucius.
EDCS-79600086.summary: This is a funerary inscription, likely from a daughter to her father, identifying her by her full name and cognomen.

EDCS-79600087.translation: To Homer, freedman of Marcus Servilius.
EDCS-79600087.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Homer, the freedman of Marcus Servilius, likely dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-79600090.translation: Vibiedia, daughter of Publius, citizen of Rome.
EDCS-79600090.summary: This inscription likely records the name and parentage of Vibiedia, a Roman citizen, possibly from an epitaph or a dedication, dated to the Imperial period.

EDCS-79600091.summary: This is a short dedication, possibly for a public work or religious offering, by a man named Eutactus, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-79600096.summary: This inscription appears to be a simple name inscription, possibly for Publius Metellius, found on a building or monument and likely dating to the Roman Republic or early Imperial period.

EDCS-06600083.summary: A Greek inscription containing a name and a possible place name or descriptor, likely from a Roman province, date uncertain.

EDCS-11400328.summary: A simple inscription identifying Annia as a freedwoman of Lucius, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-11400589.translation: To the Divine Shades. Turnina, righteous, Seramis, Speritsynetia, sweetest freedwoman, and for himself.
EDCS-11400589.summary: A funerary inscription dedicated to Turnina and her freedwoman by Seramis and Speritsynetia, also likely for themselves, probably from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-23300015.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Labianus Stotthus.

EDCS-23300058.translation: Of Caius Pomponius Felicianus, son of Apringius, from Thugga.
EDCS-23300058.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Caius Pomponius Felicianus, son of Apringius, from Thugga.

EDCS-23400009.translation: Of Publius Vettenus, son of Vettius.
EDCS-23400009.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Publius Vettenus, son of Vettius.

EDCS-39100052.translation: I come from the pure, pure ones of the earth, the queen, Eukles, son of Eubouleus, and other immortal gods. For I too wish to be a blessed offspring of yours, but fate subdued me, and lightning struck from the stars, and I escaped from the circle of bitter grief and trouble, and stepped with swift feet onto the sacred wreaths. And I entered under the bosom of the queen of the earth. Blessed and fortunate one, you will be a god instead of a mortal. A kid fell into the milk.
EDCS-39100052.summary: This is a funerary epigram, likely from the Imperial period, lamenting the fate of the deceased and hoping for divine status in the afterlife.

EDCS-39500605.translation: Of Onasus, son of Nikon, son of Nikon, son of Onasus.
EDCS-39500605.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording a patronymic lineage.

EDCS-39501263.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Mauros, son of Mizotrus.

EDCS-40000368.summary: This is a dedication to the god Heracles by Reginos, likely from the Hellenistic or Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-44800363.summary: This is a dedication, likely to a deity named Pius, possibly related to the emperor Antoninus Pius, with a repetition of the name.

EDCS-63000133.summary: This is a funerary epitaph or a simple greeting to Agathocles.

EDCS-64800059.translation: Father, may Eufaines approve, son of Klesarchos, grandson of Apollodoros, great-grandson of Theoprochidas.
EDCS-64800059.summary: This is a funerary inscription listing the ancestry of Klesarchos' son, invoking a father figure for approval.

EDCS-64800070.translation: I belong to Apollo Lykeios, son of Theagenes of Pyrrhos.
EDCS-64800070.summary: This inscription is a dedication to Apollo Lykeios by Theagenes of Pyrrhos.

EDCS-64800091.translation: I am the sacred object of Lakonos.
EDCS-64800091.summary: This inscription likely refers to a sacred object dedicated by someone named Lakonos.

EDCS-64800096.summary: This inscription simply names Achilles and Patroklos, possibly as a dedication or memorial.

EDCS-64800099.summary: This inscription records a dedication made by Automedas.

EDCS-64900791.summary: This inscription names Polydeukes and Phoebus, possibly in a votive context.

EDCS-64900796.summary: This inscription appears to be a dedication or ownership marker related to Herakles and Reginius.

EDCS-64900797.translation: To Zeus Reginius, son of Geleas.
EDCS-64900797.summary: This is a dedication to Zeus Reginius by Geleas.

EDCS-67700149.translation: Lucius, son of Lucius, for Laetitia. Lucius...oppi Caedici.
EDCS-67700149.summary: This fragmented inscription appears to be a funerary dedication for Laetitia, mentioning Lucius and possibly another name.

EDCS-81700344.translation: I come from the pure, pure earthly realms, sovereigns Eukle and Eubouleus, and you other gods and daemons. For I too pray that your lineage be blessed. And I have paid a penalty for deeds not just. Whether fate subdued me or lightning with thunderbolt, now as a suppliant I come to pure Persephone, so that she may readily send me to the holy seats.
EDCS-81700344.summary: This inscription is a supplication to chthonic deities and Persephone by a woman who seeks release after paying a penalty for unjust deeds, possibly related to a funerary context.

EDCS-81700345.translation: I come from the pure, pure earthly realms, sovereigns Eukle and Eubouleus, and you other gods and daemons. For I too pray that your lineage be blessed. And I have paid a penalty for deeds not just. Whether fate subdued me or lightning with thunderbolt, now as a suppliant I come to pure Persephone, so that she may readily send me to the holy seats.
EDCS-81700345.summary: This inscription is a supplication to chthonic deities and Persephone by a man who seeks release after paying a penalty for unjust deeds, possibly related to a funerary context.
